body.text: 134. bhagavān samyaksaṃbuddho yad arthaṃ samudāgato tadartham abhisambhāvayitvā | peyālaṃ | yāvat tehi tehi vihārehi viharan kauśāmbyām viharati ghoṣitārāme | āyuṣmān dāni chandako pañcānām āpattikāyānām anyatarānyatarām āpattim adhyomardati | so bhikṣūhi vuccati āyuṣman chandaka paśyasi etām āpattiṃ | so dān āha | nāhaṃ paśyāmi yūyam api naṃ paśyatha | bhe cyu[?]taṃ paśyantu | kim puna mama etāya duṣṭāya | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣū bhagavato ārocayeṃsu | bhagavān āha | yady eṣo bhikṣavaś chandako pañcānām āpattikāyānām anyatarānyatarām āpattim adhyomardati | sa tām āpattiṃ na paśyati | tena saṃgho āpattīya adarśanena utkṣepanīyaṃ karma karotu | tasya saṃghena utkṣepaṇīyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ | na saṃbhuñjati dharmasaṃbhogena āmiṣasaṃbhogena | tasya dāni mātā aparaṃhi bhikṣuṇīvihāre āvāsinī | so dāni taṃhi gatvā āha | sālohite saṃghenāham utkṣipto | na saṃbhuñjati me dharmasambhogena āmiṣasaṃbhogena | sā dān āha | aparyā ārya cchandaka | ahan te saṃbhuñjāmi dharmasambhogena āmiṣasambhogena | sā dāni sambhuñjati dharmasaṃbhogena āmiṣasaṃbhogena | sā dāni bhikṣuṇīhi vuccati | ārye eṣo hi ārya chandako samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinyato utkṣipto apratikṛto | mā ārye etaṃ bhikṣuṃ anuvartehi |
body.translated_text: 134. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, the perfectly awakened one, having accomplished the purpose for which he came forth—abbreviation—dwelling in various monasteries, he was residing at <s>Kauśāmbī</s> in <s>Ghoṣita's</s> park. Now the venerable <s>Chandaka</s> was suppressing one or another offense from among the five categories of offenses. The <s>bhikṣus</s> said to him: 'Venerable <s>Chandaka</s>, do you acknowledge this offense?' He said: 'I do not acknowledge it; do you see it? Let all see it! What is this wicked [offense] to me?' The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If, <s>bhikṣus</s>, this <s>Chandaka</s> suppresses one or another offense from among the five categories of offenses and does not acknowledge that offense, then the <s>saṃgha</s> should perform the act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense.' The <s>saṃgha</s> performed the act of suspension on him. No one would share with him in matters of <s>Dharma</s> or material things. Now his mother was a resident in the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> monastery. He went there and said: 'Blood-relative, I have been suspended by the <s>saṃgha</s>. No one shares with me in matters of <s>Dharma</s> or material things.' She said: 'Do not be afraid, noble <s>Chandaka</s>. I will share with you in matters of <s>Dharma</s> and material things.' She then shared with him. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> told her: 'Noble one, this venerable <s>Chandaka</s> has been suspended by the united <s>saṃgha</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Vinaya</s>, and has not been restored. Noble one, do not follow this <s>bhikṣu</s>.'

body.text: bhagavān āha | apāpāya āryamiśrikā ahaṃ ca tāvan netaṃ bhikṣuṃ anuvartiṣyaṃ | kā anyā anuvartiṣyati | anuvartiṣyāmy aham etaṃ bhikṣuṃ | kim artham aham etaṃ kim artham aham etam nānuvartiṣye | etat prakaraṇaṃ tāyo bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | mahāprajāpatī gautamī bhagavata ārocayati | bhagavān āha | yady eṣā bhikṣuṇī chandakamātā chandakaṃ bhikṣuṃ samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣiptam apratikṛtam anuvartati | tena hi taṃ gacchatha triḥkkhatto kuvege triḥkkhatto mahājane trikkhatto saṃghamadhye samanugrāhatha etasya vastusya pratiniḥsargāya | sā dāni kuvege vuccati satyaṃ tvam ārye chandakamāte āryechandakaṃ samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣiptam apratikṛtam anuvartasi | āho ty āha | sā tvaṃ kuvege vucyasi | mā ārye chandakamāto āryachandakaṃ samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣiptam apratikṛtaṃ anuvartāhi | yaṃ khalu te ārye chandakamāte mitrāya karaṇīyaṃ arthakāmāya hitaiṣiṇīya karoti te taṃ mitrā ekā vācā gacchanti | dve vāce avaśiṣṭe pratiniḥsara na pratiniḥsarāmītya āha | evam dvir api trir api | evaṃ mahājane saṃghamadhye avalokanā kartavyā yāvan na pratiniḥsarāmīty āha |
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said [to her]: 'Do not be afraid, noble ones. I myself will not follow this <s>bhikṣu</s>, who else would follow him? I will follow this <s>bhikṣu</s>! Why should I not follow him? Why should I not follow him?' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī [Gautamī]</s>. <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> reported it to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said [summoned her and admonished her].

body.text: 135. etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ tāyo bhikṣuṇīyo bhagavataḥ ārocayeṃsuḥ | anuprāptā bhagavan āryā chandakamātā trikkhatto kuvege trikkhatto mahājane trikkhatto saṃghamadhye etasya vastusya pratiniḥsargāya na ca pratiniḥsarati | bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha chandakamātāṃ | sā dāni śabdāpitā | bhagavān āha | satyaṃ tvaṃ chandakamāte | evan nāma tvaṃ chandakaṃ bhikṣuṃ samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣiptam apratikṛtaṃ saṃbhuñjasi | sā tvaṃ trikkhutto kuvege trikkhutto mahājane trikkhutto saṃghamadhye anuprāptā etasya vastusya pratiniḥsargāya na ca pratiniḥsarasi | ām bhagavan | bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtan te chandakamāte | nanv ahaṃ chandakamāte anekaparyāyeṇa daurvacanasyaṃ garhāmi daurvacanasya avarṇavādi tatra nāma tvaṃ kharākhakkhaṭaṃ vāmā apradakṣinagrāhiṇī | naiṣaś chandakamāte dharmo | naiṣa vinayo naitaṃ śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ | naivaṃ kartavyaṃ naivaṃ karaṇīyaṃ | naivaṃ karontīye vṛddhir bhavati kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu | evaṃ ca dāni tvaṃ jānantī bhikṣuṃ samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣiptam anuvartasi | tena hi na kṣamati jānantī bhikṣuṃ samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣiptam apratikṛtam anuvartituṃ |
body.translated_text: 135. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Lord, the noble <s>Chandakamātā</s> (Chandaka's mother) has been admonished three times in a small assembly, three times in a large assembly, and three times in the midst of the <s>saṃgha</s> to renounce this matter, but she does not renounce it.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon <s>Chandakamātā</s>.' She was summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is it true [that you continue to support a suspended monk despite being admonished]?'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm āmantrayati | sannipātaya gautami bhikṣuṇīyo yāvatikā bhikṣuṇīyo kauśāmbinagarīm upaniśrāya viharanti | yāvac chikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ |
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>: 'Assemble the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>Gautamī</s>—all the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> dwelling in the vicinity of the city of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>.' And so the training rule was established:

body.text: 136. yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | jānantīti svayam vā jāneya parato vā śruṇeya ākāravantena darśanena ākāravantena śravaṇena | samagreṇa saṃgheneti avyagreṇa | dharmavinayato āpattīya adarśanena āpattīya apratikarmeṇa trayāṇāṃ dṛṣṭigatānām apratiniḥsargeṇa | utkṣiptan ti asaṃbhogam kṛtaṃ |
body.translated_text: 136. 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>'—means one who is fully ordained. 'Knowingly'—means she knows either by herself or hears from others, through indicative signs or indicative testimony. 'By the united <s>sa��gha</s>'—means by the undivided [<s>saṃgha</s>]. 'In accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>'—for not acknowledging an offense, for not making amends for an offense, for not renouncing one of three wrong views. 'Suspended'—means made incommunicable.

body.text: apratikṛtaṃ ti apratyosāritaṃ | anuvarteyā ti āmiṣasaṃbhogena vā dharmasaṃbhogena vā saṃbhuñjeya |
body.translated_text: 'Not restored'—means not readmitted. 'Follows'—means shares in matters of <s>Dharma</s> or shares in material things.

body.text: sā bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṇīhi evam asya vacanīyā | eṣo hi ārye bhikṣuḥ samagreṇa saṃghena | peyālaṃ | yāvat tad eva vastuṃ pratigṛhṇeya na pratiniḥsareya yaṃ taṃ utkṣiptakaṃ bhikṣum anuvartati |
body.translated_text: That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> is to be told by the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>: 'Noble one, this <s>bhikṣu</s> has been [suspended] by the united <s>saṃgha</s>—abbreviation—up to: should she accept that very matter and not renounce it, [she is one who] follows a suspended <s>bhikṣu</s>.'

body.text: sā bhikṣuṇīti yathā chandakamātā | bhikṣuṇīhīti saṃghena mahājanena ekapudgalena yāvat tṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhitavyā samanubhāṣitavyā iti trikkhatto kuvege mahājane trikkhatto saṃghamadhye | sā kuvege vaktavyā | satyaṃ tvaṃ itthaṃnāme itthaṃnāme bhikṣusamagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣiptam apratikṛtam anuvartasi | āmo ty āha | sā dāni vaktavyā | mā ārye itthaṃnāma bhikṣuṃ samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣiptam anuvartāhi | yaṃ khalu te itthannāme mitrāya karaṇīyaṃ arthakāmāya hitaiṣinīya karoti | te taṃ mitrā ekā vācā avaśiṣṭā pratiniḥsara na pratiniḥsarāmīty āha dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyam api | peyālaṃ | saṃghamadhye pi traivācikaṃ yāvat taṃ vastuṃ pratiniḥsareya ity etaṃ kuśalaṃ | no ca pratiniḥsareya iyam pi bhikṣuṇī pārājikā bhavaty asamvāsyā |
body.translated_text: 'That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>'—refers to one like <s>Chandakamātā</s>. 'By the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>'—means by the <s>saṃgha</s>, a large group, or a single individual; she is to be admonished up to a third time—three times in a small assembly, in a large assembly, and three times in the midst of the <s>saṃgha</s>. In the small assembly, she should be told: 'Is it true, so-and-so, that you follow so-and-so the <s>bhikṣu</s>, [who was] suspended by the united <s>saṃgha</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, and not restored?'

body.text: pārājiketi pārājikāye āpattīye saṃkāśanā prakāśanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkarmatā prajñaptiḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Pārājika</s>'—means the elucidation, clarification, revelation, analysis, explanation, and formal designation of the <s>pārājika</s> offense.

body.text: 137. sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī trikkhatto kuvege samanugrāhiyamāṇā samanubhāṣiyamāṇā pratiniḥsargārhaṃ vastuṃ na pratiniḥsarati vācāyāṃ vinayātikramam āsādayati | trikkhatto mahājane samanugrāhiyaṃāṇā vā samanubhāṣiyamāṇā vā pratiniḥsargārhaṃ vastuṃ na pratinissarati vācāyām vācāyām vinayātikramam āsādayati | saṃghamadhye jñaptim adhivāsayati vinayātikramam āsādayati | prathamāyām vācāyām adhyoropitāyāṃ vinayātikramam āsādayati | vyoropitāyāṃ thūl'-accayam āsādayati | dvitīyāyāṃ vācāyām adhyoropitāyāṃ vinayātikramam āsādayati | vyoropitāyāṃ vācāyāṃ thūl@' accayam āsādayati | tṛtīyāyāṃ vācāyām adhyoropitāyāṃ thūl'-accayam āsādayati | vyoropitāyāṃ pārājikā bhavati | yadā pārājikām āpattim āpannā bhavati | ye ca kuvege mahājane ye ca saṃghamadhye vinayātikramāś ca thūl'-atyayāś ca sarve te pratipraśraṃbhyante ekā āpattir gurukā santhihati | yad iyaṃ pārājikā | antarā pratiniḥsarati pañcāsthitāsu āpattiṣu kārāpayitavyā | kin ti dāni pratiniḥsargārhaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ | kim apratiniḥsargārham abhūṣisi itthannāmaṃ bhikṣuṃ utkṣiptakam anuvartiṣyan ti | nānuvārtitaṃ anuvartāmi anuvartiṣyāmi ceti evaṃ pratiniḥsargārhaṃ |
body.translated_text: 137. If that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, when being admonished and spoken to three times in a small assembly, does not renounce the matter worthy of renunciation, she incurs a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression with each statement. When being admonished and spoken to three times in a large assembly, she does not renounce the matter worthy of renunciation, she incurs a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression with each statement.

body.text: kin ti dāni apratiniḥsargārhaṃ abhūṣisi | itthannāmaṃ bhikṣum utkṣiptakam anuvartiṣyan ti | anuvartitaṃ dāni nānuvartāmi anuvartiṣyāmi ceti evam apratiniḥsargārhaṃ ceti evam apratiniḥsārgarhaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: What then is a matter not worthy of renunciation? [If she says:] 'I will follow the <s>bhikṣu</s> so-and-so who is suspended'—whether she says 'I have followed,' 'I do not follow,' or 'I will follow'—all these are to be seen as matters not worthy of renunciation. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī jānantī bhikṣuṃ samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣiptam apratikṛtam anuvarteya sā bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṇīhi evam asya vacanīya | eṣo hi ārye bhikṣuḥ samagreṇa saṃghena dharmato vinayato utkṣipto apratikṛto | mā etaṃ bhikṣum anuvarteya | evaṃ ca sā bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṇībhir ucyamānā taṃ vastuṃ pratigṛhṇeya | na pratiniḥsareya sā bhikṣunī bhikṣuṇīhi yāvat tṛtīyakam samanugrāhitavyā samanubhāṣitavyā tasya vastusya pratiniḥsargāya | yāvat tṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhiyamāṇā vā samanubhāṣiyamāṇā vā taṃ vastuṃ pratiniḥsareya ity etaṃ kuśalaṃ | no ca pratiniḥsareya iyam pi bhikṣuṇī pārājikā bhavaty asamvāsyā |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, knowingly, follows a <s>bhikṣu</s> suspended by the united <s>saṃgha</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, who has not been restored—that <s>bhikṣu��ī</s> is to be told by the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>: 'Noble one, this <s>bhikṣu</s> has been suspended by the united <s>saṃgha</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, and has not been restored. Do not follow this <s>bhikṣu</s>.' If that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, when thus spoken to by the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, persists in that [matter and does not renounce it, she is defeated (<s>pārājikā</s>) and is expelled].

body.text: uddānaṃ

children.translated_text: Sexual intercourse, taking what is not given, killing,
false speech, improper association, and the eight-matter [rule],
concealing a transgression,
and following a suspended [monk].

body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

body.text: prapūryate vargaḥ | pārājikāḥ samāptāḥ |
body.translated_text: The section is complete. The <s>pārājikās</s> (defeat rules) are concluded.

body.text: saṃcaritra
body.translated_text: Matchmaking (<s>saṃcaritra</s>)

body.text: 138. saṃcaritrakarma yathā bhikṣūṇāṃ sarvam anvarthaṃ yāvat tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 138. The matchmaking procedure is as for <s>bhikṣus</s>; everything applies correspondingly. Up to: therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī saṃcaritraṃ samāpadyeya strīmatam vā puruṣasyopasaṃhareya puruṣasya vā mataṃ striyāyopasaṃhareya jāyattatena vā jārattatena vā antamasato tatkṣaṇīkāni pi ayaṃ dharmo prathamāpattiko saṃghātiśeṣo [(vā?)] upādiśeṣo saṃgho saṃgham evādhipati kṛtya niḥsaraṇīyo |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> engages in matchmaking—conveying a woman's [wish] to a man or a man's [wish] to a woman, whether for marriage or concubinage, or even for a momentary [union]—this offense is of the first category, a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> (formal meeting offense), requiring the <s>saṃgha</s> as authority, to be resolved by the <s>saṃgha</s>.

body.text: saṃghātiśeṣadharma 2
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśe��a</s> rule 2

body.text:
amulakaḥ
dve abhūte tathaiva kartavyā yathā bhikṣūṇāṃ | yāvat tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: Groundless [accusation]: The two [rules regarding] false [accusations] should be treated just as for <s>bhikṣus</s>. Up to: therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī duṣṭād doṣāt kupitā anāttamanā śuddhāṃ bhikṣuṇīm anāpattikāṃ amūlakena pārājikena dharmeṇānudhvaṃsaye apy eva nām' enāṃ brahmacaryāto cyāveyan ti sā tad apareṇa samayena samanugrāhiyamāṇā vā asamanubhāṣiyamānā vā amūlakam etam adhikaraṇam bhavati bhikṣuṇī ca doṣe pratiṣṭhihati doṣā avacāmīti ayam pi varge prathamāpattiko saṃghātiśeṣo yāvat |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, out of malice, anger, and displeasure, falsely accuses a pure <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who has committed no offense with a groundless <s>pārājika</s> charge, [thinking:] 'Perhaps I may thus cause her to fall from the holy life'—if she, at a later time, whether being admonished or not, [admits that] this charge is groundless and the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> stands convicted of malice, the malicious [accuser incurs a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>].

body.text: leśamātrakaṃ
body.translated_text: With a slight [basis]

body.text:
tena bhagavān āha |
yā puna bhikṣuṇī duṣṭā doṣāt kupitā anāttamanā anyabhāgiyasya cādhikaraṇasya kiñci deśaṃ leśamātrakaṃ dharmaṃ upādāya aparājikāṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ pārājikena dharmeṇānudhvaṃsaye apy eva nāmaināṃ brahmacaryā cyāveyan ti sā tad apareṇa samayena samanugrāhiyamāṇā vāsamanubhāṣiyamānā vā anyabhāgīyam eva tam adhikaraṇaṃ bhavati anyabhāgīyasya cādhikaraṇasya kiñci deśa leśamātrako dharmo upādinno bhavati bhikṣuṇī ca doṣe pratiṣṭhihati doṣā avacāmīti saṃghātiśeṣo |
body.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, being malicious, out of ill-will, angry, and displeased, taking some point or the slightest pretext from a matter belonging to another category, should falsely accuse a non-defeated <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> with a <s>pārājika</s> offense, [thinking:] 'Perhaps I may cause her to fall from the holy life' — and if at a later time, when she is being questioned or making a statement, that matter turns out to belong to another category, and the point taken was merely the slightest pretext from a matter of another category, and the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> stands firm in her ill-will [saying:] 'I speak out of ill-will' — it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> (formal meeting) offense.

body.text: saṃghātiśeṣadharma 4
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> Rule 4

body.text: ussayavādā
body.translated_text: Quarrelsome Behavior (<s>ussayavādā</s>)

body.text: 139. bhagavāñ chrāvastīyaṃ viharati | taṃhi dāni bhikṣuṇīvihāro ca tīrthikaśayyā ca | kanthāntarikā | sā kanthā patitā | taṃhi dāni bhikṣuṇīvihāre | sthūlanandā nāma bhikṣuṇī āvāsikinī | sā dān āha | tīrthikā karothaitāṃ kanthāṃ | yūyaṃ āhrīkaanapatrāpiṇo hrīrapatrāpya nipannāḥ | āryamiśrikāḥ hrīrapatrāpya sampannāḥ kāle ca vikāle ca marmāṃ praviśantāṃ niṣkrāmantāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaviṣyati cittasyopakleśo | te dān āhaṃsuḥ | ayaṃ varṣārātro yadā varṣā nirgatā bhaviṣyanti tadā kariṣyāmaḥ | sā dān āha | idānīm eva karotha | te na kurvanti | sā dāni ākrośati bhraṣṭāyūḥ naṣṭāyūḥ bhagnāśā surābhraṣṭā yānagardabhā na kariṣyatha | katham nagnāḥ | āhrīkaanopatrāpiṇo hrīrapatrāpya vipannā mithyādṛṣṭikā vinipātitāḥ | karothaitāṃ kanthāṃ | te dān āhaṃsuḥ itikitikāya dhīte vaḍaḍiṅgarapuṣṭe śramaṇike yadi marasi na karoma etāṃ kanthāṃ |
body.translated_text: 139. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Now there was a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> monastery and a <s>tīrthika</s> (non-Buddhist ascetic) lodging with a wall in between. That wall had fallen down. In that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> monastery, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Sthūlanandā</s> was a resident. She said: '<s>Tīrthikas</s>, rebuild this wall! You are shameless and immodest, devoid of moral shame and conscience. The noble ladies, possessed of moral shame and conscience, seeing [you] entering and leaving their quarters at proper and improper times, will have their minds disturbed.' They said: 'This is the rainy season. When the rains are over, we will do it.' She said: 'Do it now!' They did not do it. She then abused them: 'May your life-force be destroyed! May your life be ruined! Your hopes are shattered, you drunkards, you asses of vehicles! You will not do it? How [is it that you go about] naked? You are shameless and immodest, devoid of moral shame, holders of wrong views, destined for ruin! Build this wall!' They then said: 'You daughter of a female servant, you who were fed on rice cakes, you little female renunciant — even if you die, we will not build this wall!'

body.text: 140. tāya dāni gatvā āsane niveditaṃ | etad eva sarvam ārocayitvāha dīrghāyu yathā sā kanthā kriyate tathā karotha | āsanikā śrāddhā prasannā | te dān āhaṃsuḥ śabdāpayatha miśrasthān | te dāni śabdāpitāḥ | te āsanikā āhaṃsuḥ | he itikitikāya putrāḥ tīrthinagnāḥ surābhraṣṭā yānagardabhāḥ mithyādṛṣṭīka vinipātitāḥ | gacchatha tāṃ kanthāṃ karotha | yūyam ahrīkā anotrāpiṇo āryamiśrikā hrīrapatrāpya sampannāḥ | teṣāṃ yuṣmākaṃ kāle ca vikāle ca niṣkrāmantāṃ praviśantāṃ dṛṣṭvā āryamiśrikāṇāṃ brahmacāriṇīnāṃ bhaviṣyati cittasyānyathātvaṃ tehi dāni āsanikehi niyuktāḥ akāmakā kāryante | te divasato kanthām utthāpayanti | rātrau ca varṣeṇa pātīyati | teṣāṃ dāni tremāsaṃ karma kurvantānāṃ gataṃ | te dān āhaṃsuḥ | imāya itikitikāya dhītare vaḍaḍiṅgarapuṣṭāya śramaṇikāya mṛttikākarma kariyāmaḥ | upāsakakulehi avadhyāyanti paśyatha gṛhapatayo yuṣmākaṃ dakṣiṇīya śramaṇikāya asti me calan ti kṛtvā tremāsaṃ akāmakā karma kārāpitā | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ upāsakā kulopikānāṃ bhikṣuṇīnām ārocayanti | bhikṣuṇīyo pi mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayanti | mahāprajāpatī gautamī bhagavato ārocayati | bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha nandāṃ | sā dāni śabdāpitā | satyan nande ti | peyālaṃ | yāvat paryavadātāni bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: 140. She then went and reported to the [lay] donors. Having reported all of this, she said: 'Honorable sirs, please see to it that the wall is rebuilt.' The donors were faithful and devoted. They said: 'Summon those mixed [ascetics].' They were summoned. The donors said: 'You sons of female servants, you naked <s>tīrthikas</s>, you drunkards, you asses of vehicles, holders of wrong views, destined for ruin! Go and build that wall! You are shameless and immodest, while the noble ladies are endowed with moral shame and conscience...'

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī utsayavādā vihareyā āgārikaparivrājakehi divasam vā muhūrtam vā antamasato ārāmikaśramaṇ'uddeśehi sārdham ayam pi dharmo prathamāpattiko |
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should dwell in a quarrelsome manner with householders or wandering ascetics for a day or even a moment, or at the very least with monastery attendants or novices — this too is an offense at the first commission.

body.text: yā punar bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | utsayavādā vihareyā ti kalahaṃ kareya | āgarikehīti gṛhikehi | parivrājikehīti gautamajaṭilakaparyantehi | divasaṃ ti suryākaṃ divasaṃ | muhūrtaṃ ti tatkṣaṇaṃ tanmuhūrtaṃ | antamasato ārāmikehīti saṃghopasthāyakehi | śramaṇ'uddeśakehīti pañcadaśavarṣān upādāya yata saptatikāḥ | sārdham vihareya | ayam pi dharma prathamāpattiko saṃghātiśeṣo |
body.translated_text: 'If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Should dwell in a quarrelsome manner' means she should quarrel. 'With householders' means with laypeople. 'With wandering ascetics' means with those up to and including <s>Gautama</s> ascetics and matted-hair ascetics. 'A day' means a day with sunlight. 'A moment' means that instant, that very moment. 'At the very least, with monastery attendants' means with those who serve the <s>Saṃgha</s>. 'With novices' means those from fifteen years up to seventy years old. 'Should dwell with [them]' — this too is a first-offense <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: saṃgho tā nāma vuccanti aṣṭa pārājikā dharmāḥ | teṣām iyam āpattiḥ sāvaśeṣā sapratikarmā | saṃghātiśeṣan ti saṃghātiśeṣāye āpattīye saṃkāṣanā prakāśanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkarmatā prajñaptiḥ |
body.translated_text: The '<s>Saṃgha</s>' is the name given to the eight <s>pārājika</s> offenses. The offense regarding them still has a remainder, still has a remedy. '<s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s>' is the designation for the clarification, disclosure, opening up, analysis, and making plain of a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> offense.

body.text: sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī rājākule vā āsane vā nivedayati thūl'-accayaṃ | ākārṣāpayati saṃghātiśeṣaḥ | upāsakakule vā śrāddhakule vā nivedayati vinayātikramaḥ | ujjhāpayati samvaragāmivi | bhikṣur api rājakule nivedayati vinayātikramam āsādayati | ojjhāpayati samvaragāmivi | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: If this <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> reports [the dispute] to the royal court or to the donors, it is a <s>sthūlātyaya</s> (grave offense). If she has them dragged [before authorities], it is a <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>. If she reports to a lay follower's family or a faithful family, it is a <s>vinayātikrama</s> (disciplinary transgression). If she reproaches [others about it], it is like a <s>saṃvaragāmi</s> (restraint-related offense). If a <s>bhikṣu</s> also reports to the royal court, he incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s>. If he reproaches [others], it is like a <s>saṃvaragāmi</s>. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī utsayavādā vihareya āgārikaparivrājakehi divasam vā muhūrtam vā antamasato ārāmikaśramaṇ'uddeśehi sārdham āpattiḥ dharmo prathamāpattiko ||
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should dwell in a quarrelsome manner with householders or wandering ascetics for a day or even a moment, or at the very least with monastery attendants or novices together — this is an offense at the first commission.

body.text:
saṃghātiśeṣadharma 5
grāmāntaraṃ
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> Rule 5: Traveling to Another Village (<s>grāmāntara</s>)

body.text: 141. bhagavāṃ cchrāvastīyam viharati | taṃhi dāni rāṣṭrā nāma bhikṣuṇī | tasyā eva rāṣṭrapālā nāma bhaginī kugrāmake vūḍhā | sā tāvad anajjikā | sā preṣayati | ārye rāṣṭre āgaccha yadi mām icchasi jīvantīṃ paśyituṃ | sā tahiṃ gatā | sā ca kālagatā | so dāni bhaginīpatiko paridevati | ārye rāṣṭre yan te bhaginī kālagatā kā tāvad imaṃ dārakaṃ parihariṣyati kā tāvad imaṃ mama gṛhaṃ pratijāgariṣyati | āryāya rāṣṭrāya vayaṃ pratijāgṛtavyāḥ | tāye dāni bhavati pāpakāḥ khalu vātā vāyantīti | sā niṣkramitvā srāvastīm āgatā | sā bhikṣuṇīnām āha | āryamiśrikāyo manāsmi brahmacaryāto cyāvitā | āhaṃsuḥ | kim vā katham vā | etad eva vistareṇārocayati | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayanti | mahāprajāpatī pi gautamī bhagavata ārocayati | bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha rāṣṭrāṃ | sā dāni śabdāpitā | tad eva sarvaṃ vistareṇa pṛcchīyate | yāvad ām bhagavan | bhagavān āha | evaṃ ca nāma tvaṃ bhikṣuṇīya vinā adhvānamārgaṃ pratipadyasi | tena hi na kṣamati yāvac chikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ |
body.translated_text: 141. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Now there was a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Rāṣṭrā</s>. Her sister named <s>Rāṣṭrapālā</s> was married [and living] in a remote village. She [the sister] had no other noble lady [to help her]. She sent [a message]: 'Noble <s>Rāṣṭrā</s>, come if you wish to see me alive.' She [the nun] went there. But [the sister] had passed away. The sister's husband lamented: 'Noble <s>Rāṣṭrā</s>, since your sister has died, who now will care for this child? Who will look after this household of mine?'

body.text: 142. eṣā evārthotpattiḥ | bhikṣuṇīyo adhvānamārgaṃ gacchanti | aparā dāni bhikṣunī prāsādikā darśanīyā taruṇī ucchvāsakārī vā praśvāsakāri vā mārgāto utkramitvā upaviṣṭā | puruṣasārtho ca āgacchati | sā tehi parivāritā | te dān āhaṃsuḥ | āryā prāsādikā darśanīyā taruṇī pratyagrayauvane vartasi | kāmāḥ | paribhoktavyāḥ | sā tvaṃ kiṃ pravrajitā | ko vā te nirveda iti | āha | pravrajitāsmi |
body.translated_text: 142. This is the same origin story [told differently]. <s>Bhikṣuṇīs</s> were traveling on a road journey. Now one <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who was attractive, beautiful, and young, either panting or gasping for breath, stepped off the road and sat down. A caravan of men came along. She was surrounded by them. They said: 'Noble lady, you are attractive, beautiful, and young, in the prime of your youth. Pleasures are to be enjoyed! Why have you gone forth? What was your disillusionment?' She said: 'I have gone forth [into the religious life].'

body.text: āhaṃsuḥ | ācakṣva tāvat yāvat te tad anantaraṃ parivāriya dhārenti | tāvat tāyo bhikṣuṇīyo grāmāntaraṅ gatāḥ | tāye dāni kaukṛtyam utpannaṃ | sā mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayati | mahāprajāpatī gautamī bhagavata ārocayati | bhagavān āha | tena hi āpattiḥ akāmikāyeti |
body.translated_text: They said: 'Tell us then' — and kept surrounding and detaining her for so long that those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> had already gone on to the next village. She then felt remorse. She reported to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> reported to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'In that case, there is no offense for one [who was detained] against her will.'

body.text: 143. eṣaivārthotpattiḥ | bhikṣuṇīyo adhvānamārgaṃ gacchanti | aparā dāni bhikṣuṇī glānā | sā vinā bhikṣuṇīhi grāmāntaram utkrānta | tāye dāni kaukṛtyaṃ kṛtaṃ kaukṛtyena mahāprajāpatīye ārocayati | mahāprajāpatī gautamī bhagavata ārocayati | bhagavān āha | anāpattiḥ glānāyeti | atha khalu bhagavān mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm āmantrayati | sannipātaya gautamīti | peyālaṃ |
body.translated_text: 143. This is the same origin story [told differently]. <s>Bhikṣuṇīs</s> were traveling on a road journey. Now one <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> was ill. She, without the other <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, went on to the next village. She then felt remorse. Out of remorse, she reported to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> reported to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'There is no offense for one who is ill.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>: 'Convene [the assembly], <s>Gautamī</s>.' [The account is abbreviated.]

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṇīya vinā adhvānamārgaṃ pratipadyeya antamasato grāmāntaram pi anyatrasamaye tatrāyaṃ samayo akāmikā bhikṣuṇī bhavati glānikā vā | ayam atra samayo | ayam pi dharmo prathamāpattiko |
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should set out on a road journey without [another] <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, even to the next village — except in a [permissible] circumstance. The permissible circumstance here is: the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> was [detained] against her will, or she was ill. This is the permissible circumstance here. This too is an offense at the first commission.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti | peyālaṃ | bhikṣuṇīya vineti advitīyā | adhvānamārga triyojanaṃ dviyojanam triyojanam | antamasato grāmāntaram vā | akāmikā ti hasti kaḍevareṇa aśvakaḍevareṇa gokaḍevareṇa vā manuṣyakaḍevareṇa vā āvṛtā bhavati | glāniketi jarādurbalā vā vyādhidurbalā vā bhavati | pratyuddhṛtaṃ bhagavatā padaṃ anāpattī glānāya | ayam atra samayo | etā dāni bhikṣuṇīyo adhvānamārgaṅ gacchanti yāvatā antosīmāṅ gacchanti kiñcāpi dūraṃ dūraṃ gacchanti anāpattiḥ | atha dāni grāmāntaram vā nagarāntaram vā gacchanti kāntāramārgam vā atikrāmanti | anto hastapāśasthitāhi atikrāmitavyaṃ | paraṃ hastapāśaṃ gacchanti | antamasato caturaṅgulam pi deśanāgāmivinayātikramam āsādayati | adhyardham vā dvihastam vā gacchanti thūl'-accayam āsādayati | atha dāni ekā bhikṣunī āgatvā sīmāntare tiṣṭhati thūl'-accayam āsādayati | aparā āgatvā atikrāmati imaṃ sīmāntaran ti evaṃ yattikā atikrāmanti sarvāsāṃ thūl'-accayaṃ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>': [as before, abbreviated.] 'Without a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means without a companion. 'Road journey' means three <s>yojanas</s>, two <s>yojanas</s>, three <s>yojanas</s>. 'At the very least, to another village.' 'Against her will' means she is obstructed by an elephant carcass, a horse carcass, a cow carcass, or a human carcass. 'Ill' means weak from old age or weak from disease. The <s>Bhagavān</s> has exempted the case of illness — no offense for the ill. This is the permissible circumstance here. Now, when these <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> travel on a road journey, up to...

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṇīya vinā adhvānamārgaṃ pratipadyeya antamasato grāmāntaram pi anyatrasamaye | tatrāyaṃ samayo akāmikā bhikṣuṇī bhavati | glānikā vā | ayam atra samayo | ayam pi dharmo prathamāpattiko |
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should set out on a road journey without [another] <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, even to the next village — except in a [permissible] circumstance. The permissible circumstance here is: the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> was [detained] against her will, or she was ill. This is the permissible circumstance here. This too is an offense at the first commission.

body.text: grāmāntaraṃ ekarātraṃ pi
body.translated_text: [Traveling to] another village, even for a single night.

body.text: 144. bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati | tatra dāni karmakāraputraḥ śraddhāprasannaḥ | tasya bhāryā śuklā nāma karmāradhītā prāsādikā darśanīyā | atha bhagavān kālasyaiva nivāsayitvā pātracīvaram ādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣtaḥ | sāvadānam piṇḍāya caranto tasya gṛhaṃ gato uddeśe sthitaḥ | so dāni bhuñjati | sā pariviśantī āvṛtya sthitā | mā bhagavantam dṛṣṭvā viprakṛta utthāsyatīti | tasya dāni bhavati kin tāvad iyam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati | bhagavatā pi vaineyavaśena prabhā te utsṛṣṭā | tena cāvalokitaṃ | tena bhagavān dṛṣṭo | so dān āha | aye hi asti nāma tvaṃ mama bhagavantam āvārayasi | anarthakāmā tvaṃ | mama na tvam arthakāmā | sā dān āha nāham āryaputrasya anarthakāmā | bhagavantam ārādhayāmi | api tu mā viprakṛto bhagavantam dṛṣṭvā utthāsyasīti | tāye dāni bhavati dhig astu mama gṛhāvāsasya | yatra hi nāma priyaṃ kariṣyāmīti | apriyam uktā | sā dān āha āryaputra gacchāmy ahaṃ | parvrajāmi | so dān āha | kasmin pravacane | āha | bauddhe | āha | pravrajāhīti |
body.translated_text: 144. The <s>Bhagavān</s> dwelt in <s>Rājagṛha</s>. There a blacksmith's son was devoted in faith. His wife was named <s>Śuklā</s>, a blacksmith's daughter, graceful and beautiful. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having dressed early in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. Walking carefully for alms, he went to that man's house and stood at the appointed place. The man was eating. His wife, serving [food], stood blocking [the view], thinking: 'Lest he see the <s>Bhagavān</s> and, disturbed, rise up.' He then thought: 'Why does she stand blocking?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> too, by the power of those to be trained, released his radiance. [The man] looked around and saw the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He said: 'Ah! You are actually blocking my view of the <s>Bhagavān</s>! You wish me harm, not good!' She said: 'I do not wish you harm, noble husband. I honor the <s>Bhagavān</s>. But [I feared] lest you, disturbed, would rise upon seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' She then thought: 'Shame on my household life! Where one intends to do something pleasing, one is spoken to unpleasantly.' She said: 'Noble husband, I am going. I shall go forth.' He said: 'In which teaching?' She said: 'In the Buddhist [teaching].' He said: 'Then go forth.'

body.text: 145. sā dāni utpalavarṇāya pravrajitā upasampāditā | tāya dāni aṣṭāhena pravrajitāya yuñjantīya vyaṭayantīya vyāsayantīya tisro vidyāḥ ṣaḍabhijñāḥ | balavaśībhāvaḥ sākṣīkṛto | sā dāni balavaśībhāvaprāptā | anyataraṃ vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśrayopaniṣaṇṇā | tāye dāni śakro 'marasaṃghaparivṛtto pādavando āgato | āha |
body.translated_text: 145. She was ordained under <s>Utpalavarṇā</s> and received full ordination. Within eight days of going forth, striving, exerting, and applying herself, [she attained] the three knowledges (<s>tisro vidyāḥ</s>) and the six superknowledges (<s>ṣaḍabhijñāḥ</s>). The mastery of powers was realized by her. Having attained the mastery of powers, she was seated at the foot of a certain tree. Then <s>Śakra</s>, surrounded by the assembly of immortals, came to pay homage at her feet. [The verse] says:

children.translated_text: Behold this one established in the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Śuklā</s>, the blacksmith's daughter,
Today, eight days since going forth, she has accomplished her task, free from defilements. [1]
Well-trained by <s>Utpalavarṇā</s>, she enters the noble path,
Possessing the three knowledges and supernatural powers, skilled in reading the minds of others. [2]

children.text: maharddhikā bhikṣuṇī tā vijitā indriyāṇī ca |
children.translated_text: That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> of great supernatural power, with senses conquered,
Sits at the foot of a tree in imperturbable <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). [3]
<s>Śakra</s> <s>Vāsava</s>, with the host of immortals, having approached her,
Pays homage with joined palms to <s>Śuklā</s>, the blacksmith's daughter. [4]

body.text: sā madhurabhāṣiṇī gṛheṇa gṛhaṃ nīyate | apareṇa dāni upāsakena mahārheṇa paṭena chāditā | antarīkṣād devatā vācaṃ niścārayanti |
body.translated_text: She, the sweet-spoken one, is taken from house to house [for alms]. Another lay devotee then covered her with a valuable cloth. From the sky, deities uttered these words:

children.text: lakṣmīvān ayam upāsako puṇyam prabhūtam analpakaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'Fortunate is this lay devotee; his merit is abundant and not small,
Who has given a robe to <s>Śuklā</s>, from whom all fetters have been abandoned.' [5]
'Why do the people of <s>Rājagṛha</s> stand about as if intoxicated with honey,

children.text: ye śuklān na paryupāsanti daivasikān dharmān uttamā || [6] ||
children.translated_text: Who do not attend upon <s>Śuklā</s> and [her] supreme daily <s>Dharma</s> [teachings]?' [6]

children.text: taṃ āsecanakaṃ śāntaṃ te vai aprativāṇīyaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'That refreshing, peaceful, indeed irresistible one—
Her form is recognizable by the wise, but unrecognizable by fools.' [7]

body.text: sā dāni gṛheṇa gṛhaṃ bhāṣaṇāya nīyati | tāye dāni lābhasatkāraśloko 'bhyudgataḥ | tāye dāni bhikṣuṇīyo irṣyāpattiḥ | lābhasatkāram asahamānā tā dān āhaṃsuḥ | bhañjanaṃ etāya kṛtaṃ | tato 'syāḥ sarvo janakāyo śrotavyaṃ śraddhātavyam manyati | tāyo dāni bhagavato allīnā | etāya bhagavan jambhanaṃ sādhitaṃ | bhagavān āha | satyaṃ śukle evaṃ nāma tvayā jambhanaṃ sādhitaṃ | tena te jano śrotavyaṃ manyati | āha | ahaṃ bhagavān jambhanaṃ na jānāmi | kuto jambhanaṃ sādhayi ṣyāmi | bhagavān āha | na etāya jambhanaṃ sādhitaṃ | api tu asyāḥ praṇidhānaṃ idaṃ |
body.translated_text: She was taken from house to house for teaching. Her gains, honors, and fame had risen. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> became envious of her. Unable to bear her gains and honors, they said:

body.text: 146. bhūtapūrvam atīte 'dhvānaṃ nagare vārāṇasīyaṃ bhagavati kāśyape tatra dāni rājā kṛkī nāmābhūt | tasya sapta dhītaro abhūṣi |
body.translated_text: 146. 'In the past, long ago, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, during the dispensation of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, there was a king named <s>Kṛki</s>. He had seven daughters:'

children.translated_text: <s>Śramaṇā</s> [1], <s>Śramaṇimitrā</s> [2],
<s>Bhikṣuṇī</s> [3], <s>Bhikṣuṇīdāsikā</s> [4],
<s>Dharmā</s> [5] and <s>Sudharmā</s> [6],
And <s>Saṃghadāsī</s> as the seventh [7]. [1]

children.text: caturdaśīm pañcadaśīṃ yā ca pakṣasya aṣṭamī |
children.translated_text: On the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and the eighth of the half-month,
And during the special observance half-month, well-composed in the eightfold [precepts], [2]

body.text: poṣadham upoṣadhan ti sadā śilena saṃvṛtā ||
body.translated_text: They observed the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day), always restrained by virtue.

body.text: kāśināñ ca manāpo āsi bhadrako nāma mānavo || [3] ||
body.translated_text: And there was one beloved of the <s>Kāśi</s> people, a young man named <s>Bhadraka</s>. [3]

children.translated_text: Skilled in dance and song, in playing stringed instruments and dance,
For play and delight, the people gathered there. [4]

children.text: taṃ ca kālagataṃ jñātvā sarvās tāḥ sapta kumāriyo |
children.translated_text: And when they learned of his death, all those seven princesses,
Graceful and beautiful, the king's daughters, assembled. [5]

body.text: rājānam upasaṃkramya idaṃ vacanam abravīt || [6] ||
body.translated_text: Having approached the king, they spoke these words: [6]

children.translated_text: 'We take our leave, father, O increaser of the <s>Kāśi</s> realm;

children.text: anujānātu mo deva śmaśānaṃ yāmaṃ prekṣitum || [7] ||
children.translated_text: May the lord permit us—we wish to go and view the cremation ground.' [7]

children.text: adya pañcadaśī deva divyā nakṣatra mālinī |
children.translated_text: 'Today is the fifteenth, O lord, adorned with divine constellations;

children.text: anujānātu mo nātha śmaśānaṃ yāmaṃ paśyituṃ || [8] ||
children.translated_text: May the master permit us—we wish to go and see the cremation ground.' [8]
'In that frightful, terrifying place, foul-smelling and hair-raising,
A place of lamentation for humans—what will you do in the cremation ground?' [9]
'Where the lifeless, food for others, unconscious,
Cast aside, the dead lie in the extremely terrifying cremation ground.' [10]

children.text: yatra gṛdhrā śṛgālāś ca kākolūkās tathā vṛkāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Where vultures and jackals, crows, owls, and wolves
Devour the limbs—in the extremely terrifying cremation ground.' [11]

children.text: yatra gṛdhrā śṛgālāś ca kākolūkās tathā vṛkāḥ> |
children.translated_text: 'Where vultures and jackals, crows, owls, and wolves

children.text: astrān ādāya gacchanti śmaśāne kiṃ kariṣyatha || [12] ||
children.translated_text: Go bearing weapons—what will you do in the cremation ground?' [12]
'Where bones are seen, scattered in every direction,
Standing conch-white—what will you do in the cremation ground?' [13]
'Impaled upon stakes, impure, reeking of phlegm,

children.text: keśānām ākare raudre śmaśāne kiṃ kariṣyatha || [14] ||
children.translated_text: In that terrible repository of hair—what will you do in the cremation ground?' [14]
'Strewn with rogues and wanderers, frequented by thieves and serpents,
An abode of evil humans—in the extremely terrifying cremation ground.' [15]

body.text:
amanuṣyāna āvāse rākṣasānān niveśane |
sarvapretāna āvāse | śmaśāne bahubhīṣaṇe || [16] ||
body.translated_text: 'An abode of non-humans, a dwelling of <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), an abode of all ghosts—in the extremely terrifying cremation ground.' [16]

children.translated_text: 'Those delicately adorned ones, wearing jeweled bracelets,
Seizing each other's arms, they wail—in the extremely terrifying cremation ground.' [17]
'Those delicately adorned ones, wearing jeweled bracelets,
With hair disheveled, they wail—in the fearful, dreadful cremation ground.' [18]

children.text: yatra mātā pitā bhrātā bhaginī jñātibāndhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Where mother, father, brother, sister, relatives, and kinsmen,
Heavy-hearted, turn away—in the fearful, terrible cremation ground.' [19]
'Where mother, father, brother, sister, relatives, and kinsmen
Depart without taking leave—in the extremely terrible cremation ground.' [20]
'With the sound of "Alas! Alas!" from the waters, with the lamentation of relatives,
With terrible putrid stench—in the extremely terrible cremation ground.' [21]
'Where fans and palm-leaf fans are scattered in every direction,
In that terrible place confused with the smoke of funeral pyres—what will you do in the cremation ground?' [22]

body.text: ayaṃ prāsādavaro kūṭāgāro sunirmito | [22a]
body.translated_text: 'Here is this excellent mansion, a peaked pavilion, well-built, [22a]

children.text: yatra annañ ca pānañ ca ratīyo ca upasthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where food and drink and pleasures are at hand—

children.text: atra ramatha kanyāyo śmaśāne kiṃ kariṣyatha || [23] ||
children.translated_text: Enjoy yourselves here, O princesses! What will you do in the cremation ground?' [23]
'[Behold] this delightful lotus pond, adorned with <s>cakravāka</s> birds,
Well-covered with white lotuses, water-lilies, and fragrant night-lotuses. [24]
Filled with flocks of various birds, resounding with various calls—

children.text: atra ramatha kanyāyo śmaśāne kiṃ kariṣyatha || [25] ||
children.translated_text: Enjoy yourselves here, O princesses! What will you do in the cremation ground?' [25]

body.text: kumāryo āhaṃsuḥ |
body.translated_text: 148. The princesses said:

body.text: vayaṃ pi tāta jānāmo śmaśāne bhayabhairave

children.text: durgandhaṃ kuṇapaṃ caiva kovidāraṃ ca puṣpitaṃ || [1] ||
children.translated_text: Its foul smell, its corpses, and also the blossoming <s>kovidāra</s> tree. [1]

body.translated_text: 'We too know, father, the fearful, dreadful cremation ground,

children.text: vayam api tātaṃ jahiṣyāmo tato 'py asmāṃ jahiṣyati |
children.translated_text: We too shall abandon our father, and he too shall abandon us;

children.text: nānābhāvo vinā bhāvo na cireṇa bhaviṣyati || [2] ||
children.translated_text: The state of being otherwise, the state of being apart—before long it shall come to be. [2]'
The king said:
'O princesses with the perception of suffering, [......]
With an untroubled mind, enter the <s>atimuktaka</s> [cremation ground].' [3]

children.text: anujñātā kṛkiṇā rājñā niryātāḥ kāśīnāṃ purāt |
children.translated_text: Permitted by King <s>Kṛki</s>, they departed from the city of the <s>Kāśis</s>;

children.text: sarvās tāḥ ratham āruhya gatāḥ śmaśānaprekṣikāḥ || [4] ||
children.translated_text: All of them, mounting chariots, went to view the cremation ground. [4]
They saw on the road a corpse, cast aside, abandoned,
Foul-smelling, impure, undressed, and discolored. [5]

children.text: tāyo yānād avataritvāna sarvāḥ sapta kumāriyo
children.translated_text: Then, descending from the chariots, all seven princesses
Gathered around it on all sides and spoke these words:

children.text: sarvāsāṃ vo ayan dharmaḥ sarvīṣā eṣa dharmatā |
children.translated_text: 'This is the <s>dharma</s> (nature) of you all; this is the natural law of all;

children.text: eṣa asya śarīrasya sarvā gāthāṃ karomahe || [6] ||
children.translated_text: This is [the fate] of this body—let us all compose a verse.' [6]
'This one, formerly with body anointed with sandalwood, wearing white garments, attended by servants,

children.text: chāyaṃ kulañ ca avekṣamāno so khajjate śivapathikāya madhye || [7] ||
children.translated_text: Regarding his beauty and family with pride—he is now devoured in the middle of the path of jackals.' [7]
'A city of a skeleton of bones, plastered with flesh and blood,

children.text: yatra rāgasya doṣasya mohasyāpi samūha yaḥ || [8] ||
children.translated_text: Where passion, hatred, and delusion are heaped together. [8]

body.text: imam nagaram utsṛjya nāgarīśo kahiṃ gataḥ || [9] ||
body.translated_text: Having abandoned this city, where has the lord of the city gone?' [9]

children.text: yo dvicakraṃ dviarañ ca imaṃ parihared rathaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'Whoever would drive this chariot with two wheels and two axles—

children.text: imaṃ rathaṃ samutsṛjya śārathī so kahiṃ gataḥ || [10] ||
children.translated_text: Having abandoned this chariot, where has the charioteer gone?' [10]

children.text: ūrdhvaśākham adho mūlaṃ ya imaṃ parihare dhvajaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'Whoever would carry this banner with branches above and root below—

children.text: imaṃ dhvajaṃ samutsṛjya dhavajahāro so kahiṃ gataḥ || [11] ||
children.translated_text: Having abandoned this banner, where has the banner-bearer gone?' [11]

children.text: ya imaṃ pariharet kāyaṃ aśvaṃ bhadram ca vāṇijo |
children.translated_text: 'Whoever would drive this body like a fine horse, a merchant—

children.text: imaṃ kāyaṃ samutsṛjya vāṇijo so kahiṃ gataḥ || [12] ||
children.translated_text: Having abandoned this body, where has the merchant gone?' [12]

children.text: ya imāṃ pariharen nāvaṃ asmimāne mahārṇave |
children.translated_text: 'Whoever would steer this boat on this great ocean—

children.text: imān nāvaṃ samutsṛjya nāviko so kahiṃ gataḥ || [13] ||
children.translated_text: Having abandoned this boat, where has the boatman gone?' [13]

children.text: yo 'yam asmin āgāre vāsaṃ kalpeya adhvagaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Whoever, a traveler, would make his abode in this dwelling—

children.text: imam āgāraṃ samutsṛjya adhvago so kahiṃ gataḥ || [14] ||
children.translated_text: Having abandoned this dwelling, where has the traveler gone?' [14]

children.text: mama gāthā subhaṇitā mama gāthā subhaṇitā |
children.translated_text: 'My verse is well-spoken! My verse is well-spoken!'
Thus they exclaimed to one another at the <s>Atimuktaka</s> cremation ground. [15]

children.text: tataś ca maghavān chakro devarājaḥ śacīpatiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maghavān</s> <s>Śakra</s>, king of the gods, lord of <s>Śacī</s>,

children.text: samvegajātās tāḥ kanyāḥ dṛṣṭvā tā upasaṃkramet || [16] ||
children.translated_text: Seeing those princesses born of spiritual urgency, approached them. [16]

children.text: sarvāsāṃ vo subhāṣitaṃ sarvāsāṃ vo subhaṇitaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'Well-spoken by all of you! Well-composed by all of you!

children.text: varaṃ varetha kanyāyo yat kiñcin manasepsitaṃ || [17] ||
children.translated_text: Choose a boon, O princesses—whatever your heart desires.' [17]

children.text: ko nu divyena varṇena antarīkṣasmi tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: 'Who is it that stands in the sky with divine radiance?

children.text: ko vā tvaṃ kasya vā putraḥ kathaṃ jānāma te vayaṃ || [18] ||
children.translated_text: Who are you, whose son are you? How shall we know you?' [18]
'I am <s>Śakra</s>, the thousand-eyed, <s>Maghavān</s>, the bull among gods,
Whom the hosts of gods worship when gathered in <s>Sudharmā</s> [hall]. [19]
I am <s>Śakra</s>, the thousand-eyed, king of the gods, lord of <s>Śacī</s>;

children.text: varaṃ varetha kanyāyo yat kiñcin manasepsitaṃ || [20] ||
children.translated_text: Choose a boon, O princesses—whatever your heart desires. [20]

children.text: śakraś ca vo varaṃ dadyāt trayastriṃśeśvaraḥ prabhūḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the Thirty-three, the mighty, would grant you a boon;

children.text: varaṃ varetha kanyāyo kṣipraṃ vyāharato mama || [21] ||
children.translated_text: Choose a boon, O princesses—speak quickly to me!' [21]

body.text: 148. kumāryo āhaṃsuḥ |
body.translated_text: 148. The princesses said:

children.text: yasya mūle chavir nāsti patran nāsti kuto latā |
children.translated_text: 'One at whose root there is no bark, no leaf—whence then a creeper?

children.text: yo dhīro bandhanān muktaḥ tan me śakra varaṃ dada || [1] ||
children.translated_text: That wise one freed from bonds—grant me that boon, O <s>Śakra</s>! [1]
A <s>bhikṣu</s> wearing dust-colored robes, lean, invited by the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: dhyāyantaṃ vṛkṣamūlasmi tan me śakra varaṃ dada || [2] ||
children.translated_text: Meditating at the foot of a tree—grant me that boon, O <s>Śakra</s>! [2]

children.text: yasya rāgaś ca doṣaś ca avidyā ca pradālitā |
children.translated_text: One whose passion, hatred, and ignorance are shattered,

children.text: kṣīṇāsravam arhantaṃ (!) tan me śakra varaṃ dada || [3] ||
children.translated_text: An <s>Arhat</s> with defilements destroyed—grant me that boon, O <s>Śakra</s>! [3]

children.text: yasya śailopamaṃ cittaṃ sthitan na anukampati |
children.translated_text: One whose mind is like a mountain, steadfast, unmoved by compassion,

children.text: yo vimuktiṃ saṃjāneyā tan me śakra varaṃ dada || [4] ||
children.translated_text: One who would realize liberation—grant me that boon, O <s>Śakra</s>! [4]

children.text: yasyā ure ca pāre ca madhye nāsti na kiñcana |
children.translated_text: One for whom on this shore, the far shore, and in between there is nothing at all,

children.text: akiñcanam adānaṃ ca tan me śakra varaṃ dada || [5] ||
children.translated_text: One possessing nothing, without clinging—grant me that boon, O <s>Śakra</s>! [5]

children.text: vāri puṣkarapatre vā ārāgre iva sarṣapaḥ |
children.translated_text: Like water on a lotus leaf, or like a mustard seed on the point of an awl,

children.text: yo na lipyati kāmeṣu tan me śakra varaṃ dada || [6] ||
children.translated_text: he who is not stained by sensual desires — grant me that boon, O <s>Śakra</s>! [6]
One of great learning, of varied discourse, an attendant of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: parṇabhāravisaṃyuktaṃ tan me śakra varaṃ dada || [7] ||
children.translated_text: freed from the burden of [worldly] foliage — grant me that boon, O <s>Śakra</s>! [7]

body.text: śakra āha |
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: nāham arhantam īśemi nāham arhanteṣv īśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: I have no power over <s>Arhats</s>; I am not the master of <s>Arhats</s>.
Choose another boon, O maidens — even [something rivaling] the moon and sun! [8]

body.text: kumāryo āhuḥ |
body.translated_text: The maidens said:

children.translated_text: One who has no mastery yet desires to be master, [is] an inferior boon-granter.

children.text: asvāmiko varaṃ dattvā kathaṃ śakra kariṣyasi || [9] ||
children.translated_text: Having granted a boon over which you have no mastery, what will you do, O <s>Śakra</s>? [9]

children.text: ubhau kūlau asaṃprāptaḥ atīrthe prataren nadīm |
children.translated_text: Not reaching either bank, you would cross the river at a non-ford.

children.text: eṣa śakra viṣaṇṇo si paṇkevāsi jaradgavaḥ || [10] ||
children.translated_text: Here, O <s>Śakra</s>, you are dejected — like an old ox stuck in the mud! [10]

body.text: śakra āha |
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: upāsikā vo kanyāyo api ca ye upāsakā |
children.translated_text: You, O maidens, are <s>upāsikās</s> (lay-women), and there are also <s>upāsakas</s> (lay-men).

children.text: dharmeṇa vo ahaṃ bhrātā anujānāmi vo varaṃ || [11] ||
children.translated_text: By the <s>Dharma</s> I am your brother; I grant you your boon. [11]

body.text: kumāryo āhaṃsuḥ |
body.translated_text: The maidens said:

children.text: naiva te śakra yācāmo nāpi unnodayāma te |
children.translated_text: We do not ask anything of you, O <s>Śakra</s>, nor do we urge you on.

children.text: svayam eva śakra jānāhi kiṃ vareṇa kumāriṇāṃ || [12] ||
children.translated_text: Know for yourself, O <s>Śakra</s>, what use is a boon for maidens? [12]

body.text: 149.atha bhagavān tāsāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāṃ pūrve nivāsapratisaṃyuktāṃ pratijñākathāṃ vyākārṣīt |
body.translated_text: 149. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> recounted the aspiration-story connected with the previous abodes of those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>.

children.text: kadāhaṃ vīṇāṃ vā madhurāṃ saptatantrīyutāṃ manoramām |
children.translated_text: 'When shall I, [like] a sweet <s>vīṇā</s> fitted with seven strings and delightful,

children.text: dharmaṃ pravyāhariṣyāmi tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [1] ||
children.translated_text: proclaim the <s>Dharma</s>? When will that come to pass? [1]'

body.text: samanvāharasi śukle | evaṃ hy etad bhagavan | eṣāpi tatraivāsi | etāye praṇidhānam abhūṣi | aparāpi tatraivāsi | tām api bhagavān vyākārṣīt |
body.translated_text: 'Do you recall, <s>Śuklā</s>?' 'Indeed so, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'She too was there. This was her aspiration.' There was another too who was also there. The <s>Bhagavān</s> recounted her [story] as well:

children.translated_text: 'When shall I cross the subterranean waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: amajjamānā gamiṣyāma tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [2] ||
children.translated_text: without sinking? When will that come to pass? [2]'

body.text: samanvāharasy utpalavarṇe | evaṃ hy etad bhagavan eṣāpi tatraivāsi | etasyāpy etaṃ praṇidhānam abhūṣi | aparāpi tatraivāsi | tām api bhagavān vyākārṣīt |
body.translated_text: 'Do you recall, <s>Utpalavarṇā</s>?' 'Indeed so, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'She too was there. This too was her aspiration.' There was another too who was also there. The <s>Bhagavān</s> recounted her [story] as well:

children.translated_text: 'When shall I, having gathered rag-cloths from the road,

children.text: saṃghāṭīṃ kṛtvā dhārayiṣyaṃ tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [3] ||
children.translated_text: make a patchwork robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>) and wear it? When will that come to pass? [3]'
'When shall I, in mountain fastnesses, having abandoned fear and dread,

children.text: cittaṃ ṛjuṃ kariṣyāmi tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [4] ||
children.translated_text: make my mind upright? When will that come to pass? [4]'

body.text: samanvāharasi paṭaccare | evam hy etad bhagavan | eṣāpi tatraivāsi | etasyāpy etaṃ praṇidhānam abhūṣi | aparāpi tatraivāsi | tām api bhagavān vyākārṣīt |
body.translated_text: 'Do you recall, <s>Paṭaccarā</s>?' 'Indeed so, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'She too was there. This too was her aspiration.' There was another too who was also there. The <s>Bhagavān</s> recounted her [story] as well:

children.translated_text: 'When shall I rub with my hand this shaven head, touched by the razor's edge?

children.text: pāṇinā parimārjiṣyaṃ tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [5] ||
children.translated_text: When will that come to pass? [5]'
'When shall I, on a winter's night, with robes dampened by the rain,

children.text: piṇḍapātaṃ cariṣyāmi kadā nas tad bhaviṣyati || [6] ||
children.translated_text: go forth on the alms-round? When will that come to pass for us? [6]'

body.text: samanvāharasi kṛśagautami | evam etad bhagavan | eṣāpi tatraivāsi | etasyā pretaṃ praṇidhānam abhūṣi | aparāpi tatraivāsi | tām api bhagavān vyākārṣīt |
body.translated_text: 'Do you recall, <s>Kṛśagautamī</s>?' 'Indeed so, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'She too was there. This too was her aspiration.' There was another too who was also there. The <s>Bhagavān</s> recounted her [story] as well:

children.translated_text: 'When shall I, like the king of stars, surrounded by constellations,

children.text: saṃghaṃ parihariṣyāmi tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [7] ||
children.translated_text: attend upon the <s>Saṃgha</s>? When will that come to pass? [7]'

children.text: kadāhaṃ candro ca vimalo viprasanno anāvilo |
children.translated_text: 'When shall I, pure and spotless like the moon, clear and untroubled,

children.text: śuddhaṃ cittaṃ adhiṣṭhihiṣyaṃ tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [8] ||
children.translated_text: establish a purified mind? When will that come to pass? [8]'

body.text: samanvāharasi mahāprajāpati | evaṃ hy etad bhagavan | eṣāpi tatraivāsi | etasyāpy etat praṇidhānam abhūṣi | aparāpi tatraivāsi | tām bhagavān vyākārṣīt |
body.translated_text: 'Do you recall, <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>?' 'Indeed so, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'She too was there. This too was her aspiration.' There was another too who was also there. The <s>Bhagavān</s> recounted her [story]:

children.translated_text: 'When shall I give to the <s>Saṃgha</s> a monastery that is a refuge, [...] well-built?

children.text: saṃghe dānāni dāsyāmi tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [9] ||
children.translated_text: When will that come to pass? [9]'

children.text: kadāhaṃ mañcam vā pīṭham vā bisi caturasrakāṇi vā |
children.translated_text: 'When shall I give to the <s>Saṃgha</s> beds, seats, and four-cornered cushions?

children.text: saṃghe dānāni dāsyāmi tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [10] ||
children.translated_text: When will that come to pass? [10]'
'When shall I give to the <s>Saṃgha</s> <s>Kāśi</s>-cloth, linen, and cotton garments?

children.text: saṃghe dānāni dāsyāmi tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [11] ||
children.translated_text: When will that come to pass? [11]'

children.text: kadāhaṃ sumbhakaṃ pātraṃ sukṛtaṃ sādhu niṣṭhitaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'When shall I give to the <s>Saṃgha</s> a <s>sumbhaka</s> bowl, well-crafted and finely finished?

children.text: saṃghe dānāni dāsyāmi tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [12] ||
children.translated_text: When will that come to pass? [12]'
'When shall I give to the <s>Saṃgha</s> various foods, prepared with various flavors?

children.text: saṃghe dānāni dāsyāmi tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [13] ||
children.translated_text: When will that come to pass? [13]'
'When shall I give to the <s>Saṃgha</s> rice-porridge served with pure meat?

children.text: saṃghe dānāni dāsyāmi tat kadā nu bhaviṣyati || [14] ||
children.translated_text: When will that come to pass? [14]'

body.text: 150. tatra tāsāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāṃ cakṣur gocaraṃ nāsti | yāṃ jānesuḥ | tāyo āhaṃsuḥ | kā puna sā bhagavan āsi | bhagavān āha | viśākhā mṛgāramātā |
body.translated_text: 150. Now those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> did not have [divine] vision regarding her. They did not know her. They asked: 'Who then was she, <s>Bhagavān</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Viśākhā Mṛgāramātā</s> (Viśākhā, the mother of Mṛgāra).'

body.text: tena kālena tena samayena aparā hy etā bhikṣuṇīyo kṛkiṇo rājñaḥ sapta dhītaro abhūṣi | atha śuklā bhikṣuṇī gṛheṇa gṛhaṃ bhāṣaṇāya nīyati | sā dāni apareṇa gṛhabhāṣaṇāya nītā bhikṣuṇīhi vipravustā | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ mahāprajāpatī gautamī bhagavato ārocayati | bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha śuklāṃ | sā dāni śabdāpitā | bhagavān | āha | satyaṃ śukle | evaṃ nāma tvaṃ bhikṣuṇībhir vinā vipravasasi | tena hi na kṣamati bhikṣuṇīhi vinā vipravasituṃ ekāṃ rātrim pi |
body.translated_text: At that time, at that occasion, there were other <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> who had been the seven daughters of King <s>Kṛkin</s>. Then the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Śuklā</s> was being taken from house to house for conversation. She was then taken by another for household conversation and became separated from the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> reported it to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon <s>Śuklā</s>.' She was then summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is it true, <s>Śuklā</s>, that you dwell apart from the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>?' 'Therefore, it is not proper for a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> to dwell apart [from the community] even for a single night.'

body.text: 151. eṣaivārthotpattiḥ | bhagavāñ chrāvastīyaṃ viharati | vistareṇa nidānaṃ kṛtvā | bhikṣuṇīyo dāni adhvānaṃ gacchanti | tahin dāni aparā bhikṣuṇī jarādurbalā vyādhidurbalā sārthāt parihīṇā | sā rātriṃ vipravustā | tāya dāni kaukṛtyaṃ kṛtaṃ | kaukṛtyena bhikṣuṇīnāṃ vistareṇārocayati | yāvat mahāprajāpatī pi gautamī bhagavato ārocayati | bhagavān āha | tena hi anāpattiḥ glānāya |
body.translated_text: 151. This itself is the origin-story. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. With the detailed background explained: <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> were traveling on a road. There, another <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, weak from old age and weak from illness, fell behind the caravan. She spent the night separated [from them]. She then felt remorse. With remorse, she reported it in detail to the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. Eventually <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> also reported it to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, there is no offense for one who is ill.'

body.text: 152. eṣaivārthotpattiḥ | bhagavān śrāvastīyaṃ viharati | vistareṇa nidānaṃ kṛtvā | kāpilavāstavyehi śākiyehi saṃsthāgāraḥ kārāpitaḥ | na co aciraniṣṭhitaḥ | tehi dāni tahiṃ rakṣapālāḥ sthāpitāḥ | na kasyacit praveśo dātavyo ti bhagavān prathamaṃ paribhokṣyati | paścād vayaṃ paribhokṣyāmo ti | atha rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kośalasya putro virūḍhako nāma kumāraḥ kapilavastuṃ gatako mātulānām antike śikṣāmāṇāya | so dāni tehi rakṣapālehi pramattehi saṃsthāgāraṃ praviṣṭaḥ krīḍanāya | so dāni tehi rakṣapālehi anyehi ca śākiyehi dṛṣṭo | te dāni ruṣitā itikitikāya putra dāsīputra kahiṃ praviṣṭo 'si ti | ocapeṭitaḥ | ekena hastena bāhāyāṃ gṛhītvā dvitīyena hastena grīvāyāṃ saṃsthāgārād bahiś choritaḥ | virūḍhako utkaṇṭhitaḥ | taṃ dāni tehi śākiyehi saṃsthāgāra puruṣamātrābhūmiṃ khānāpayitvā navena pāṃsunā pūrayitvā gandhodakena siktaḥ | virūḍhakena śrutaṃ | sa sutarāṃ ruṣitaḥ | āghātacittam utpāditavān | yady ahaṃ rājyaṃ pratilabheyaṃ śākiyānāṃ nidhanaṃ kariṣye | so dāni śrāvastīyam āgataḥ | tasya duḥkhaśāyī nāma baṭukaḥ sevako | so dāni tasyāha | yadāhaṃ rājye pratiṣṭhito bhaveyaṃ tadā me smārayiṣyasi śākiyānām antam gamiṣyaṃ | rātri trivantam eva vairam anuvicitayati | kadāci dāni rājā prasenajit kośalo udyānabhūmin nirgataḥ | tañ ca virūḍhakena nagaradvāraṃ bandhāpitaṃ | śaṅkhā ādhmāsyanti ghuṣyanti | virūḍhako rājā virūḍhakasya rājyam iti | rājā prasenajit kośalo na bhūyaḥ praveśaṃ labhati | virūḍhakenāmātyānāṃ dūto pracito | yasya bhavanto gṛheṇārthaḥ putradāreṇa cārthaḥ sa praviśatu nagaraṃ | evam akriyamāṇe yuṣmākaṃ putradāraṃ vyasanam āpādayiṣyāmīti | amātyā rājānaṃ pṛcchanti | kim ājñāpayati devo yudhyāmaḥ | rājā bravīti | mā yudhyantu bhavantaḥ | idānim vā paścād vā etasyaiva etaṃ rājyaṃ gacchatha | etasyaiva ājānatha | mā paścād yuṣmākaṃ duḥkhaṃ utpādayiṣyati | te ekadvikāya nagaraṃ praviṣṭāḥ | rājā dāni ātmatṛtīyo, udyānabhūmīyaṃ saṃsthito pānīyapālo mallī ca rājā dṛṣṭasatyo na paritasyati | vastu vistareṇa kartavyaṃ | yāvat virūḍhako mātyān āmantrayati | yo dāni bhaṇe rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ jugupseya tasya kiṃ daṇḍaḥ | āmātyā āhaṃsuḥ | vadho mahārāja | rāja āha | pūrvam ahaṃ kumārabhūtaḥ śākiyānāṃ saṃsthāgāraṃ praviṣṭaḥ tehi mama jugupsāya saṃsthāgāraṃ puruṣasaṃsthāgāraṃ puruṣamātraṃ khānāpayitva pāṃsunā pūrayitvā kṣīragandhodakena bhittiyo tāyo dhovitāyo? mayā teṣāṃ vairaṃ pratikartavyaṃ yadi bhagavāṃs teṣāṃ nānukampati | atha bhagavān anukampati | nāhaṃ śakṣyāmi kiñcit pratikartuṃ | āmātyā āhaṃsuḥ | śrūyate mahārāja | śramaṇo gautamo vītarāgaḥ | vītarāgaś ca jñātīnāṃ nirapekṣā bhavanti | udyujyantu mahārāja | śakṣyāma vayaṃ teṣāṃ nigrahītuṃ | bhagavān dāni virūḍhakasya imam evaṃ rūpaṃ cetaḥ parivitarkam ājñāya kālasyaiva nivāsayitvā pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīye nagarīye piṇḍāya caritvā anyataraṃ śākhoṭavṛkṣaṃ niśrāya niṣīdati sma | atha khalu rājā virūḍhako caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ sannāhayitvā hastikāyaṃ aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ śrāvastyāṃ nagaryāṃ niryāti kapilavastuṃ nagaraṃ saṃprasthitaḥ | adrākṣīd rājā virūḍhako bhagavantaṃ śākhoṭakavṛkṣaṃ niśrāya niṣaṇṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca puna yena bhagavāṃs tena hastināgaṃ prerayati | atha khalu rājā virūḍhako yāvad eva yānasya bhūmis tāvad yānena gatvā hastināgāt pratyāruhya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantam etad avocat | santi bhagavann anye vṛkṣāḥ | aśvatthanyagrodhasaptaparṇādyāḥ śobhanāś ca śītalāś ca tān utsṛjya itarasya pratyavarasya viralapatrasya śākhoṭakavṛkṣasyādhastān niṣaṇṇaḥ | bhagavān āha | śītalā mahārāja jñātīnāṃ cchāyā | atha khalu rājño virūḍhakasya etad abhavat | anukampati bhagavān jñātīn iti | tato yeva pratinivartayitvā śrāvastīn nagaram anupraviṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: 152. This itself is the origin-story. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. With the detailed background explained: The <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> had a council-hall built. It had been recently completed. They placed guards there: 'No one is to be allowed entry. The <s>Bhagavān</s> shall enjoy it first; afterwards we shall enjoy it.' Then the prince <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, son of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, had gone to <s>Kapilavastu</s> to learn in the presence of his maternal uncles. When the guards were inattentive, he entered the council-hall to play. He was then seen by those guards and other <s>Śākyas</s>. They were angered: 'Son of a slave-woman's son! Where have you entered!' He was slapped. Seized by one hand on the arm and by the other on the neck, he was thrown out of the council-hall. <s>Virūḍhaka</s> was distressed. Then those <s>Śākyas</s> had the council-hall dug to a man's depth, filled with fresh soil, and sprinkled with scented water. <s>Virūḍhaka</s> heard of it. He was greatly angered and harbored a hostile intent: 'If I obtain the kingdom, I shall destroy the <s>Śākyas</s>.' He then returned to <s>Śrāvastī</s>. He had a servant boy named <s>Duḥkhaśāyin</s>. He told him: 'When I am established in the kingdom, you shall remind me — I shall bring about the end of the <s>Śākyas</s>.' Night and day he brooded over the enmity. One day King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> went out to the park-grounds. <s>Virūḍhaka</s> had the city gate closed. Conch-shells were blown and it was proclaimed: '<s>Virūḍhaka</s> is king! The kingdom belongs to <s>Virūḍhaka</s>!' King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> could no longer gain entry. <s>Virūḍhaka</s> dispatched a messenger to the ministers: 'Whoever desires [the welfare of] his household, wife, and children — let him enter the city. If you do not do so, I shall bring calamity upon your wives and children.' The ministers asked the king: 'What does His Majesty command? Shall we fight?' The king said: 'Do not fight, lords. Now or later, this kingdom belongs to him. Go; submit to him. Let him not cause you suffering later.' They entered the city one or two at a time. The king then remained in the park-grounds with only two companions — the water-carrier and <s>Mallī</s>. The king, being a <s>stream-enterer</s> (<s>dṛṣṭasatya</s>), was not distressed. The matter should be told in detail. Eventually <s>Virūḍhaka</s> addressed his ministers: 'What punishment is due to one who insults a <s>kṣatriya</s> king?' The ministers said: 'Death, O great king.' The king said: 'Previously, when I was a prince, I entered the council-hall of the <s>Śākyas</s>. They treated me with contempt, had the hall dug to a man's depth, filled it with soil, and washed the walls with milk-scented water. I must take revenge upon them — unless the <s>Bhagavān</s> shows them compassion. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> shows compassion, I shall not be able to do anything against them.' The ministers said: 'It is heard, O great king, that the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is free from passion. Those free from passion are indifferent toward relatives. Make ready, O great king! We shall be able to subdue them.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing this thought and deliberation of <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, dressed at the proper time, took his bowl and robe, walked for alms in the city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and sat down at the foot of a certain <s>śākhoṭa</s> tree. Then King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, having equipped his fourfold army — elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry — marched out of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, heading for <s>Kapilavastu</s>. King <s>Virūḍhaka</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> seated at the foot of the <s>śākhoṭa</s> tree and directed his elephant toward him. King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, having gone as far as possible by vehicle, descended from his elephant, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, there are other trees — <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>nyagrodha</s>, <s>saptaparṇa</s>, and others — both beautiful and cool. Having passed them by, why do you sit beneath this inferior, thin-leafed <s>śākhoṭa</s> tree?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Cool, O great king, is the shade of one's kinsmen.' Then King <s>Virūḍhaka</s> thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> feels compassion for his kinsmen.' And so he turned back and re-entered <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

body.text: bhagavān dāni śrāvastīyaṃ yathābhiramyaṃ viharitvā kapilavastuṃ nagaraṃ prakrāmi | yāvac chākyān vinayati | vinayitvā tatraiva viharati nyagrodhārāme | virūḍhakīyaṃ sūtraṃ vistareṇa kartavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having dwelt at <s>Śrāvastī</s> as long as he wished, set out for <s>Kapilavastu</s>. He converted the <s>Śākyas</s>. Having converted them, he continued dwelling there at the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s>. The <s>Virūḍhaka Sūtra</s> should be told in full detail.

body.text: 153. eṣā evārthotpattiḥ | bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | rājā dāni virūḍhako śākīyān vadhitvā śākiyakanyāyo ādāya śrāvastīṃ pratigataḥ tadyathā | cārū ca nāma | upacārū ca nāma | sumanā ca nāma | manoharā | sālavatī | abhayā ca nāma | so dāni sārdhaṃ krīḍanto ramanto paricārayantaḥ abhikṣṇaṃ vadati | nihatā me grāmakaṇṭakāḥ | śākiyajanapadakaṇṭakāḥ | nihatā me pratyarthikāḥ pratyamitrāḥ | yad idam śākiyāḥ śākyaputrā iti |
body.translated_text: 153. This is the origin-story. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, having slaughtered the <s>Śākyas</s>, took the <s>Śākya</s> maidens and returned to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, namely: <s>Cārū</s>, <s>Upacārū</s>, <s>Sumanā</s>, <s>Manoharā</s>, <s>Sālavatī</s>, and <s>Abhayā</s>. While sporting, enjoying, and being attended by them, he repeatedly said: 'Destroyed are my village-thorns, the <s>Śākya</s> country-thorns! Destroyed are my adversaries and enemies—these <s>Śākyas</s>, sons of <s>Śākya</s>!'

body.text: atha khalv abhayā rājadhītā rājānaṃ virūḍhakam etad avocat | mā deva evaṃ vada nihatā me grāmakaṇṭakāḥ śākiyā iti | santi deva śākiyāḥ kṣāntisampannāḥ | sauratyasampannāḥ | evaṃ śīlaśrutatyāgasamādhiprajñāsampannāḥ | evaṃ buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ | dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ | buddhe avetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ | dharme saṃghe avetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ | prāṇātipātāt prativiratāḥ | yāvad āryakānteḥ śīleḥ samanvāgatāḥ | santi deva śākiyāḥ śrotaāpannāḥ sakṛdāgāmino nāgāminas te devena adūṣakā anaparādhino jīvitād vyavaropitāḥ | tat te duḥkhaṃ vedanīyaṃ bhaviṣyati | bahu te pāpakaṃ karma kṛtaṃ | bahu te apuṇyaṃ prasūtaṃ |
body.translated_text: Then the princess <s>Abhayā</s> said this to King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>: 'Do not say this, Your Majesty: "Destroyed are my village-thorns, the <s>Śākyas</s>." There are <s>Śākyas</s>, Your Majesty, endowed with patience, endowed with gentleness, endowed with virtue, learning, generosity, concentration, and wisdom, who have gone to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge, gone to the <s>Dharma</s> for refuge, possessed of unwavering faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, in the <s>Dharma</s>, in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, who have refrained from taking life, who were endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones. There are <s>Śākyas</s>, Your Majesty, who are <s>Śrotaāpannas</s> (stream-enterers), <s>Sakṛdāgāmins</s> (once-returners), and <s>Anāgāmins</s> (non-returners). Those whom you, Your Majesty, have put to death though blameless and guiltless—that will result in painful retribution for you. Much evil <s>karma</s> has been done by you; much demerit has been produced by you.'

body.text: 154. atha rājā virūḍhakaḥ kupitaḥ yāvat kāraṇāntikaṃ mahāmātram āmantrayati | tvaṃ hi bhaṇe puruṣa mama bhogehi jāyayasi | mama sukhena jīvasi | kanyāyo śākiyāyinīyo mama pratyarthikāyo pratrasitāyo | mama jīvitaṃ necchanti | mama sukhaṃ nābhinandanti | so 'ham antaḥpuramadhyagato pi etāsām aviśvastaḥ | śayanagato pi śayyāṃ kalpayanto pi | tena hi bhaṇe mahāmātra imāyo śākiyāyinīyo daṇḍahatāyo kṛtvā karṇanāsāhastapādacchinnāyo kṛtvā taptena telena kāyaṃ pariṣiñcitvā jīvantikāyo evaṃ parikhāyāṃ cchorayā | atha kāraṇāntikasya etad abhavat | yan dāni ahaṃ śākiyāyinīnāṃ āsi darśanaṃ pi na labhamāno tāyo etāyo mama hastagatāyo yan nūnam aham etāhi saha krīḍeyaṃ rameyaṃ paricārayeyaṃ | so dāni tāhi sārdhaṃ svake gṛhe pravicārayati | aśrauṣīd rājā virūḍhako kāraṇāntikas tāhi sārdhaṃ krīḍati yāvan na ca pi yathoktaṃ karotīti | atha khalu virūḍhakaḥ kāraṇāntikam āmantrayati | gaccha tāsāṃ śākiyāyinīnāṃ yathoktaṃ kuru | mā te jīvitād vyavaropayiṣyāmīti | atha kāraṇāntikaḥ yathoktam akārṣīt | yāvat parikhāyāṃ jīvantīyo eva choritāyo | tāyo tatra duḥkhaṃ tīvrāṃ kaṭukāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti | anventi krandanti evan tānenti trātenti | bhaginījñātikāpriyaṃ śākiya maṇḍalaṃ | ramaṇīyā bhavati to janma bhūmiḥ | hā ramaṇīyo jambudvīpaḥ | sūktavādī bhagavān iti paridevanti | tahi dāni mahājanakāyo sannipatito |
body.translated_text: 154. Then King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, angered, addressed the chief minister in charge of punishments: 'You, fellow, live off my wealth, you enjoy my comforts! These <s>Śākya</s> maidens are my enemies and adversaries. They do not wish for my life; they do not rejoice in my happiness. Even in the midst of the inner palace, I am not safe from them. Take these six <s>Śākya</s> maidens, cut off their hands and feet, cut off their ears and noses, and throw them into a ditch!' The minister said: 'Very well, Your Majesty.' Having cut off the hands and feet of those <s>Śākya</s> women, cut off their ears and noses, he threw them into a ditch.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān kālasyaiva nivāsayitvā pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīn nagarīṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ | yāvad āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayati | kasyaiṣā gautamī mātā | mahato janakāyasya nirghoṣo yāvad rājñā virūḍhakena ṣaṇṇāṃ śākiyāyinīnāṃ yāvat tasya kṛpaṇena yāvan sūktavādī bhagavān iti krandanti | sādhu bhagavān arthakāmo jñātīnām anukampyārthaṃ upasaṃkrāmatu | apy eva nāma bhagavataḥ sammukhād dharmaṃ śruṇitvā api svargopigā bhaveṃsuḥ |
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having dressed early in the morning and taken up his bowl and robe, entered the city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. He addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Whose mother is that, <s>Gautamī</s>? What is this loud cry of the great crowd?' [He was told] that King <s>Virūḍhaka</s> had [mutilated] the six <s>Śākya</s> women, and they were pitifully crying: 'Well-spoken is the <s>Bhagavān</s>!'

body.text: 155. atha khalu bhagavāṃ śakraṃ devānām indraṃ samanvāharati sma | atha khalu śakro devānām indraḥ śacim āmantrayati | eṣa śaci bhagavān jñātīnām upasaṃkramati anukampārthaṃ | gaccha śaci tāyo śākiyāyinīyo parikhāyā uddharitvā saṃprajānaṃ niṣīdāpehi vastreṇācchādehi bhagavān upasaṃkramiṣyati | atha khalu śacī tāyo śākiyāyinīyo parikhāyā uddharitvā saṃprajānan niṣīdāpayitvā vastreṇācchāditā |
body.translated_text: 155. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> mentally summoned <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, addressed <s>Śacī</s>: 'See, <s>Śacī</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> is going to visit his kinswomen out of compassion. Go, <s>Śacī</s>, lift those <s>Śākya</s> women out of the ditch, seat them mindfully, cover them with cloth—the <s>Bhagavān</s> will approach them.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān yāvat tāyomaindryā spharitvā yat kiñcit kāyikaṃ caitasikaṃ ca duḥkhavedanāgataṃ sarvaṃ taṃ pratiprasraṃbheti | bhikṣūn āmantrayati | tṛpyatāṃ bhikṣavo bhagavatīṣu ko bhikṣavo bhavam abhinandeya ko upādiyeya anyatra bālapṛthagjanānāṃ andhānāṃ acakṣukānāṃ paśyatha | bhikṣavaḥ etāyo śākiyāyinīyo manuṣyakehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi krīḍitvā ramitvā pravicārayitvā etarhi jñātikṣaye ca bhogakṣaye ca karmasya ca sammukhībhāvād duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti |
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> pervaded them with his divine power, and whatever bodily and mental painful feelings they had experienced—all of that was calmed. He addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'Be satisfied, <s>bhikṣus</s>, with these noble women. Who, <s>bhikṣus</s>, would delight in existence? Who would cling [to it], other than foolish ordinary people, blind, without eyes? See, <s>bhikṣus</s>, these [women]—'

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tāyo śākiyāyinīyo āmantrayati | sacen manyatha bhaginīyo yad idaṃ yuṣmākaṃ hasto ca pādo ca chinno api tu te vedayanti vā na vā | no hīdaṃ bhagavan | asti ca tatpratyayā duḥkhā vedanā | evaṃ hy etad bhagavan sacen manyatha bhaginīyo cakṣuḥ svabhāvaṃ vedayati | yāvad asti ca tatpratyayā duḥkhā vedanā | evaṃ hy etad bhagavan | evam aśiṣṭāny āyatanāni | evaṃ skandhadhātavaḥ | evaṃ keśā romā nakhā | evaṃ sarvā aśubhapālī | evaṃ ca punar duḥkhā vedanā parādhīnā parapratibaddhā pratyayādhīnā pratyayapratibaddhā iti viditvā dvā triṃśatīhi ākārehi prakṛti bhinnaḥ | saṃskārapuñjaḥ parijñeyaḥ | ataś ca bhaginīyo ārya śrāvaka imesāṃ pañcopādānaskandhānāṃ nātmānaṃ samanupaśyati | ātmīyān yāvat pratyātmam eva parinirvāti | idam avocat bhagavān | yāvat tāyo paṭa śākiyāyinīyo dhītāṃ anāgāmitāṃ sākṣāt kuryuḥ | pañcānāñ ca bhikṣuśatānam anupādāyāsravebhyaś cittāni vimucyeyuḥ | anekeṣāñ ca devatāśatasahasrāṇāṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣu viśuddhaṃ |
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed those <s>Śākya</s> women: 'If you consider, sisters, that your hands and feet have been cut off—yet do they feel sensation or not?' 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. But there is painful sensation conditioned by that.' 'Just so it is, sisters. If you consider, sisters, does the eye experience sensation by its own nature?'... up to: 'There is indeed painful sensation conditioned by that.'

body.text: 156. athāyuṣmān vāgīśas tasyām eva parṣadi yāvad bhagavān āha | pratibhātu te vāgīśa yāvad adhyābhāṣi |
body.translated_text: 156. Then the Venerable <s>Vāgīśa</s>, in that very assembly... the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Let it come to you, <s>Vāgīśa</s>,' and he spoke:

children.translated_text: This [world], gone to the perishable, is indeed empty,
Wherein the one who grasps wrongly is defeated;
Thinking thus 'I' and 'mine,'
They increase the funeral pyre again and again. [1]

children.text: śūnyam asāram kañ ca kāyaṃ viditvā
children.translated_text: Having known this body to be empty and without essence,
Subject to cessation and destruction as it is,
Arisen and dissolved, gone through existence—
Who, a practitioner yoked to the goal, would delight in those gone through existence? [2]

body.text:
idañ ca duḥkhaṃ vedayitvā
tasya mūlaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca utpadyati |

children.translated_text: And having seen its root, it arises;
Body and mind [rooted] in the root of suffering—
This goes with the current; the liberated mind destroys <s>Māra</s>. [3]

body.translated_text: Having experienced this suffering,
