body.text: 182. bhagavān śrāvastīyaṃ viharati | aparo dāni manuṣyo kāṣṭhavāṇijyāṃ karoti | so dāni kāṣṭhavāham ādāya antarāpaṇam okasto | āpaṇiko āha | kiṃ kāṣṭhavāhasya mūlyaṃ | āha | kārṣāpaṇaṃ gaccha gṛhadvāre avatāriyā gacchāhi | ito yeva kārṣāpaṇaṃ gṛhītvā yāsyasīti | bhavati ca śeṣaṃ vyavahārakāle | so dāni kāṣṭhavāham ādāya gacchati | sthūlanandā nāma bhikṣuṇī upāśrayāto niḥkramati | tayā ca dṛṣṭo | āha | dīrghāyu vikrayo kāṣṭhavāho | āha | vikrīto | āha | kathaṃ vikrīto | āha | kārṣāpaṇena | ahaṃ dvau kārṣāpaṇā dāsyāmi | so dāni manuṣya paśyati yady ahaṃ dvau kārṣāpaṇā labhāmi mah'argham mayā vikrītaṃ bhaviṣyati | so taṃ adhikaritvā kāṣṭhavāhamūlyaṃ gṛhṇiya śakaṭam āruhitvā tasyāpaṇikasyāgratenopayāti | so dān āha | āgaccha kārṣāpaṇaṃ gṛhṇāhi | so dān āha | mayā anyaṃhi vikrīto | so dān āha | kathaṃ | vikrīto | āha | dvābhyāṃ kārṣāpaṇābhyāṃ | kena krīto | āha | eṣātra nandā nāma śramaṇikā | tayā krīto | so dāni ojjhāyati | kiyanto tāye śramaṇikāye kārṣāpanāḥ | mayā kārṣāpaṇena paṇitaṃ | sā dvihi kārṣāpaṇehi paṇeti | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocenti yāvad bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 182. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Now a man was engaged in the timber trade. He took a load of wood into the marketplace. The shopkeeper said: 'What wood...'

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | jānantīti svayam vā jāneya parato vā śruṇeya ākāravantena darśanena ākāravantena śramaṇena | paropagataṃ ti pareṇa gṛhītaṃ | cetāpayed iti jānāpayet | nissargikapācatikaṃ | peyālaṃ | etaṃ dāni āpaṇikasya vā prāvarikasya vā kiñcid bhāṇḍam upagatam bhavati | tena ca bhikṣuṇī arthīkā bhavati na dāni kṣamati tahiṃ antarāyayituṃ | yatati nissargikaṃ bhavati | atha khu ekā śca sthitvā pratipālayitavyaṃ | yadānena pratimuktaṃ | bhavati tato so pṛcchitavyo vaktavyo | kiṃ tvayā mukto | yadi tāvad āha | parimaṇḍāmy ahaṃ me bhante | na kṣamati jānāpayituṃ | atha dān āha | jānāpayatu ārye nāham arthiko eteneti | jānāpayati anāpatiḥ | atha dāni bhikṣuṇīye kiñcid upakreyam bhavati pātram vā cīvaram vā na kṣamati antarā yatituṃ | yatati vinayātikramaḥ | atha dāni saṃghamadhye vaḍḍho vaḍḍhikāya jānāpayati anāpattiḥ | bhikṣur api paropagataṃ cetāpayati vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Knowingly' means she knows herself or has heard from another, with evidence of seeing, with evidence of hearing. 'Property of another' (<s>paropagata</s>) means that which has been taken by another...

madyapānaṃ [56] | nādarya [57] | upaśrotra [58] |
viniścaya [59] | saṃmohena [60] ||
body.translated_text: Summary verse: Poking with a finger [51]; for the purpose of theft [52]; earth [53]; invitation-ending [54]; 'I will not train' [55]; drinking liquor [56]; disregarding [57]; eavesdropping [58]...

body.text: ṣaṣṭho vargaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Sixth section.

body.text:
uddānaṃ |
sabhakto [61] | rājñaḥ [62] | sūcīgṛhaṃ [63] |
mañca [64] | tūla [65] | niṣīdanaṃ [66] |
kaṇḍupraticchādanaṃ [67] | sugatacīvaraṃ [68] |
abhyākhyānaṃ [69] | pariṇāmanena [70] ||
body.translated_text: Summary verse: With food [61]; king's [62]; needle-house [63]; bed [64]; cotton [65]; sitting-cloth [66]; itch-covering [67]; <s>Sugata</s>-robe [68]; ...

body.text: saptamo vargaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Seventh section.

body.text: ete sapta vargāḥ sādhāraṇāḥ | yathā yeva bhikṣuṇā tathā yeva kartavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: These seven sections are shared [with the monks]. They should be done just as [they are done] by a <s>bhikṣu</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 71
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 71:

body.text: saṃkramaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: Exchanging [robes] (<s>saṃkramaṇa</s>).

body.text: 184. bhagavān vaiśālīyaṃ viharati | atha bhadrā kāpileyī antevāsinīye apratisaṃviditā saṃghāṭiṃ prāvaritvā jñātikulaṃ gatā | bhikṣuṇīyo gocaraṃ prasthitāyo | tā dān āhaṃsuḥ | ehy ārye piṇḍapātaṃ gacchāmaḥ | āha | yāvat saṃghāṭīṃ gṛhṇāmi | sā dāni mārgayati ātmanaḥ saṃghāṭin na paśyati | tāye dāni bhavati avaśyam āryāya saṃghāṭī prāvaritā | arhati āryā mama saṃghāṭīṃ prāvaritvā gantuṃ | sā dān āha | gacchatha yūyaṃ āryamiśrikāyo nāhaṃ gacchāmi kim arthaṃ | āryā saṃghāṭīṃ prāvaritvā gatā | tā dān āhaṃsuḥ | āryāye saṃghāṭīṃ prāvaritvā āgacchāhīti | sā dān āha | notsahāmi āryā mama guruvarabhāvanīyā ceti | na gatā | sā chinnabhaktā saṃvṛtā | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | mahāprajāpatī pi gautamī bhagavata ārocayet | yāvad bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha bhadrāṃ | sā dāni śabdapitā yāvat satyaṃ bhadreti | etad eva sarvaṃ | bhagavān vistareṇa pṛcchati | yāvad evan nāma tvaṃ cīvarasaṃkramaṇaṃ karoṣi | duṣkṛtan te bhadre | tena hi na kṣamati cīvarasaṃkramaṇaṃ kartuṃ | atha khalu bhagavān mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm āmantrayati | peyālaṃ | yāvat |
body.translated_text: 184. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s>. Then <s>Bhadrā Kāpileyī</s>, without informing her pupil, wrapped herself in the latter's outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>) and went to her relatives' house. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> had set out for their alms-round. They said: 'Come, Noble One, let us go for almsfood.' She said: 'Let me just get my outer robe.' She searched for her own outer robe and could not find it. She then thought: 'The Noble One must have wrapped herself in my robe. It is not right for the Noble One to go wearing my outer robe.' She said: 'You go, Noble Ladies; I am not going. Why? The Noble One has gone wearing my robe.' They said: 'Come wearing the Noble One's robe!' She said: 'I cannot dare—the Noble One is my venerable teacher, to be honored.' She did not go. She went without food. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> too reported it to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon <s>Bhadrā</s>.' She was summoned. 'Is this true, <s>Bhadrā</s>?' Everything [was confirmed]. The <s>Bhagavān</s> questioned her in detail, [saying]: 'How is it that you exchange robes? You have done wrong, <s>Bhadrā</s>. Therefore, it is not permissible to exchange robes.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. [Abbreviation.] Until:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī cīvarasaṃkramaṇaṃ kuryāt pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should exchange robes—it is a <s>pācattika</s> (expiation) offense.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti | peyālaṃ cīvaran ti cīvaraṃ nāma saṃghāṭi yāvat dakaśāṭikā | saṃkramaṇan ti anyā anyāya | pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | na dāni kṣamati antevāsinīye apratisaṃviditā saṃghāṭīṃ prāvarituṃ | atha dāni prāvarati vaktavyā iyam mayā saṃghāṭī prāvaritā | yadi praviśeṣi mama saṃghāṭīṃ prāvaritvā praviśesi | athātirekaṃ cīvaram bhavati vaktavyā | iyam mayā tava saṃghāṭī prāvaritā | yadi praviśesi iminā cīvareṇa praviśesīti |
body.translated_text: 'If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' — [abbreviated]. 'Robe' means the outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>) up to the bathing cloth (<s>dakśāṭikā</s>). 'Transfer' means [giving] from one to another. It is a <s>pācattika</s> (expiation) offense, up to the rule establishment. It is not permissible for a pupil to wear the outer robe without informing [the preceptress]. If she wears it, she should say: 'This outer robe has been worn by me. If you [need to] enter, enter wearing my outer robe.' If there is an extra robe, she should say: 'This outer robe of yours has been worn by me. If you [need to] enter, enter with this robe.'

body.text: atha dāni bhikṣuṇī saṃghāṭiṃ dhoveti vā sīveti vā rañjeti vā | yadi pratibalā bhavati tasyā api saṃvibhāgaṃ kartavyaṃ | vaktavyā | tiṣṭha tvaṃ iheva ahan tava piṇḍapātasaṃvibhāgaṃ kariṣyāmīti | bhikṣuṇāpy evaṃ vaktavyaṃ | na vadati vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: Now, if a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> washes, sews, or dyes the outer robe — if she is capable, a share should be given to the other [nun] as well. She should say: 'Stay here; I will share alms-food with you.' A <s>bhikṣu</s> should also be told likewise. If she does not tell, she incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s> (disciplinary transgression). Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī cīvarasaṃkramaṇaṃ kuryāt pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should make a transfer of robes, it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: pācattikadharma 72
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> Rule 72

body.text: śramaṇacīvaraṃ
body.translated_text: The Renunciant's Robe (<s>śramaṇacīvara</s>)

body.text: 185. bhagavān śrāvastīyaṃ viharati | rāṣṭrapālā bhāgineya | yasyārthotpatti vistareṇa kartavyā |
body.translated_text: 185. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. <s>Rāṣṭrapālā</s>'s nephew — the origin story should be given in full.

body.text: eṣā evārthotpattiḥ | bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | gartodaro ca gartodaramātā ca gartodarapitā ca āgarasyānāgariyaṃ pravrajitāḥ | gartodarapitā gartodaramātā ca śākyehi pravrajitā gartodaro tīrthikehi | so dāni hastakambalena prāvṛto śītena khaṇakhaṇāyanto dantavīṇikāṃ vādayanto vihāram āgato | snehacarito mātṛgrāmo | so dān āha | putra gartodara śīta kito si | so dān āha | āma | tāya tasya uttarāsaṅgo surabho suphoṣito dinno prāvaraṇāya | so dāni prāvaritvā pānāgāraṃ gatvā pibanto āsati | jano dani ojjhāyati kim eṣāṃ mithyādṛṣṭikānāṃ vinipatitānāṃ yānagardabhānāṃ surābhraṣṭānāṃ ṛṣidhvajanena dinnena bhikṣuṇīhi śrutaṃ | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha gartodaramātāṃ | sā dāni śabdāpitā | tad eva sarvaṃ | bhagavān vistareṇa pṛcchati | yāvad ām bhagavan | bhagavān āha duṣkṛtaṃ te gartodaramāte | tena hi na kṣamati āgārikasya vā parivrājakasya vā svahastaṃ śramaṇacīvaraṃ dātuṃ | atha khalu bhagavān mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm āmantrayati | peyālaṃ yāvat paryavadātāni bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: This is the same origin story. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. <s>Gartodara</s>, <s>Gartodara</s>'s mother, and <s>Gartodara</s>'s father had all gone forth from the household life to homelessness. <s>Gartodara</s>'s father and <s>Gartodara</s>'s mother were ordained by the <s>Śākyas</s> [Buddhists], while <s>Gartodara</s> was ordained by the <s>tīrthikas</s>. He then came to the monastery wrapped in a woolen blanket, shivering with cold, his teeth chattering...

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī āgārikasya vā parivrājakasya vā svahastaṃ pramāṇacīvaraṃ dadyāt pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should give a properly-measured renunciant's robe with her own hand to a householder or a wandering ascetic, it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | āgārikasyeti gṛhiṇaḥ | parivrājakasyeti gautamajaṭilakaparyantaṃ kṛtvā | svahastan ti hastena hastaṃ | śramaṇacīvaran ti ṛṣidhvajaṃ | dadyāt pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | na kṣamati āgārikasya vā parivrājakasya vā svahastaṃ śramaṇacīvaraṃ dātuṃ | atha dāni bhikṣuṇī bhavati kṛtapuṇyā striyo dāni maṅgalārthāya dārakasya dārikāye vā kāṣāya khaṇḍaṃ yācanti | na kṣamati svahastaṃ dātuṃ kalpiyakārikāya dātavyaṃ | bhikṣur api āgārikasya vā parivrājakasya vā svahastaṃ śramaṇacīvaraṃ deti vinayātikramam āsādayati | atha dāni bhikṣuḥ kṛtapuṇyo bhavati yāvat kalpiyakārakeṇa dātavyaṃ | na kṣamati mahāntaṃ paṭaṃ dātuṃ | atha khu pottikhaṇḍaṃ dātavyaṃ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'To a householder' means to a layperson. 'To a wandering ascetic' means including up to <s>Gautama</s> ascetics and matted-hair ascetics. 'With her own hand' means hand to hand. 'Renunciant's robe' means the banner of a sage (<s>ṛṣidhvaja</s>). 'Should give' — it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to the rule establishment. It is not permissible to give a renunciant's robe with one's own hand to a householder or a wandering ascetic. Now, if a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>...

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī āgārikasya vā parivrājakasya vā svahastaṃ śramaṇacīvaraṃ dadyāt pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should give a renunciant's robe with her own hand to a householder or a wandering ascetic, it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: 186. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | bhikṣuṇīyo dāni kumārīnivastaṃ nivāsenti | jano dāni ojjhāyati | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīhi śrutaṃ | bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha | tena hi na kṣamati kumārīnivastena antaragṛhaṃ praviśituṃ | bhagavatā dāni antaravāso 'nujñāto | bhikṣuṇīyo dāni yathāgatān paṭān navān tantrodgatān puṣpadaśān antaravāsaṃ kurvanti | bhagavān āha | prāmāṇiko kartavyo | atha khalu bhagavān mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm āmantrayati | sannipātya gautamīye yāvat |
body.translated_text: 186. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Now, some <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> were wearing a maiden's garment [as their lower robe]. People criticized [them]. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> heard of this matter. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. [Abbreviated.] Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore it is not permissible to enter a household wearing a maiden's garment.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> then [prescribed the inner garment]...

body.text: antarvāsaṃ bhikṣuṇīya kārāpayantīya prāmāṇiko kārāpayitavyo tatredaṃ pramāṇaṃ dīrghaso catvāri vitastiyo | sugata vitastinā | tiryag dve tad uttariṃ kārāpeya cchedanapācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> having an inner garment (<s>antarvāsa</s>) made should have it made to the proper measure. The proper measure here is: in length, four spans (<s>vitasti</s>) by the <s>Sugata</s> span; in width, two [spans]. If she has it made exceeding [this measure], it is a <s>pācattika</s> requiring cutting [to size].

body.text: pācattikadharma 73, 74
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> Rules 73, 74

body.text: antarvāsan ti yat tad bhagavatānujñātaṃ | bhikṣuṇīya kārāpayantīyeti svayaṃ vā kuryāt pareṇa vā kārāpayet | tatredaṃ pramāṇaṃ dīrghaśo ti āyāmo | vistaro ti tiryag catvāri vitastiyo | sugatavitastinā ti tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho tasya yo vitasti so dvyardho mañcakapādo tad uttarim kārāpayed iti paraṃ pramāṇato cchedanapācattikaṃ | yāvat prajñaptiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Inner garment' means that which was authorized by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. 'A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> having it made' means she makes it herself or has it made by another. 'The proper measure here in length' means the longitudinal dimension. 'In width' means transversely, four spans. 'By the <s>Sugata</s> span' means [the span of] the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one — his span equals two and a half bedpost [measures]. 'If she has it made exceeding [this measure]'...

body.text: sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī dīrghaśo karoti prāmāṇikaṃ tiryak karoti atirekaṃ | evaṃ karoti kārāpeti niṣṭhāpanāntikaṃ āpattiḥ | kṛtaṃ labhati paribhogāntikaṃ vinayātikramam āsādayati | evaṃ tiryak karoti prāmāṇikaṃ dīrghaśo karoti atirekaṃ | ante karoti prāmāṇikaṃ madhye karoti atirekaṃ | madhye karoti prāmāṇikaṃ ante karoti atirekaṃ | dviguṇaṃ māpeti udakena saṃkucati saṃkucitaṃ māpeti udakena phoṣeti śuṣkaṃ vaḍḍhiṣyatīti pācattikam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: If that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> makes [the garment] to the proper measure in length but exceeds in width — [whether] she makes it or has it made, the offense [is incurred] at the completion [of making]. Having made it, she incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s> for each use. Likewise if she makes it to the proper measure in width but exceeds in length; if she makes the ends to the proper measure but the middle excessive; if she makes the middle to the proper measure but the ends excessive...

body.text: antarvāsaṃ bhikṣuṇīya kārāpayantīya prāmāṇikaṃ kārāpayitavyaṃ tatredaṃ pramāṇaṃ | dīrghaśo catvāri vitastiyo | sugatavitastinā | tiryag dve tad uttariṃ kārāpeya cchedanapācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> having an inner garment made should have it made to the proper measure. The proper measure here is: in length, four spans by the <s>Sugata</s> span; in width, two [spans]. If she has it made exceeding [this measure], it is a <s>pācattika</s> requiring cutting [to size].

body.text: pācattikadharma 74
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> Rule 74

body.text: saṃkakṣikā
body.translated_text: The Shoulder Cloth (<s>saṃkakṣikā</s>)

body.text: 187. bhagavān śrāvastīyaṃ viharati | aparā dāni bhikṣuṇī prāsādikā darśanīyā | tāye dāni pīnehi stanehi cīvaram utkṣiptaṃ | sā manuṣyehi uccagghīyati | paśyatha bhaṇe śramaṇikāya kīdṛśaṃ cīvaram utkṣiptaṃ | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha | tena hi saṃkakṣikā nāma kartavyā | bhagavatā dāni saṃkakṣikā anujñātā | bhikṣuṇīyo tathāgatān paṭān puṣpadaśān saṃkakṣikāṃ kurvanti | yāvat tena hi na kṣamati tathāgatān paṭān puṣpadaśān saṃkakṣikāṃ kartuṃ | yāvat tena hi prāmāṇikā kartavyā | yathāntarvāse tathaiva kartavyaṃ | yāvat tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 187. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Now, a certain <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> was attractive and beautiful. Her robe was lifted up by her full breasts. People laughed at her: 'Look, friends, how the female renunciant's robe is lifted up!' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. [Abbreviated.] Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said [that a shoulder cloth should be prescribed]...

body.text: saṃkakṣikāṃ bhikṣuṇīya kārāpayantīya prāmāṇikā kārāpayitavyā tatredaṃ pramāṇaṃ | dīrghaśo catvāri vitastiyo | sugatavitastinā | tiryag dve | tad uttariṃ kārāpeya cchedanapācattikaṃ | ṇka ||
body.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> having a shoulder cloth (<s>saṃkakṣikā</s>) made should have it made to the proper measure. The proper measure here is: in length, four spans by the <s>Sugata</s> span; in width, two [spans]. If she has it made exceeding [this measure], it is a <s>pācattika</s> requiring cutting [to size].

body.text: dakaśāṭikā
body.translated_text: The Bathing Cloth (<s>dakśāṭikā</s>)

body.text: 188. vaiśālyāṃ nidānaṃ | bhadrā dāni kāpileyī sarpiṇikāṃ nadīṃ snānāya gatā | cīvaran nikṣipitvā avatīrṇā snānāya | pañca licchavikumārāḥ tāye pratibaddhacittāḥ nadītīre sthitāḥ | bhadrāye aṅgayaṣṭiṃ paśyitukāmāḥ | sā dān āha dīrghāyuḥ gacchatha gacchatha yāvad aham uttarāmi | tā dān āhaṃsuḥ | nahi | āryāye vayam aṅgayaṣṭiṃ paśyitukāmāḥ | sā dān āha | dirghāyuḥ kim anena pūtikāyena navadvāreṇāśucipragharantena dṛṣṭena | prakramatha yāvad aham uttarāmi | te dān āhaṃsuḥ | nahi nahi | āryāye vayam aṅgayaṣṭiṃ paśyitukāmāḥ | te dāni yadā na gacchanti cirañ ca bhavati | sā dāni andho bālajano ti kṛtvā ekaṃ hastam agrato kṛtvā aparaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā uttīrṇā | te tāṃ vivasanāṃ dṛṣṭvā mūrcchitāḥ patitāḥ | uṣṇaṃ śoṇitam mukhād āgataṃ | kālagataṃ kālagatāḥ | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhikṣuṇīyo bhagavantam āhaṃsuḥ | paśya bhagavan katham iya pañca licchavikumārāḥ pratibaddhacittāḥ bhadrāyāṃ mūrcchitāḥ patitāḥ | bhagavān āha | naitarhi yeva ete bhadrāyāṃ pratibaddhacittāḥ mūrcchitāḥ patitāḥ | anyadāpy ete bhadrāyāṃ pratibaddhacittāḥ anyadāpi bhagavan anyadāpi bhikṣuṇīyo |
body.translated_text: 188. At <s>Vaiśālī</s> is the setting. <s>Bhadrā Kāpileyī</s> had gone to the river <s>Sarpiṇikā</s> to bathe. Having set aside her robes, she descended into [the water] to bathe. Five <s>Licchavi</s> youths, whose minds were attached to her, stood on the riverbank, wishing to see <s>Bhadrā</s>'s bodily form. She said: 'Long-lived ones, go away, go away, until I come out!' They said: 'No...'

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo atītam adhvānaṃ yāvat triṃśabhavane | anyatarasmiṃ bhavane bharaṇī nāma apsarā upapannā | prāsādikā darśanīyā atirivānyāsām apsarāṇāṃ abhibhūya bhāsate | atirivānyāsām apsarāṇāṃ abhibhūya bhāsate tapati virājate | tasyāḥ pañca devaputrāḥ pratibaddhacittāḥ | śakraś ca nāma devānām indraḥ | mātalisaṃgrāhako | jayo | vijayo | khāṇu devaputro pañcamaḥ | te dān āhaṃsuḥ | na tāvad eṣā śakyā asmābhiḥ pañcadhā kartuṃ | eṣa gāthāṃ kurmaḥ | yo 'tra sarvasuṣṭhu adhyavasito bhaviṣyati sa grahīṣyatīti |
body.translated_text: In the past, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, in a former time, up to [the heaven of] the Thirty-three [gods]. In a certain existence, an <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) named <s>Bharaṇī</s> was reborn. She was attractive, beautiful, surpassing and outshining the other <s>apsarases</s> in radiance, surpassing and outshining the other <s>apsarases</s> in brilliance and splendor. Five <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) had their minds attached to her. And <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods...

children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, spoke this verse:

children.text: utthito vā niṣaṇṇo vā āsane na labhate sukhaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'Whether standing or sitting, he finds no comfort on his seat;'

children.text: śayito ca sukhaṃ labhe yadā kāmā jahanti mā || [1] ||
children.translated_text: 'and he finds comfort in sleep — when desires abandon me.' [1]
<s>Mātali</s> the charioteer spoke this verse:

children.text: sukhaṃ tvam asi devendra yaṃ supto labhase sukhaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'You are happy, O lord of gods, [you] who find comfort in sleep;'

children.text: bheryā saṃgrāmaśīrṣe vā sadā kāmā hananti māṃ || [2] ||
children.translated_text: '[But] as if by drums on the battlefield, desires constantly strike me.' [2]
The <s>devaputra</s> <s>Jaya</s> spoke this verse:

children.text: bheryās tu hanyamānāyā bhaved vīcī muhur muhuḥ |
children.translated_text: 'When a drum is being struck, there arise waves again and again;'

children.text: kāṣṭhasrotā upapannaṃ vā sadā kāmā hananti me || [3] ||
children.translated_text: 'like a log carried by the current — desires constantly strike me.' [3]
The <s>devaputra</s> <s>Vijaya</s> spoke this verse:
'Of a log being carried, there arises an entanglement there;'
'like the eyes of a moth, my [eyes] are always wide open [with longing].' [4]
The <s>devaputra</s> <s>Khāṇu</s> spoke this verse:

children.text: sarve bhavanto sukhitā yeṣāṃ gāthā pratibhānti |
children.translated_text: 'All of you sirs are happy, to whom verses come spontaneously;'

children.text: ahaṃ khalu na jānāmi kiṃ jīvāmi marāmi vā || [5] ||
children.translated_text: 'I indeed do not know whether I am alive or dead.' [5]
Those <s>devaputras</s> said:

children.text: tvaṃ suṣṭhu adhyavasito tathaiva eṣā bharaṇī |
children.translated_text: 'You are the most resolute among us, and so too is this <s>Bharaṇī</s>;'
'let the goddess who is beautiful in all limbs be yours.' [6]

body.text: bhagavān āha | syād vo bhikṣuṇiyo yuṣmākam evam asyād anyā sā bharaṇī nāma apsarā abhūṣi | naitad evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ | eṣā sā bhadrā apsarā abhūṣi | anye te devaputrāḥ etad eva te pañca licchavikumārāḥ | tadāpy ete etāya pratibaddhacittāḥ | etarhy apy ete etāya pratibaddhacittāḥ | bhikṣuṇīyo āhaṃsuḥ | kasya bhagavan karmaṇo vipākena bhadrā prāsādikā darśanīyā mahākulīnā maheśākhyā mahābhogā kṣiprādhigamā ca | atha khalu bhagavān bhadrāṃ kāpileyīm āmantrayati | pratibhātu te bhadre bhikṣuṇīnām ātmopanāyikāṃ pūrvenivāsapratisaṃyuktāṃ kathāṃ | atha khalu bhadrā anekavidhaṃ pūrvenivāsam anusmarantī bhikṣuṇīyo āmantreti |
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You might think, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, that the <s>apsarā</s> named <s>Bharaṇī</s> was someone else. It should not be seen thus. It was this <s>Bhadrā</s> who was that <s>apsarā</s>. Those other <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods) were these very five <s>Licchavi</s> youths. Then too their minds were attached to her; now too their minds are attached to her.' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> said: 'By the ripening of what <s>karma</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is <s>Bhadrā</s> attractive, beautiful, of great family, of great renown, of great wealth, and quick in attainment?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Bhadrā Kāpileyī</s>: 'Let it occur to you, <s>Bhadrā</s>, to relate to the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> an account connected with your own former lives.' Then <s>Bhadrā</s>, recollecting her manifold former lives, addressed the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>:

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhaginyaḥ atītam adhvānaṃ nagaraṃ vārāṇasī kāśījanapado | tatra dāni strī abhūṣi daridrā | sā dāni anyatarāya śreṣṭhibhāryāya śabdāpitā keśān prasādhanāya | sā tāye śreṣṭhibhāryāye keśān prasādhayati |
body.translated_text: 'In the past, sisters, in a former time, the city was <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in the <s>Kāśī</s> country. There was a poor woman there. She was summoned by a certain merchant's wife to dress her hair. She was dressing the merchant wife's hair.'

body.text: buddhānāṃ bhagavatām anutpādāt pratyekabuddhā utpadyante |
body.translated_text: 'In the absence of <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) arise.'

body.text: atha śuṇṭhīka nāma pratyekabuddho piṇḍapātāya caranto tasmin gṛhe piṇḍāya praviṣṭo | pratyekabuddhas tūṣṇīm eva tiṣṭhati | na kocid ālāpiya deti | sā dāni strī tāṃ śreṣṭhibhāryāṃ āha | dehi etasya bhikṣāṃ | sā śreṣṭhibhāryā ūrdhvam avalokayitvā āha | kā imasyaivaṃ durvarṇasya alpeśākhyasya bhikṣān dāsyati | sā jalpati | na ete kāyaprāsādikā icchīyanti | cittaprāsādikā ete icchīyanti | sā dān āha | no tasya demi | sā dāni daridrā strī āha | āryadhīte dehi me yan mamādyabhaktaṃ tvayā dātavyam tam aham imasya dadāmi | tāya dāni ājñaptaṃ | yan tavādyabhaktaṃ prāpuṇati taṃ gṛhītvā udake prakṣipāhi etasya vā dehīti | tāya taṃ bhaktaṃ pratiladbhaṃ | hastasyaivaṃ kṛtvā prasādena tasya pratyekabuddhasya dattaṃ | sa pratyekabuddhas vata eva vaihāyase prakrāntaḥ | sā dāni dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanā gṛhaṃ praviṣṭā | śreṣṭhinā ca dṛṣṭo gṛhāto ṛṣī vaihāyasena prakrānto | tataḥ śreṣṭhi gṛhaṃ praviṣṭo pṛcchati | kocid iha ṛṣiḥ praviṣṭaḥ | āha | praviṣṭo | āha | kiñcit tasya dattaṃ | āha | nahi | imāya daridrastriyāya dattaṃ śreṣṭhī utkaṇṭhito īdṛśo dakṣiṇīyo mama gṛhaṃ praviṣṭo na ca saṃmānito | so dāni śreṣṭhī tāṃ striyam āha | dehi me etaṃ puṇyaṃ yaṃ tvayā adya sañcitaṃ | dadāmi te prabhūtaṃ hiraṇyaṃ suvarṇaṃ | sā dān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Then a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> named <s>Śuṇṭhīka</s>, going on his alms-round, entered that house for alms. The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stood in silence. No one spoke to him or gave [anything]. Then that poor woman said to the merchant's wife: "Give to this mendicant!"'

body.text: kṣīyati sarvaṃ dhanadhānyaṃ jātarūpaṃ rajataṃ ca |

children.text: na kṣīyante puṇyephalaṃ dattaṃ munīnāṃ sarvathā | [7] ||
children.translated_text: But the fruit of merit given to sages is never exhausted in any way. [7]

body.translated_text: All wealth, grain, gold, and silver are exhausted,

body.text: yad aham evaṃ daridrā para vaktavyā anyathā |

children.translated_text: It is from not seeing such [holy ones] and from not sharing wealth. [8]

children.text: durvarṇatāya mucye haṃ avaikalyatā ca bhogehi |
children.translated_text: May I be freed from ill-complexion and from deficiency in wealth;
May I not live on what others give, dependent on others' families. [9]

body.translated_text: That I am thus poor and dependent on others' words [is] otherwise [explained]:

body.text: evaṃ caṅkrameyaṃ na bhe yathā caṅkramase vīra |

children.translated_text: May I thus be free from passion, released from the bonds of existence. [10]

body.translated_text: May I walk in meditation just as you walk, O hero;

body.text: pāratrikaṃ sunihitaṃ avaikalyatā hṛṣṭā |

children.text: bhavāmi muditā [ḥ ḥ] dattvā ṛṣisya āhāraṃ | [11] ||
children.translated_text: I shall be delighted, having given food to the sage. [11]

body.translated_text: With a well-established crossing to the other shore, complete, and joyful,

body.text:
ito cyavitvā upapadyiṣyaṃ nandane ramye
tatra pravicāriṣyaṃ devagaṇasamākule | ||
body.translated_text: Having passed away from here, I shall be reborn in the delightful <s>Nandana</s> [grove], and there I shall wander about, surrounded by hosts of gods.

body.text: bhaktaṃ samaye dānaṃ dattaṃ mayā

children.translated_text: To one well-established, for the abandonment of suffering. [12]

body.translated_text: Food given in due season, a gift given by me

body.text: atha śreṣṭhinā sā bhāryā avasāditā | sā daridrā strī bhaṭṭārikā sthāpitā |
body.translated_text: Then the merchant dismissed that wife. The poor woman was established as the chief wife.

body.text:
syād vo bhaginyaḥ anyā sā daridrā strī naitad evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ | aham eva sā daridrā strī | yaṃ so mayā pratyekabuddho piṇḍapātena pratimānito prasannacittāya tasya karmaṇo vipākenāhaṃ prāsādikā | peyālaṃ | api tu bhaginyaḥ naitad evaṃ mayā kuśalamūlam avaropitaṃ yenāhaṃ prāsādikā darśanīyā | kṣiprādhigamā ca | anyadā pi mayā kuśalamūlaṃ avaropitaṃ |
189. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhaginyo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasīyaṃ nagare kāyaci striyāya lohacakraṃ paṭalake kṛtvā puṣpehi okiritvā kāśikena vastreṇa praticchādeyitvā bhagavato kāśyapasya dattaṃ | dattvā ca praṇidhānam akārṣīt | rathasya cakraṃ sanābhinemikaṃ vastrottamena praticchādayitvā ye munivarasākṣikṛtā hi dharmā aham api taṃ sākṣikaromi dharmaṃ | sā dāni kenacit kāryeṇa aparādhinī svāminā avasāditā | sā dāni utkaṇṭhitā | āha | dhig astu strībhāvaḥ | paribhūto mātṛgrāmaḥ | gacchāmi udbandhiṣyaṃ | sā rajjum ādāya nirgatā | tatra ca nātidūre bhagavato kāśyapasya stūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasādajātā | alaṅkāravibhūṣitā kāśikavastraprāvṛtā candānuliptagātrā sā cintayati | ahaṃ mariṣyaṃ | bhagavato kāśyapasya stūpe pūjāṃ kariṣyaṃ | sā prasannacittā tāni alaṅkārāṇi muñcitvā stūpe avakiritvā kāśikena vastreṇācchādayitvā candanenānulimpitvā praṇidhānaṃ akārṣīt | anāgate 'dhvani evamvidhaṃ śāstāram ārāgīyeyaṃ | sa ca me dharman deśeya tasyāhaṃ dharman deśitam ājāneyan ti | sā tahim udbandhitvā kālagatā | tāvattriṃśabhavane upapannā | apsarasahasraparivṛtā sā tahiṃ yāvadāyuḥ sthitvā tataś cyavitvā manuṣyeṣūpapannāḥ | vaiśalīyaṃ kāpilasya gotrasya brāhmaṇakule upapannā | tāye dāni jñātikehi bhadreti nāma kṛtaṃ | anarthikā kāmaguṇehi pañcahi yā niṣkramitvā pravrajitā sarvāsravakṣayam akārṣīt | kāśikāni vastrāṇi pratyagraṃ cānulepanaṃ bhagavato kāśyapasya yā prasannābhiropayet | sā kāpileyī bhagavato pādāṃ vandati śāstuno | yāvad bhagavān āha | tena hi dakaśāṭikā nāma kartavyā | bhikṣuṇīyo āhaṃsuḥ | paśya bhagavan katham iyaṃ bhadrā sthaviramahākāśyapena sārdhaṃ pravrajitā | bhagavān āha | na etarhi yeva ete ubhaye pravrajitā | anyadāpy ete ubhaye pravrajitāḥ | anyadāpi bhagavan anyadāpi bhikṣuṇīyo |
body.translated_text: 'You might think, sisters, that the poor woman was someone else. It should not be seen thus. I myself was that poor woman. Because I honored that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> with alms-food with a serene mind, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> I am attractive...' abbreviated.

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo atītam adhvānaṃ catvāro rājaṛṣayaḥ kumbhakārakule vāsam upagatāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'In the past, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, in a former time, four royal sages (<s>rājaṛṣis</s>) took lodging in a potter's house.'

children.translated_text: <s>Khāṇuvarṇa</s> of the <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, and <s>Bhārgava</s> of the <s>Gandhāras</s>,

children.text: nimī rājā videhānāṃ ugrasenaś ca kṣatriyaḥ || [13] ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Nimi</s> of the <s>Videhas</s>, and <s>Ugrasena</s> the <s>Kṣatriya</s>. [13]

body.text: ete catvāro rājaṛṣayaḥ ugratejā mahābalā kumbhakārakule vāsa ekarātram upāgamat | kumbhakāram upasamkramya tān eva paripṛcchati | kiṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutvā vā pravrajyām ārocatha |
body.translated_text: These four royal sages, of fierce splendor and great power, came to stay one night in the potter's house. Approaching the potter, he questioned them: 'Having seen or heard what did you declare your renunciation?'

children.translated_text: The great king <s>Khāṇuvarṇa</s>, bull among men of the <s>Kaliṅgas</s>,
When questioned by the potter, spoke this word: [14]

body.text:
śaṅkhāṃ suvarṇottaraniṣṭhitān nāri |
pinandhana pinandhati

children.text: śabda dvitīyā tu samāgatā yato ramāgatā yato
children.translated_text: Accompanied by sound, she came; she came having delighted—
Having seen and heard the fault of attachment,
I practice the life of a mendicant. [15]

body.translated_text: A woman adorning herself with golden shell-ornaments,

children.translated_text: The great king <s>Bhārgava</s> too, bull among men of the <s>Gandhāras</s>,
When questioned by the potter, spoke this word: [16]
Birds, for the sake of a corpse—
Over a single one, many fall upon [it];
For the sake of food they run about—
Having seen that, I practice the life of a mendicant. [17]
King <s>Nimi</s> too, the great king of <s>Videha</s>, lord of <s>Mithilā</s>,
When questioned by the potter, spoke this word: [18]
I saw [a tree] of cloud-like color,
With limbs smeared [with oil] like lamp-wicks,
That very [tree], broken and fallen for the sake of fruit—
Having seen that, stirred with <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency), I practice the life of a mendicant. [19]
King <s>Ugrasena</s> too, bull among men of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,
When questioned by the potter, spoke this word: [20]
A bull, in the midst of such splendor,
Endowed with a body of trembling hump and fine color—
I saw him broken for the sake of desire;
Having seen him broken, I practice the life of a mendicant. [21]
All these, god-like, have assembled,
Like a fire blazing in the night.
I too shall go forth...
Abandoning pleasures that delight the mind. [22]

body.text: kumbhakārabhāryā kathayati |

children.text: ayam eva kālo nahi anyad asti |
children.translated_text: This alone is the time; there is nothing else.
There is no instructor beyond this.
I too shall go forth—
But where will my little children go? [23]

body.translated_text: The potter's wife speaks:

children.text: āmaṃ pakvan na jānanti atha loṇam aloṇakaṃ |
children.translated_text: They do not know raw from cooked, nor salted from unsalted;
Like a bird released from a man's hand,
[They are] fledglings with unformed wings, young children, unknowing. [24]

body.text: pravrajitam anupravrajāmi

children.translated_text: I shall follow the one who wanders. [25]

body.translated_text: I shall follow the one who has gone forth;

children.text: nimī rājā bodhisattvaḥ kaliṅga pi śārisutaḥ |
children.translated_text: King <s>Nimi</s> was the <s>Bodhisattva</s>; <s>Kaliṅga</s> was <s>Śāriputra</s>;

children.text: ugrasenaś ca maudgalyo ānando āsi bhārgavo |
children.translated_text: <s>Ugrasena</s> was <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>; <s>Ānanda</s> was <s>Bhārgava</s>;

children.text: kumbhakāraḥ kāśyapo āsi bhadrā sā kumbhakārikā || [26] ||
children.translated_text: The potter was <s>Kāśyapa</s>; <s>Bhadrā</s> was the potter's wife. [26]
Then too both [men and women] went forth;
Now too both have gone forth. [27]

body.text: bhagavatā dāni bhikṣuṇīnām udakaśāṭikā anujñātā | bhikṣuṇīyo dāni tathāgatān paṭān dakaśāṭikāṃ kurvanti | bhagavān āha | tena hi na kṣamati yathāgataṃ paṭaṃ dakaśāṭikāṃ kartuṃ | yāvac chikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ |
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Bhagavān</s> had permitted a bathing cloth (<s>udakaśāṭikā</s>) for <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> then made bathing cloths from newly obtained cloth. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, it is not permissible to make a bathing cloth from newly obtained cloth.' Up to: the training rule was laid down.

body.text: dakeśāṭikāṃ bhikṣuṇīya kārāpayantīya prāmāṇikā kārāpayitavyā | tatredaṃ pramāṇan | dīrghaśo catvāri vitastiyo | sugatavitastinā | tiryag dve tad uttariṃ kārāpaye cchedanapācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: When a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> has a bathing cloth made, it should be made to the standard measure. The measure here is: four hand-spans in length, by the <s>Sugata</s> hand-span; two in width. If she has one made exceeding that—it is a <s>chedanapācattika</s> (cutting and expiation).

body.text: dakaśāṭikā ti yā sā bhagavatā anujñātā | kārāpayantīye ti svayaṃ kuryāt pareṇa vā kārāpaye | prāmāṇikan ti tatredaṃ pramāṇaṃ catvāri vitastiyo | sugatavitastinā ti sugato nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho tasya yo vitasti so dvy ardho mañcakapādo tiryag dve tad uttariṃ kārāpaye pācattikaṃ | atha dāni ekānte nikuñje pradeśe snāyanti vinā dakaśāṭikāya anāpattiḥ | bhikṣur api vinā dakaśāṭikāya snāyati vinayātikramam āsādayati | atha nikuñjapradeśe snāyati vinā dakaśāṭikāya anāpattiḥ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Bathing cloth' means that which was permitted by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. 'Having it made' means she makes it herself or has another make it. 'To the standard measure' means the measure here is four hand-spans. 'By the <s>Sugata</s> hand-span' means the <s>Sugata</s> is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One...

body.text: dakaśāṭikāṃ bhikṣuṇīya kārāpayantīya prāmāṇikā kārāpayitavyā | tatredaṃ pramāṇaṃ | dīrghaśo catvāri vitastiyo | sugatavitastinā | tiryag dve | tad uttarim kārāpaye cchedanapācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: When a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> has a bathing cloth made, it should be made to the standard measure. The measure here is: four hand-spans in length, by the <s>Sugata</s> hand-span; two in width. If she has one made exceeding that—it is a <s>chedanapācattika</s> (cutting and expiation).

body.text: pācattikadharma 76
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> (Expiation) rule 76.

body.text: kaṭhina
body.translated_text: <s>Kaṭhina</s> (robe-cloth).

body.text: 190. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | sthūlanandā nāma bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṇīsaṃghena adhyeṣṭā | śakyasi ārye saṃghasya kṛtena paṭān yācituṃ | sā dān āha | śakyaṃ | sā dāni durbalakuleṣu gatvā āha | mahāpuṇyo śakyasi saṃghasya paṭaṃ dātuṃ | āhaṃsuḥ | ārye ājñāsyāmaḥ punar apy āgamiṣyasi | sā punaḥ punar āgacchati | āhaṃsuḥ | jñāsyāmaḥ jñāsyāma iti | sā dāni jalpati | yadi yūyaṃ dātukāmā dadatha | ayaṃ saṃghasya cīvarakālo atikramati | kiṃ jñāsyāma iti vadatha | tehi dāni na dattaṃ | cīvarakālo 'tikrānto | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ yāvad bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 190. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Sthūlanandā</s> was requested by the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Saṃgha</s>: 'Noble One, can you solicit cloth for the <s>Saṃgha</s> from what has been done [i.e., from donors]?' She said: 'I can.' She then went to weak [i.e., poor] families and said: 'O meritorious one, can you give cloth to the <s>Saṃgha</s>?' They said: 'Noble One, we shall see. Come again.' She came again and again. They said: 'We shall see, we shall see.' She then said: 'If you wish to give, then give! The <s>Saṃgha</s>'s robe-season is passing. Why do you keep saying "we shall see"?' They did not give. The robe-season passed. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> — up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī durbalāya cīvarapratyāśāya saṃghasya kaṭhināstāraṃ vyatināmayet pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should let the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s <s>kaṭhina</s> (robe-ceremony) spreading lapse due to a weak expectation of robes — it is a <s>pācattika</s> (confession offense).

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | durbalāyeti apratibalāya | cīvarapratyāśāyeti cīvaraṃ nāma kālaṃ yāvat kṣaumunikā | saṃghasya kaṭhināstārikaṃ | vyatināmayed iti atikrāmayet pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | eṣā dāni bhikṣuṇī utsāhīyati | ārye śakṣyasi saṃghasya kaṭhinaṃ yācituṃ | yadi pratibalā bhavati utsahitavyaṃ | utsahitvā na durbalakulāni yācitavyāni | atha khalu ye pratibalāḥ pitā putrā vā bhrātarau vā bhaginīyo vā jñātisambandhā vā gotrasambandhā vā te yācitavyā | te pratibalā dātuṃ te yācitvārocayitavyāḥ | atha dān āhaṃsuḥ jñāsyāma jñāsyāma iti vaktavyā | detha vā pratyākhyātha vā cīvarakālo 'tikramati | atha dāni apratibalā bhavati utsāhayitavyā sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī saṃghasya kaṭhinavivarārthāya | utsahayitvā naiva yācati naiva yāvayeti na bhikṣuṇīsaṃghasyārocayati na labhyatīti pācattikam āsādayati | phu | bhikṣur api durbalāya cīvarapratyāśāya saṃghasya kaṭhināstāraṃ vyatināmayeti vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Due to a weak [expectation]' means due to an incapable [source]. 'Expectation of robes' means robes — up to linen cloth. 'The <s>Saṃgha</s>'s <s>kaṭhina</s> spreading.' 'Should let lapse' means should allow to pass — it is a <s>pācattika</s> — up to the rule establishment. That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> is encouraged: 'Noble One, will you be able to solicit the <s>kaṭhina</s> for the <s>Saṃgha</s>?' If she is capable, she should undertake it. Having undertaken it, she should not solicit from weak [poor] families. Rather, those who are capable — a father, sons, brothers, sisters, kinship relations, or clan relations — those should be solicited. Those who are capable of giving, having been solicited, should be informed. If they then say 'we shall see, we shall see,' she should tell them: 'Either give or refuse — the robe-season is passing!' If she is incapable, that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should be encouraged for the purpose of opening the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s <s>kaṭhina</s>. Having been encouraged, if she neither solicits nor arranges nor informs the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Saṃgha</s> that [robes] are not obtainable — she incurs a <s>pācattika</s>. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too who lets the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s <s>kaṭhina</s> spreading lapse due to a weak expectation of robes incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s> (disciplinary transgression). Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī durbalāya cīvarapratyāśāya saṃghasya kaṭhināstāraṃ vyatināmayet pācattikaṃ | phu ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should let the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s <s>kaṭhina</s> spreading lapse due to a weak expectation of robes — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 77
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 77.

body.text: cīvarapārihārikaṃ
body.translated_text: The reserve robe (<s>cīvarapārihārika</s>).

body.text: 191. bhagavān śrāvastīyaṃ viharati | tā dāni bhikṣuṇīyo sāntararottareṇa prāvṛtā bhagavato pādavandikā āgatā tāsāṃ nirgatānāṃ agnidāha utpannaḥ | tāsāṃ dagdhāni cīvarāṇi | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | peyālaṃ | yāvad āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha | etaṃ va ta dāni yūyaṃ pārihārikaṃ cīvaraṃ na pariharatha | tena hi pārihārikaṃ cīvaraṃ pariharitavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: 191. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, wrapped in their inner and outer robes, came to pay respect at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. After they had departed, a fire broke out. Their robes were burned. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> — abbreviated — up to: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is it because you do not carry your reserve robe? Therefore, a reserve robe should be carried.'

body.text: eṣā yevārthotpattiḥ | bhagavān śrāvastīyaṃ viharati | tā dāni bhikṣuṇīyo śākīyakanyāyo ca mallakanyāyo ca kolitakanyāyo ca sukumārapravrajitā ca | bhārikāṃ saṃghāṭiṃ pariharantīyo kilamyantī | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha | tena hi anujānāmi glānāye | atha khalu bhagavān mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm āmantrayati | sannipātaya gautami | peyālaṃ | yāvat |
body.translated_text: This itself is the origin-story. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> — <s>Śākya</s> maidens, <s>Malla</s> maidens, <s>Kolita</s> maidens, and those who had gone forth from a delicate upbringing — were becoming fatigued carrying the heavy patchwork robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>). The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> — abbreviated — up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, I grant an exemption for one who is ill.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>: 'Assemble [the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>], <s>Gautamī</s>' — abbreviated — up to:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī agilānā pārihārikaṃ cīvaraṃ na pariharati pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, when not ill, does not carry her reserve robe — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | pārihārikaṃ cīvaran ti saṃghāṭī yāvat dakaśāṭikā | pariharatīti yena gaccheya tahiṃ netavyā | agilānā ti pratyuddhṛtaṃ padaṃ bhagavatā anāpattiḥ gilānāya | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī agilānā pārihārikaṃ cīvaraṃ na pariharati pācattikam āsādayati | atha dāni cetiyaṃ vandati caṅkramati vā anto sīmam vā gacchati anāpattiḥ | bhikṣur api pārihārikaṃ cīvaraṃ na pariharati vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Reserve robe' means the patchwork robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>) up to the bathing cloth (<s>dakaśāṭikā</s>). 'Should carry' means wherever she goes, she should take it with her. 'When not ill' — this is the exemption laid down by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: there is no offense for one who is ill. That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, when not ill, who does not carry her reserve robe incurs a <s>pācattika</s>. However, if she goes to worship at a shrine, or goes on a walking meditation, or goes within the boundary (<s>sīmā</s>) — there is no offense. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too who does not carry his reserve robe incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s>. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī agilānā pārihārikaṃ cīvaraṃ na pariharati pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, when not ill, does not carry her reserve robe — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 78
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 78.

body.text: pacati
body.translated_text: Cooking.

body.text: 192. bhagavān vaiśālīyaṃ viharati | bhadrāye dāni kāpileyīye jñātikulāto devasikaṃ bhaktam ānīyati | sā taṃ vihārake pacitvā khādati | tāye dāni putrabhrātṛkā āgatāḥ | bhadrāye avalokanāya gatāḥ | sānyeṣām āha bhuñjiṣyatha | te dān āhaṃsuḥ bhuñjiṣyaṃ | tāye tato dinnaṃ | āha | mṛṣṭaṃ khalv imaṃ | kuto imaṃ | sā dān āha | yuṣmākaṃ gṛhāto ānītaṃ | āhaṃsuḥ | asmākaṃ gṛhe na evaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ pacyati | āha | kiṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhadrāyiṇīyo ceṭiyo jāniṣyanti | kathaṃ paritavyan ti | evam evopakaraṇāni asphātikā kurvanti | te dāni gṛhaṃ gatvā tā dāsīyo daṇḍakaśāhatāyo kṛtāyo | itikitikāye dhītaro evam ettakam upakaraṇaṃ dadāmo yūyam asphātikaṃ karotha | tā rodamānā āhaṃsuḥ | āryadhītā asmākaṃ hanāyeti | bhikṣuṇīhi śrutaṃ | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtaṃ te bhadre | tena hi na kṣamati parāhṛtaṃ khādanīyam vā bhojanīyam vā pacitum vā pacāyitum vā bhṛjjitum vā bhṛjjāpayitum vā |
body.translated_text: 192. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s>. Now for <s>Bhadrā Kāpileyī</s>, food was brought daily from her family's household. She would cook it in the monastery and eat it. One day her brother's children came. They went to visit <s>Bhadrā</s>. She offered them [food], saying: 'Will you eat?' They said: 'We will eat.' She gave them some. They said: 'This is indeed rich! Where did this come from?' She said: 'It was brought from your household.' They said: 'In our household, such rich [food] is not cooked!' She said: 'Do your good women servants know how to cook properly?' — thus [implying they were incompetent]. They then went home and beat those servant women with sticks and whips, [saying]: 'Daughters of wretchedness! We give this much provisions and you make inferior [food]!' The [servants], weeping, said: 'It is the noble lady's daughters [i.e., the nuns] who are causing us trouble!' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> heard of it. This matter — abbreviated — up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>Bhadrā</s>. Therefore it is not proper to cook or have cooked, to fry or have fried, food brought from outside — whether edible or provisions.'

body.text: eṣā evārthotpattiḥ | bhagavāṃ cchrāvastīyam viharati | tā dāni bhikṣuṇīyo śākiyakanyāyo ca kolitakanyāyo ca piṇḍāya carantīyo | paryupāsitaṃ bhojanaṃ labhanti | paryupāsitaṃ odanam | paryupāsitaṃ sūpaṃ | paryupāsitaṃ śākaṃ | paryupāsitaṃ kulmāṣaṃ | tāyo bhuktvā bhuktvā vamanti | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | peyālaṃ | yāvat labhyaṃ bhagavan bhikṣuṇīya tūṣṇīṃ kṛtvā bhoktuṃ | bhagavān āha labhyaṃ | atha khalu bhagavān mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm āmantrayati | yāvat paryavadātāni bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: This itself is the origin-story. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> — <s>Śākya</s> maidens, <s>Kolita</s> maidens — while going on their alms-round, would receive stale food: stale rice, stale soup, stale vegetables, stale porridge. Having eaten this repeatedly, they would vomit. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> — abbreviated — up to: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, is it permissible for a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> to eat silently [without protest]?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It is permissible.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> — up to: 'so that [the rules] will be made clear.'

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī parāhṛtaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyam vā puno puno pacitvā vā pacāpetvā vā bhṛjjitvā vā bhṛjjāpetvā vā kaṭhitvā vā kaṭhāpetvā vā agilānā khādaye vā bhuñjeya vā pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, when not ill, should eat or consume food — whether edible or provisions — brought from outside, having cooked it again or had it cooked, having fried it or had it fried, having toasted it or had it toasted — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti | peyālaṃ | parāhṛtan ti grāmato vā ānītaṃ nagarato vā ānītaṃ | khādanīyan ti khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyan ti bhojanīyaṃ | pacitvā ti svayaṃ | pacāpayitvā ti parehi | bhṛjjitvā ti svayaṃ | bhṛjjāpayitvā ti parehi | kaṭhitvā ti svayaṃ | kaṭhāpayitvā ti parehi | agilānā ti pratyuddhṛtaṃ bhagavatā padaṃ anāpattir gilānāye | kin dāni atra gailānyam abhipretaṃ | jarādurbalā vā bhoti vyādhidurbalā vā bhuktvā vā vamati | aphāsuṃ vā bhoti idam atra gailānyam abhipretaṃ | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī rasagṛdhyā parāhṛtaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ puno puno paceya vā pacāpeya vā pācāttikam āsādayati | atha dāni śītalam bhavati labhyā uṣṇīkartuṃ | na dāni thālikāya vā piṭharikāya vā | atha khalu tāmrapātreṇa vā kupātreṇa vā kāṃsikāya vā uṣṇīkartavyaṃ | bhikṣur api svayaṃ pacati vinayātikramam āsādayati | atha dāni kalpiyakāreṇa pacāpeti anāpattiḥ | atha dāni śītalo bhavati piṇḍapāto uṣṇīkaroti anāpattiḥ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' — abbreviated. 'Brought from outside' means brought from a village or brought from a city. 'Edible' means edible food. 'Provisions' means provisions. 'Having cooked' means [done] by herself. 'Having had [it] cooked' means by others. 'Having fried' means by herself. 'Having had [it] fried' means by others. 'Having toasted' means by herself. 'Having had [it] toasted' means by others. 'When not ill' — this is the exemption laid down by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: there is no offense for one who is ill. What illness is intended here? Being weak from old age, or weak from disease, or [one who] vomits after eating, or [one who] feels unwell — this is the illness intended here. That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, out of greed for flavor, if she cooks or has cooked the alms-food brought from outside again and again — she incurs a <s>pācattika</s>. However, if [the food] is cold, it is permissible to heat it — but not in a pot (<s>thālikā</s>) or a cauldron (<s>piṭharikā</s>). Rather, it should be heated in a copper vessel, an earthen vessel, or a bronze vessel. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too, if he cooks by himself, incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s>. But if he has it cooked by a proper attendant (<s>kalpiyakāra</s>), there is no offense. If the alms-food is cold and he heats it, there is no offense. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī parāhṛtaṃ khādanīyam vā bhojanīyam va puno pacitvā vā pacāpetva vā bhṛjjitvā vā bhṛjjāpayitvā vā kaṭhitvā vā kaṭhāpayitvā vā agilānā khādeya vā bhuñjeya vā pācattikaṃ | hrā ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, when not ill, should eat or consume food — whether edible or provisions — brought from outside, having cooked it or had it cooked, having fried it or had it fried, having toasted it or had it toasted — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 79
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 79.

body.text: dakavijanena
body.translated_text: With water and a fan (<s>dakavījana</s>).

body.text: 193. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | gartodaro ca gartodaramātā ca gartodarapitā ca agārasyānagāriyaṃ pravrajitāḥ | gartodarapitā ca gartodaramātā ca śākyehi pravrajitā gartodara tirthakeṣu | gatodarapitā bhuñjati gartodaramātā vījayantī agrato tiṣṭhati pānīyamallakaṃ dhāreti | so dāni tāye kānicit kānicit pūrvacaritāni jalpati | yāni tāye amanaāpāni | tāya tasya pānīyamallakaṃ mastake āpiṭṭitaṃ | vījanadaṇḍena ca mastake āhato | akhallamahallaakuśalaaprakṛtijñaḥ | adyāpi tvaṃ ajalpitavyāni jalpasi | sā bhikṣuṇīhi dṛṣṭā | tā dān āhaṃsuḥ | mā ārye evaṃ karohi | agrapariṣā eṣā na labhyā evaṃ kartuṃ | sā dān āha | ayaṃ khalu akhalla akuśalo aprakṛtijño adyāpi yāni tāni ajalpitavyāni jalpati | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | yāvad bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtaṃ te gartodaramāte | naiṣa dharmo naiṣa vinayo | evaṃ ca dāni bhikṣuṃ bhuñjantaṃ dakavījanena upasthihasi | tena hi na kṣamati dakavījanena upasthihituṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 193. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. <s>Gartodara</s>, <s>Gartodara</s>'s mother, and <s>Gartodara</s>'s father had all gone forth from the household life to the homeless life. <s>Gartodara</s>'s father and <s>Gartodara</s>'s mother were ordained among the <s>Śākyas</s>; <s>Gartodara</s> [was ordained] among the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist ascetics). <s>Gartodara</s>'s father was eating while <s>Gartodara</s>'s mother stood before him fanning him, holding a water-bowl. He then began telling her certain past events — things disagreeable to her. She then struck the water-bowl on his head and hit his head with the fan-handle. 'Ignorant, foolish, unskilled one, not knowing proper conduct! Even now you speak of things not to be spoken of!' She was seen by the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. They said: 'Do not act thus, Noble One! This is the foremost assembly — it is not proper to act in such a way.' She said: 'This ignorant, unskilled one, not knowing proper conduct, even now speaks of things that should not be spoken of!' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> — up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, mother of <s>Gartodara</s>. This is not the <s>Dharma</s>, this is not the <s>Vinaya</s>. And now you attend upon a <s>bhikṣu</s> while he eats, with water and a fan! Therefore it is not proper to attend [upon a <s>bhikṣu</s> while eating] with water and a fan.' Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṃ bhuñjantaṃ dakavījanena upasthiheya pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should attend upon a <s>bhikṣu</s> while he eats with water and a fan — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | peyālaṃ | bhikṣun ti upasampannaṃ | pe | bhuñjantaṃ ti pañcajātakam vā pañcajātakasaṃsṛṣtam vā yad vā kiñcit khādyaṃ bhojyaṃ | dakavījanena upasthiheyā ti pānīyamallakaṃ dhārayet | vījanavātam vā dadyāt pācattikaṃ | yāvatprajñaptiḥ | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī udakamallakan dhārayati nīvījanaṃ vinayātikramam āsādayati | vījayati na udakamallakan dhāreti vinayātikramam āsādayati | ubhayaṃ karoti pācattikaṃ | nobhayaṃ anāpattiḥ | sā eṣā āpattiḥ ekasya bhikṣusya ekabhikṣuṇīye | atha dāni saṃbahulā bhikṣū bhavanti anāpattiḥ | atha dāni bhikṣuṇīye pitā vā bhrātā vā bhikṣur bhavati kiñcāpi vījayaty anāpattiḥ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained — abbreviated. '<s>Bhikṣu</s>' means one who is fully ordained — abbreviated. 'While he eats' means [eating] the five kinds of staple food, or food mixed with the five kinds, or whatever is edible or provisions. 'Should attend with water and a fan' means should hold the water-bowl, or should give fanning air — it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to the rule establishment. That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, if she holds the water-bowl but does not fan — she incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s>. If she fans but does not hold the water-bowl — she incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s>. If she does both — it is a <s>pācattika</s>. If she does neither — there is no offense. This offense [applies when] one <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> [attends] one <s>bhikṣu</s>. But if there are several <s>bhikṣus</s> — there is no offense. If the <s>bhikṣu</s> is the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>'s father or brother, even if she fans him — there is no offense. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṃ bhuñjantaṃ dakavījanena upasthiheya pācattikaṃ || 0 ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should attend upon a <s>bhikṣu</s> while he eats with water and a fan — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 80
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 80.

body.text: laśunañ ca khādati
body.translated_text: Eating garlic.

body.text: 194. bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati | meghīyo nāma laśunavāṇijako | tena bhikṣuṇīsaṃgho laśunena upanimantrito | tā dāni ṣaḍvargiṇīyo khādanti pi mardenti pi ujjhenti pi viśrāṇenti pi ādāya pi gacchanti | so dāni kadācit vāṭaṃ pratyavekṣituṅ gataḥ | tena dāni so dṛṣṭo vāṭo vidhvasto | so dān āha | kenāyaṃ vāṭo vidhvasto | āha tvayā āryamiśrikā upanimantritāḥ | laśunena tāyo dāni khādanti mardenti pi ujjhenti pi viśrāṇenti pi ādāya pi gacchanti | tasya dāni aprasādo jāto | āha | yadi khādanti kim mardenti | peyālaṃ | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | yāvad bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 194. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>. A garlic merchant named <s>Meghīya</s> had invited the <s>bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha</s> [to a meal] with garlic. Now the group-of-six [nuns] ate it, crushed it, discarded it, gave it away, and took it with them. Once he went to inspect his garden. He saw the garden devastated. He said: 'Who has devastated this garden?' It was said: 'You, sir, invited the noble sisters with garlic. They eat it, crush it, discard it, give it away, and take it with them.' He became displeased. He said: 'If they eat it, why do they crush it?'—abbreviation. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī laśunaṃ khādeya pācattikaṃ || laśunan ti laśunaṃ nāma jātimaṃ sevimaṃ nāgaraṃ kaccharuhaṃ pārvateyaṃ brahmadeyaṃ āvarantakaṃ māgadhakaṃ kosalakaṃ | yaṃ cā punar anya pi kiñcil laśunaṃ sarvaṃ laśunaṃ na kṣamati | āman na kṣamati pakvan na kṣamati | yakṛn na kṣamati | kāpi kāpi na kṣamati abhyantaraparibhogāya |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> eats garlic—it is a <s>pācattika</s> (expiation). 'Garlic' means garlic of the following kinds: cultivated, wild, urban, marsh-grown, mountain, brahmin-gift, <s>Āvarantaka</s>, <s>Māgadhaka</s>, and <s>Kosalaka</s>. And whatever else is any kind of garlic—all garlic is not permissible. Raw is not permissible; cooked is not permissible. The juice is not permissible. In any and every form it is not permissible for internal consumption.

body.text: atha dāni bhikṣuṇīya gaṇḍam vā piṭakam vā kṣatam vā upahatam vā bhavati labhyan taṃ mrakṣituṃ | mrakṣayitvā na kṣamati abhyāgame pradeśe sthātuṃ | atha khu pratigupte pradeśe sthātavyaṃ yāvad varttā bhavati | +++++ dhoviya niṣkramitavyaṃ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: Now, if a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> has a boil, an abscess, a wound, or an injury, she may apply it as an ointment. Having applied it, she should not stand in a public area but should stay in a secluded place while the treatment lasts. [After treatment] she should wash [it off] and then come out. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī laśunaṃ khādeya pācattikaṃ || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> eats garlic—it is a <s>pācattika</s>. [1]

body.text: pācattikadharma 81
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 81

body.text: deti
body.translated_text: Giving [food]

body.text: 195. bhagavān śrāvastīyaṃ viharati | rāṣṭrapālāya bhikṣuṇīya bhaginī kālagatā | sā dāni tāsāṃ bhāgineyakānāṃ nānāprakāraṃ khajjaṃ bhojjaṃ bhakṣayitvā deti | jano dāni ojjhāyati | paśyatha bhaṇe śramaṇikā śraddhādeyaṃ gṛhiṇān dadāti | etam prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | yāvac chabdāpayatha rāṣtrapālāṃ | sā dāni śabdāpitā | tad eva sarvaṃ bhagavān vistareṇa pṛcchati | āha | ām bhagavan | bhagavān āha | tena hi na kṣamati āgārikasya svahastaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ dātuṃ |
body.translated_text: 195. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The sister of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Rāṣṭrapālā</s> had died. She would prepare various hard and soft foods and give them to those nephews [of her sister]. People were displeased: 'Look, these female ascetics give away what was donated in faith by householders!' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. Up to: 'Summon <s>Rāṣṭrapālā</s>.' She was summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> questioned her about everything in detail. She said: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, it is not permissible to give hard or soft food with one's own hand to a householder.'

body.text: eṣā evārthotpattiḥ | gartodaro ca gartodarapitā ca gartodaramātā ca agārasyānagāriyaṃ pravrajitā | gartodarapitā gartodaramātā ca śākyehi pravrajitāḥ | gartodara tīrthikehi pravrajitaḥ | yāvat sa gartodaramātuḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrānto tāya gartodaramātāya tasya nānāprakārasya khajjakasya pūraṃ pātraṃ dinnaṃ | so dāni taṃ gṛhya pānāgāraṃ gatvā ātmanā ca khādati pārāṃś ca chandeti | te dān āhaṃsuḥ | kahiṃ tvayā imaṃ labdhaṃ | so dān āha | mā śabdaṃ | śākiyāyinānāṃ śramaṇīyo dakṣiṇīyāyo | tāsāṃ pi vayaṃ dakṣiṇīyāyo | tāsāṃ pi vayaṃ dakṣiṇīyāḥ | jano dāni ojjhāyati | bhikṣuṇīhi śrutaṃ | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtan te gartodaramāte | tena hi na kṣamati āgārikasya vā parivrājakasya vā khādanīyam vā bhojanīyam vā dātuṃ | atha khalu bhagavān | peyālaṃ | yāvat |
body.translated_text: This is the circumstance of the origin: <s>Gartodara</s>, his father, and his mother all went forth from the household life to homelessness. <s>Gartodara</s>'s father and mother went forth among the <s>Śākyas</s>; <s>Gartodara</s> went forth among the non-Buddhist ascetics. Up to: he approached <s>Gartodara</s>'s mother, and she gave him a full bowl of various hard foods. Having taken it, he went to a drinking-hall and ate it himself and shared with others. They said: 'Where did you get this?' He said: 'Don't tell anyone. The <s>Śākya</s> female ascetics are worthy of gifts; and we too are worthy of their gifts.' People were displeased. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> heard this. This matter—abbreviation—up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>Gartodaramātā</s>. Therefore, it is not permissible to give hard or soft food to a householder or a wandering ascetic.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>—abbreviation—up to:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī āgārikasya vā parivrājakasya vā svahastaṃ khādanīyam vā bhojanīyam vā dadyāt pācattikaṃ | yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | āgārikasyeti gṛhiṇaḥ | parivrājakasyeti gautamajaṭilakaparyantasya | svahastan ti hastena hastaṃ | bhājanena vā bhājanaṃ | khādanīyan ti yaṃ khādanīyaṃ | bhojanīyan ti yaṃ bhojanīyaṃ | dadyāt pācattikaṃ | eṣa dāni bhikṣuṇīya kocid āgacchati | sālohito vā bhrātā vā | yadi tāvad asya kiñcid dātuṃ bhavati na kṣamati svahastaṃ dātuṃ | kalpiyakārikāya dātavyaṃ | atha dāni kalpiyakārī na bhavati vaktavyaṃ | ato svayaṃ gṛhṇīya khādatha | atha dāni paśyati | rasagṛddhī ya eṣo sarvaṃ khādatīti | yattakaṃ parityaktaṃ tattakaṃ pratigrāhayitvā śeṣaṃ | vaktavyo | gopehīti | tato bhūmīyan nikṣipiya vaktavyo | gṛhṇīya khādatha | atha dāni pravrajitako āgacchati na kṣamati svahastaṃ khādanīyam vā bhojanīyam vā dātuṃ | kalpiyakārīya dātavyaṃ | atha dāni kalpiyakārī na bhavati ato yeva gṛhṇīya khādāhīti | atha dān āha | sālohite kim asmākaṃ caṇḍālehi viya pravartasi | vaktavyaṃ | tathā yūyaṃ durākhyāte pravacane pravrajitāḥ | atha dāni grāmāntaraṃ gacchati labhyan tena kalpiyakṛtyaṃ kārāpayituṃ | ato ātmā ca khādatha asmākañ ca pratigrāhatha | atha dāni jānāti | rasagṛdhrā iti śeṣaṃ pūrvavat | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> gives hard or soft food with her own hand to a householder or a wandering ascetic—it is a <s>pācattika</s>. 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>'—means one who is fully ordained. 'Householder'—means a layperson. 'Wandering ascetic'—means [non-Buddhist ascetics] up to <s>Gautama</s>-ascetics and matted-hair ascetics. 'With one's own hand'—means hand to hand, or vessel to vessel. 'Hard food'—means whatever is hard food. 'Soft food'—means whatever is soft food. 'Gives'—it is a <s>pācattika</s>. Now, when a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> has someone come—a relative or a brother: if she has something to give, it is not permissible to give with her own hand; it should be given through the one who makes it allowable (<s>kalpiyakārikā</s>). If there is no such person, she should say: 'Take it yourself and eat.' If she then sees that the person is greedy for taste and eats everything, she should have him accept as much as she has given up and say of the rest: 'Keep it.' Then she should place it on the ground and say: 'Take it and eat.' Now if a wandering ascetic comes, it is not permissible to give hard or soft food with one's own hand; it should be given through the one who makes it allowable. If there is no such person, [she should say:] 'Take it yourself and eat.' If he says: 'Relative, why do you treat us like outcasts?'—she should say: 'You have gone forth in a poorly-taught doctrine.' If he goes to another village, she may have him make the food allowable there: 'Eat yourself and accept [some] for us as well.' If she then knows he is greedy for taste, the rest is as before. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī āgārikasya vā parivrājakasya vā svahastaṃ khādanīyam vā bhojanīyam vā dadyāt pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> gives hard or soft food with her own hand to a householder or a wandering ascetic—it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma82, 83
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rules 82, 83

body.text: cikitasati
body.translated_text: Practicing medicine (<s>cikitsati</s>)

body.text: 196. bhagavān kauśāmbīyaṃ viharati | chandakamātā bhikṣuṇī rājño 'nataḥpuraṃ praviśati | kuśalā mūlabhaiṣajyānāṃ patrabhaiṣajyānāṃ phalabhaiṣajyānāṃ | sā dāni rājakulehi amātyakulehi āpaṇikakulehi śreṣṭhikulehi strīṇāṃ bastiṃ sthapeti | mūḍhagrabhāṃ cikitsati | añjanaṃ pratyañjanaṃ vamanaṃ virecanaṃ svedakarma nastakarma śastrakarma bhaiṣajyām anuprayacchati | sā upasarpaṇaṃ bhavati khajjaṃ bhojjaṃ labhati | tā dāni bhikṣuṇīyo ojjhāyanti | neyaṃ pravrajyā vaidyikā iyaṃ | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | yāvad bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha chandakamātāṃ | sā dāni śadbāpitā | bhagavān āha | satyaṃ chandakamāte cikitsitavidyayā jīvikāṃ kalpayasi | ām bhagavan | bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtaṃ chandakamāte | tena hi na kṣamati cikitsitavidyayā jīvikāṃ kalpayituṃ | atha khalu bhagavān | peyālaṃ | yāvat |
body.translated_text: 196. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Kauśāmbī</s>. The <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Chandakamātā</s> used to enter the king's inner palace. She was skilled in root-medicines, leaf-medicines, and fruit-medicines. She would administer enemas to women of royal families, minister families, merchant families, and guild-master families; she treated difficult pregnancies; she administered collyrium, counter-collyrium, emetics, purgatives, sweating treatments, nasal treatments, surgical procedures, and prescribed medicines. She received patronage [for this] and obtained hard and soft foods. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> were displeased: 'This going forth is not [for practicing] medicine.' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon <s>Chandakamātā</s>.' She was summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is it true, <s>Chandakamātā</s>, that you earn a livelihood through the art of medicine?' 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>Chandakamātā</s>. Therefore, it is not permissible to earn a livelihood through the art of medicine.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>—abbreviation—up to:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī cikitsitavidyayā jīvikāṃ kalpayet pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> earns a livelihood through the art of medicine—it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: cikitsitavidyā nāma ahividyā viṣavidyā yāvad grahacaritaṃ | tena jīvikāṃ kalpayati pācattikaṃ | yāvat prajñaptiḥ | na kṣamati bhikṣuṇīya cikitsituṃ | labhyam upadiśituṃ | bhikṣur api cikitsitavidyayā jīvikāṃ kalpayati vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'The art of medicine' means: snake-charming, knowledge of poisons—up to knowledge of planetary movements. If she earns a livelihood from that—it is a <s>pācattika</s>. Up to the formal designation. It is not permissible for a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> to practice medicine, [but] it is permissible to give advice. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too incurs a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression if he earns a livelihood through the art of medicine. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī cikitsitavidyayā jīvikāṃ kalpayet pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> earns a livelihood through the art of medicine—it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 83
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 83

body.text: vācayati
body.translated_text: Teaching [medicine] (<s>vācayati</s>)

body.text: 197. bhagavān kauśāmbīyaṃ viharati | bhagavatā śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ | na kṣamati cikitsitun ti | chandakamātā na bhūyo cikitsati | jano dāni āgacchati | sādhv ārye cikitsāhi | sā dān āha | na kṣamati cikitsituṃ bhagavatā śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ | api tu eṣa detha mama kiñcid vāciṣyaṃ | sā āgārikāṃś ca parivrājakāṃś ca cikitsitavidyāṃ vācayati | bhikṣuṇīyo dāni ojjhāyanti | neyaṃ kiñcit pravrajyā vaidyakavācikā iyaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 197. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Kauśāmbī</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> had established the training rule: 'It is not permissible to practice medicine.' <s>Chandakamātā</s> no longer practiced medicine. But people came [saying]: 'Noble one, please treat [us].' She said: 'It is not permissible to practice medicine; the <s>Bhagavān</s> has established a training rule. But give me something and I will teach you.' She then taught householders and wandering ascetics the art of medicine. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> were displeased: 'This going forth is not [for] teaching medicine.' Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī āgārikam vā parivrājakam vā cikitsitavidyāṃ vācayet pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> teaches the art of medicine to a householder or a wandering ascetic—it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti | pe | āgārika iti gṛhiṇaḥ | parivrājaka iti gautamajaṭilakaparyantaṃ kṛtvā | cikitsitavidyām iti ahividyā viṣavidyā yāvad grahacaritaṃ | kāyaṃ cikitsitaṃ vācayed iti uddiśet | yāvat prajñaptiḥ | na kṣamati bhikṣuṇīye āgārikam vā parivrājakam vā cikitsitavidyāṃ vācayituṃ | labhyaṃ upadiśituṃ | bhikṣur api cikitsitavidyāṃ vācayati vinayātikramam āsādyati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>'—abbreviation. 'Householder'—means a layperson. 'Wandering ascetic'—means up to <s>Gautama</s>-ascetics and matted-hair ascetics. 'Art of medicine'—means snake-charming, knowledge of poisons—up to knowledge of planetary movements. 'Teaches bodily medicine'—means instructs. Up to the formal designation. It is not permissible for a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> to teach the art of medicine to a householder or wandering ascetic, [but] it is permissible to advise. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too incurs a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression if he teaches the art of medicine. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī āgārikam vā parivrājakam vā cikitsitavidyāṃ vācayet pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> teaches the art of medicine to a householder or a wandering ascetic—it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 84
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 84

body.text: gṛhivaiyāpṛtyaṃ
body.translated_text: Doing household work (<s>gṛhivaiyāpṛtya</s>)

body.text: 198. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | viśākhāya dāni mṛgāramātāya ubhayato saṃgho bhaktenopanimantrito | tā dāni bhikṣuṇīyo kalyato yevāgatvā āhaṃsuḥ | upāsike yaṃ dāni tvayā ubhayato saṃgho bhaktenopanimantrito kin dāni vayam upāsikāya upakāraṃ karoma | sā dān āha | kim āryamiśrikā upakāraṃ kariṣyanti | uddiśatha svādhyāyatha | yoniśo manasi karotha | evaṃ mamopakāro kṛto bhaviṣyati | evam etad api tu upakāraṃ kariṣyāmaḥ | tāyo dāni talakam abhiruhitvā karpāsaṃ gṛhītvā anyāhi cikitsitaṃ | anyāhi vilopitaṃ | anyāhi piñjitaṃ | anyāhi vihataṃ | anyāhi kartitaṃ | tāyo sūtrapiṇḍakaṃ gṛhṇīya upāsikām upasaṃkrāntāḥ | upāsike upakāraḥ kṛtaḥ | āha | naiṣa mama upakāro yaṃ mamāryamiśrikā piñjeyur vā loḍheyur vā vikaḍḍheyur vā karteyur vā | eṣo mamopakāro yam āryamiśrikā matsakāśād bhuktvā uddiśatha svādhyāyetha yāvad buddhānāṃ śāsane yogam āpadyetha | yat tāya upāsikāya avadhyāpitaṃ taṃ dāni bhikṣuṇīhi śrutaṃ | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtaṃ vo bhikṣuṇīyo | tena hi na kṣamati gṛhivaiyāpṛtyaṃ kartuṃ | yāvat |
body.translated_text: 198. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. <s>Viśākhā Mṛgāramātā</s> had invited both <s>saṃghas</s> for a meal. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> came early and said: 'Lay-devotee, since you have invited both <s>saṃghas</s> for a meal, what service shall we do for the lay-devotee?' She said: 'What service will the noble sisters do? Recite, study, apply yourselves wisely—that will be your service to me.' 'Even so, we will do some service.' They went up to the terrace, took the cotton, and some combed it, some carded it, some teased it, some beat it, some spun it. They took the spun thread-balls and went to the lay-devotee: 'Lay-devotee, the service is done.' She said: 'This is not my service—that the noble sisters card, tease, pull apart, or spin for me. This is my service: that the noble sisters, having eaten at my place, recite, study—up to: apply yourselves to the practice in the <s>Buddhas</s>' teaching.' What was spoken in reproof by that lay-devotee was heard by the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. They reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. Abbreviation. Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. Therefore, it is not permissible to do household work [for laypeople].' Up to:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī gṛhivaiyāpṛtyaṃ kuryāt pācattikaṃ | yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | gṛhīti āgāriko | vaiyāpṛtyam iti karteya vā piñjeya vā yāvat | ohaneya vā pīṣeya vā paceya vā sīveya vā | yā punar anya pi kiñcid gṛhivaiyāpṛtyam kuryāt pācattikaṃ | yāvat prajñaptiḥ | na kṣamati bhikṣuṇīya gṛhivaiyāpṛtyaṃ kartuṃ | atha dāni mālyopahāro bhavati | gandhāropaṇaṃ vā | sā āha | āryamiśrikāhi sāhāyyaṃ kartavyam iti kiñcāpi gandham vā pīṣayati | sumanāṃ vā granthayati anāpattiḥ | bhikṣur api gṛhivaiyāpṛtyaṃ karoti vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should do household work—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense. 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Householder' means a layperson. 'Work' means she should card, or comb, or grind, or cook, or sew, or do any other household work—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense. Up to the rule establishment. It is not permissible for a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> to do household work. But if there is a flower-offering, or an application of incense, and she says: 'The Noble Ladies should help'—even if she grinds incense or strings <s>sumanā</s> flowers, there is no offense. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too, if he does household work, incurs a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī gṛhivaiyāpṛtyaṃ kuryāt pācattikaṃ || 4 ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should do household work—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense. [4]

body.text: pācattikadharma 85
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 85:

body.text: saṃbhojanīyaṃ
body.translated_text: Visiting a family at an intimate time (<s>saṃbhojanīya</s>).

body.text: 199. bhagavāṃ cchrāvastīyaṃ viharati | sthūlanandā nāma bhikṣuṇī madhyāhne vighane aparaṃ kulam upasaṃkrāntā | tahin dāni dve bhāryāpatikā kleṣotpīḍitā raho saṃjñino maithunaṃ pratiṣetukāmāḥ | sā dāni apratisaṃviditā sahasā tahiṃ praviṣṭā | so dāni manuṣyo uddhāvito utkaṇṭhito karmaṇy enāṃ rājā tena parivāteti | imān tāvad itikitikāya dhītāṃ śramaṇikāṃ viṭṭālayiṣyan ti | sā dāni bhītā | prapalānā bhikṣuṇīnāṃ kathayati | manāsmi āryamiśrikāyo brahmacaryāto cyāvitā yāvad etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtaṃ te nande evan nāma tvaṃ jānantī sambhojanīyaṃ kulan divā pūrve apratisaṃvicitā upasaṃkrāmasi | atha khalu bhagavān mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm āmantrayati | sannipātaya gautami bhikṣuṇīyo | peyālaṃ | yāvat |
body.translated_text: 199. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Sthūlanandā</s>, at midday, at an inconvenient time, went to another family's house. There a husband and wife, tormented by passion, wishing to engage in sexual intercourse in private, were together in seclusion. She, without having announced herself, suddenly entered there. That man, agitated and flustered, [thought]: 'The king punishes such action—that I should be harassed by this busybody ascetic woman!' She became frightened. Having fled, she told the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>: 'I think, Noble Ladies, I have been made to fall from the holy life.' [She explained the incident.] The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. [Abbreviation.] Until the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>Nandā</s>. How is it that you, knowingly, visit a family at an intimate time, during the day, without having announced yourself?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>: 'Assemble, <s>Gautamī</s>, the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>.' [Abbreviation.] Until:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī jānantī saṃbhojanīyaṃ kulaṃ divā pūrve apratisaṃviditā upasaṃkrameya pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, knowingly, should visit a family at an intimate time, during the day, without having previously announced herself—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | jānantīti svayam vā jāneya parato vā śruṇeya | kulaṃ ti brāhmaṇādi kulaṃ | yahiṃ strīpuruṣakaṃ sthālīpiṭharakaṃ kaṇṭikāmusalakaṃ sūpellakaṃ yavaprasthakaṃ imaṃ paścimakaṃ kulaṃ | sambhojanīyan ti strī puruṣasya bhojanaṃ puruṣasyāpi strī bhojanaṃ | yadi vigate madhyāhne pūrve apratisaṃviditā ti aśabdakarṇikāya | anāhūtā upasaṃkrameyā ti praviśet pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | yaṃ dāni jñāyate etaṃ saṃbhojanīyaṃ kulan ti nahi kṣamati tahiṃ pūrve apratisaṃviditaṃ anāhūtāya upasaṃkramituṃ | yadi tāva dauvāriko bhavati vaktavyaṃ | praviśāmīti | yady āha | mā praviśehīti na praviśitavyaṃ | atha dān āha | pratipālehi tāvat yāvat pratisaṃvidāyāmīti | yadi praviśitvā na niṣkrāmati na kṣamati praviśituṃ | atha dāni tuṇutuṇā śabdo bhavati acchaṭikā dātavyā utkāśitavyaṃ vā | yadi tāva tūṣṇīkā bhavati na kṣamati praviśituṃ | atha dāni pratyudgacchanti svāgatam āryāyeti praviśeti praveṣṭavyaṃ | bhikṣur api saṃvidito upasamkramati vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Knowingly' means she knows herself or has heard from another.
