The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'How is it that you, being a leader among the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> who have fallen into quarrel, dispute, and controversy, do not settle the disputes, do not have them settled, and do not make an effort toward their settlement? Therefore, it is not permissible.' Then: until 'they will be utterly purified.' Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, being a leader among <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> who have fallen into quarrel, dispute, and controversy, should not settle the disputes, should not have them settled, and should not make an effort toward their settlement—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | kalahajātānām iti vācākalahaṃ kurvantīnāṃ vātayuktaṃ mama yuktam ity ādi | bhaṇḍanajātānām iti anyamanyaṃ mama ghaṭanaṃ kurvantīnāṃ | vigrahavivādam āpannānāṃ viharantīnām iti tadyathā | dharmo adharmo vinayo avinayo | āpattir anāpattiḥ | gurukā laghukā sapratikarmā apratikarmā sāvaśeṣā niravaśeṣā | dharmakarma adharmakarma samagrakarma vyagrakarma yāvat sthānārhaṃ karma iti viharantīnāṃ | vṛṣabhī samānā ti prabhū samānā | adhikaraṇāni na vyupasamayed iti svayan | na vyupasamāpayed iti parehi | na vyupasamānāyautsukyaṃ kuryāt pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | etā dāni bhikṣuṇīyo kalahajātā bhaṇḍanajātā vigrahavivādam āpannā viharanti na dāni kṣamati tāyo adyupekṣituṃ | atha khu vyupasamitavyāḥ vyupasamāpayitavyāḥ | autsukyaṃ kartavyaṃ upasamanāya pratyāśaṃsitavyaṃ parasparaṃ kṣamāpayitavyāḥ prāptakālaṃ yathārūpaṃ paribhāṣayitavyāḥ samagrīkartvyāḥ | atha dāni na śaknoti anyā bhikṣuṇī adhyesitavyā udyojayitavyā upāsakopāsikāyo bhikṣubhikṣuṇīyo | atha tāny adhikaraṇāni karkkaśāni bhavanti durvyupasamāni teṣām eva adhikaraṇānāṃ kālam āgamayati samayam āgamayati paripākam āgamayati | kālaṃ ca samayam ca paripākaṃ cāgamya vyupaśamayaty anāpattiḥ bhikṣur api bhikṣūṇāṃ kalahajātānāṃ bhaṇḍaṇajātānāṃ vigrahavivādam āpannānām viharantānāṃ vṛṣabho samāno adhikaraṇāni na vyupaśamayati na vyupasamāpayati na vyupasamānāyautsukyaṃ karoti vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha | yā puna bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṇīnāṃ kalahajātānāṃ bhaṇḍanajātānāṃ vigrahavivādam āpannānāṃ viharantīnāṃ vṛṣabhī samānā adhikaraṇāni na vyupasamayen na vyupasamāpayen na vyupasamānāyautsukyaṃ kuryāt pācattikaṃ ||3 ||
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Who have fallen into quarrel' means those engaged in verbal quarrel: 'my [position] is correct, yours is correct,' and so forth. 'Who have fallen into dispute' means those who form factions against each other. 'Who have entered into controversy' means: what is <s>Dharma</s> and what is non-<s>Dharma</s>, what is <s>Vinaya</s> and what is non-<s>Vinaya</s>; what is an offense and what is not an offense; what is grave and what is light; what admits of remedy and what does not; what has remainder and what has no remainder; what is a valid legal act and what is an invalid legal act; what is a complete act and what is an incomplete act; up to: what is an act worthy of status—while they are living thus. 'Being a leader' means being capable. 'Should not settle the disputes' means by herself. 'Should not have them settled' means by others. 'Should not make an effort toward their settlement'—it is a <s>pācattika</s>. Up to the rule establishment. When these <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> have fallen into quarrel, dispute, and controversy, it is not permissible to overlook them. Rather, [the disputes] should be settled, should be caused to be settled; effort should be made; settlement should be sought; they should be made to ask mutual forgiveness; they should be admonished as is fitting for the occasion; harmony should be brought about. But if she is unable [to do this herself], another <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should be requested and urged [to help]—laymen, laywomen, <s>bhikṣus</s>, and <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. But if those disputes are harsh and difficult to settle, one should wait for the right time, the right occasion, and the ripening [of conditions]. Having awaited the time, occasion, and ripening, [if she then] settles [them]—there is no offense. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too, being a leader among <s>bhikṣus</s> who have fallen into quarrel, dispute, and controversy, if he does not settle the disputes, does not have them settled, and does not make an effort toward their settlement, incurs a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, being a leader among <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> who have fallen into quarrel, dispute, and controversy, should not settle the disputes, should not have them settled, and should not make an effort toward their settlement—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense. [3]

body.text: pācattikadharma 126
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 126:

body.text: udvartanaṃ
body.translated_text: Anointing (<s>udvartana</s>).

body.text: 240. bhagavān vaiśālīyam viharati | bhadrā dāni kāpileyī jñātikulaṃ nīyate udvartanāya snāpanāya gṛhapatinīhi nīyate | vayam āryām udvartayāmaḥ snāpayiṣyāmaḥ asmākaṃ puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyati | kecit prasādena kecid aṅgayaṣṭiṃ paśyitukāmāḥ | sā dāni prāsādikā darśanīyā | kautūhalajātiko mātṛgrāmaḥ | varṇalolāṃ udvartayanti kāleyakena tuṅgeyakena svaṅgakena padmakena gandhacūrṇehi | sā pi dāni adhivāsayati | bhikṣuṇīyo dāni ojjhāyanti | paśythāryamiśrikāyo adyāpīyaṃ pravrajitā mahacchandā | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | pe | yāvad āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha | evan nāma tvaṃ gṛhiṇīnām udvartnaparimardanasnāpanasammatena udvartāpayasi | tena hi na kṣamati | atha khalu bhagavān yāvat paryavadātāni bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: 240. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s>. <s>Bhadrā Kāpileyī</s> was taken to her relatives' house for anointing and bathing. The housewives took her, [saying]: 'We shall anoint the Noble One; we shall bathe her; it will be merit for us.' Some [did it] out of devotion, some wishing to see her bodily form. She was indeed graceful and beautiful. Women are curious by nature. They anointed her with cosmetic substances: <s>kāleyaka</s>, <s>tuṅgeyaka</s>, <s>svaṅgaka</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, and fragrant powders. And she permitted it. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> were displeased: 'Look, Noble Ladies, even after going forth, she is still greatly desirous!' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. [Abbreviation.] Until: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'How is it that you have yourself anointed with the anointing, rubbing, and bathing substances approved for housewives? Therefore, it is not permissible.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> [spoke] until 'they will be utterly purified.'

body.text: yāni khalu punar imāni gṛhiṇīnām udvartanaparimardanasnāpanasammatāni tathārūpehi bhikṣuṇī agilānā udvartāpayet parimardāpayet pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, should have herself anointed or rubbed with those anointing, rubbing, and bathing substances approved for housewives—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: yāni khalu punar imāni gṛhiṇīnam iti kṣatriyakanyakānāṃ brāhmaṇakanyakānāṃ gṛhapatikanyakānāṃ | udvartanaparimardanasnāpanasammatānīti kāleyakam vā tuṅgeyakam vā cikkasam vā | yady eko vā tehi bhikṣuṇīhi agilānā udvartāpayet | kin tāvad atra gailānyam abhipretaṃ jarādurbalā vā vyādhidurbalā vā bhavati udvartāpayaty anāpattiḥ | udvartāpayed iti parimardāpayet pācattikaṃ | atha dāni gaṇḍam vā piṭakam vā bhavati labhyā bhaiṣajyehi udvartāpayituṃ parimardāpayituṃ | atha dāni pittasaṃkṣobho bhavati labhyā cikkasenāliṃpituṃ | atha dāni vātasaṃkṣobho bhavati labhyā godhūmacikkasenāliṃpituṃ | atha dāni sannipāto bhavati saṃyuktehi bhaiṣajyehi udvartāpayitavyaṃ parimardāpayitavyaṃ āliṃpitavyaṃ | tāya pi dāni āliṃpiya na kṣamati abhyāgame pradeśe sthātuṃ | atha khalu pratigupte pradeśe sthātavyaṃ | yadāvarta bhavati tadā udvartayitvā niṣkramitavyaṃ | bhikṣur api agilāno cikkasenodvartāpayet parimardāpayed vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Those which are approved for housewives' means for <s>Kṣatriya</s> maidens, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> maidens, and householder maidens. 'Anointing, rubbing, and bathing substances' means <s>kāleyaka</s>, <s>tuṅgeyaka</s>, or <s>cikkasa</s> [oil]. If a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, has herself anointed even with one of these—what is meant by 'illness' here? She is weakened by old age or weakened by disease—she may have herself anointed, there is no offense. 'Should have herself anointed' means 'should have herself rubbed'—it is a <s>pācattika</s>. But if there is a boil or abscess, it is permissible to have [the area] anointed and rubbed with medicines. If there is a bile disturbance, it is permissible to apply <s>cikkasa</s> [oil]. If there is a wind disturbance, it is permissible to apply wheat-<s>cikkasa</s> [oil]. If there is a combined disturbance, one should have [the body] anointed, rubbed, and smeared with combined medicines. But even after being smeared, it is not permissible to stand in a public place. Rather, one should stand in a secluded place. When [the oil] has been absorbed, then one may go out after anointing. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too, if not being ill, has himself anointed and rubbed with <s>cikkasa</s> [oil], incurs a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī gṛhiṇīnām udvartanaparimardanasnānasammatehi udvartāpayeta parimardāpayeta pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should have herself anointed or rubbed with anointing, rubbing, and bathing substances approved for housewives—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: pācattikadharma 127
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 127:

body.text: bhikṣuṇī
body.translated_text: By a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>.

body.text: 241. bhagavān vaiśālīyam viharati | bhagavatā dāni śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ na kṣamati gṛhiṇīnām udvartanaparimardanasnānasammatehi udvartāpayituṃ parimardāpayituṃ | sā dāni bhadrā bhikṣuṇīhi udvartāpayati parimardāpayati | bhikṣuṇīyo dāni ojjhāyanti | peyālaṃ | yāvad bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 241. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> had laid down the training rule: it is not permissible to have oneself anointed or rubbed with anointing, rubbing, and bathing substances approved for housewives. Then <s>Bhadrā</s> had herself anointed and rubbed by <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> were displeased. [Abbreviation.] Until the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī agilānā bhikṣuṇīya udvartāpayet parimardāpayet pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, should have herself anointed or rubbed by a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | bhikṣuṇīyeti upasampannāya | agilānā ti kin tāvad atra gailānyam abhipretaṃ jarādurbalā vā vyādhidurbalā vā bhoti | pratyuddhṛtaṃ bhagavatā anāpattiḥ gilānāya | udvartāpayet parimardāpayet pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī agilānā bhikṣuṇīya udvartāpayati na parimardāpayati vinayātikramaḥ | parimardāpayati nodvartāpayati vinayātikramaḥ | ubhayaṃ karoti pācattikaṃ | nobhayam anāpattiḥ | bhikṣur api agilāno bhikṣuṇā udvartāpayati parimardāpayati vinayātikramaḥ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'By a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means by one who is fully ordained. 'Not being ill' — what is meant by illness here? She is weakened by old age or weakened by disease. The <s>Bhagavān</s> has exempted [this case]: there is no offense for one who is ill. 'Should have herself anointed or rubbed'—it is a <s>pācattika</s>. Up to the rule establishment. If this <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, has herself anointed by a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> but not rubbed—it is a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression. If she has herself rubbed but not anointed—it is a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression. If she does both—it is a <s>pācattika</s>. If she does neither—there is no offense. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too, if not being ill, has himself anointed and rubbed by a <s>bhikṣu</s>—it is a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī agilānā bhikṣuṇīya udvartāpayet parimardāpayet pācattikaṃ || phu ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, should have herself anointed or rubbed by a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: pācattikadharma 128
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 128:

body.text: śrāmaṇeri
body.translated_text: By a novice (<s>śrāmaṇerī</s>).

body.text:
evaṃ eva śrāmaṇeryā nāsti nānākaraṇaṃ | tena bhagavān āha |
yā puna bhikṣuṇī agilānā śrāmaṇerīya udvartāpayet parimardāpayet pācattikaṃ || phu ||
body.translated_text: The same applies regarding a novice. There is no difference. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, should have herself anointed or rubbed by a novice—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: pācattikadharma 129
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 129:

body.text: śikṣamāṇā
body.translated_text: By a trainee (<s>śikṣamāṇā</s>).

body.text: etad eva śikṣamāṇāyāḥ | śikṣamāṇā nāma aṣṭādaśahi vartehi dve varṣāṇi śikṣamāṇā yāvat | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: The same applies regarding a trainee. A '<s>śikṣamāṇā</s>' means one who has been training for two years in the eighteen observances. Until: Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī agilānā śikṣamāṇāya udvartāpayet parimardāpayet pācattikaṃ ||grā ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, should have herself anointed or rubbed by a trainee—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: pācattikadharma 130
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 130:

body.text: gṛhiṇī
body.translated_text: By a laywoman (<s>gṛhiṇī</s>).

body.text: etad eva gṛhiṇīya | nāsti nānākaraṇaṃ | gṛhiṇīti gṛhasthā | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: The same applies regarding a laywoman. There is no difference. 'Laywoman' means a householder woman. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī agilānā gṛhiṇīya udvartāpayet parimardāpayet pācattikaṃ || hrā ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, should have herself anointed or rubbed by a laywoman—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: pācattikadharma 131
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 131:

body.text: viśuddhisaṃvāsena
body.translated_text: Regarding the purity-observance (<s>viśuddhisaṃvāsa</s>).

body.text: 242. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | bhikṣuṇīyo dāni sannipatitāḥ poṣadha karmāya | jetā nāma bhikṣuṇī | sā nāgacchati | tāye dūto 'nupreṣito | ārye āgacchāhi bhikṣuṇīyo sannipatitāḥ poṣadhakarmāya | sā dān āha | bhagavatā viśuddhasya viśuddhipoṣadhaḥ prajñaptaḥ | yāvatikā kā viśuddhā ahan tāsām anyatamāsāṃ tatra nāgacchāmi | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | pe | yāvad āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtaṃ te jete | tvañ ca nāma poṣadhan na satkaroṣi | kā anyā satkariṣyati ko ca poṣadhasya satkāro | agilānāya upasaṃkramitavyaṃ | gilānāya chando dātavyo | atha khalu bhagavān yāvat paryavadātāni bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: 242. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> had assembled for the <s>poṣadha</s> ceremony. A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Jetā</s> did not come. A messenger was sent to her: 'Noble One, come; the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> have assembled for the <s>poṣadha</s> ceremony.' She said: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has prescribed the purity-<s>poṣadha</s> for those who are pure. As many as are pure—I am one of them. I do not come there.' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. [Abbreviation.] Until: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>Jetā</s>. If you do not honor the <s>poṣadha</s>, who else will honor it? And what is the honor of the <s>poṣadha</s>? One who is not ill should attend in person. One who is ill should send her consent.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> [spoke] until 'they will be utterly purified.'

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī anvardhamāsaṃagilānā viśuddhisaṃvāsaṃ na satkareya pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, every half-month, not being ill, should not honor the purity-observance—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | anvardhamāsaṃ viśuddhisaṃvāsaṃ ti cāturdaśikena vā cāturdaśikaṃ pāñcadaśikena vā pāñcadaśikaṃ | agilānā poṣadhan na satkāroti | kin dāni atra gailānyam abhipretaṃ | eṣā bhavati jarādurbalā vā vyādhidurbalā vā śirāviddhikā vā bhavati asukhā bhaiṣajyaṃ vā pītam bhavati | ghṛtaṃ vā pītam bhavati | chando dātavyo |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Every half-month, the purity-observance' means on the fourteenth or the fifteenth [day of the half-month]. 'Not being ill, does not honor the <s>poṣadha</s>' — what is meant by illness here? She is weakened by old age, or weakened by disease, or has had a vein opened, or is unwell, or has taken medicine, or has drunk ghee. She should send her consent.

body.text: sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī agilānā poṣadhan na gacchati | gilānā vā chandan na deti pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: If this <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, does not go to the <s>poṣadha</s>; or, being ill, does not send her consent—it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: bhikṣur api agilāno naiva poṣadhaṃ gacchati na cchandan deti vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣu</s> too, if not being ill, neither goes to the <s>poṣadha</s> nor sends his consent, incurs a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī anvardhamāsaṃ agilānā viśuddhisaṃvāsan na satkareya pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, every half-month, not being ill, should not honor the purity-observance—it is a <s>pācattika</s> offense.

body.text: uddānaṃ |
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

body.text: upasaṃkramati [1(123)] | kalaho [3(124)] | viśoko [2(125)] | udvartanaṃ [4(126)] | bhikṣuṇī [5(127)] | śrāmaṇerī [6(128)] | śikṣamāṇā [7(129)] | gṛhiṇīya [8(130)] | viśuddhisaṃvāsena [9(131)] ||
body.translated_text: Approaching [1(123)]; quarrel [3(124)]; free from sorrow [2(125)]; anointing [4(126)]; by a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> [5(127)]; by a novice [6(128)]; by a trainee [7(129)]; by a laywoman [8(130)]; the purity-observance [9(131)].

body.text: pūryate trayodaśamo vargaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The thirteenth section is complete.

body.text: pācattikadharma 132
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 132:

body.text:
ovādopasaṃkramaṇaṃ
viśuddhipoṣadhaṃ
body.translated_text: Seeking instruction (<s>ovādopasaṃkramaṇa</s>), the purity-<s>poṣadha</s>.

body.text: 243. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | therabhikṣū paryāyeṇa bhikṣuṇīyo ovadanti | te dāni āyuṣmanto ṣaḍvargikāḥ ovādakavāraṃ na labhanti | te dān āhaṃsuḥ | na ete yuṣmākaṃ ovādakavāraṃ dāsyanti | kasya dāni vayam ovādakavāraṃ gacchāmaḥ | te dān āhaṃsuḥ | āyuṣmāṃ cchāriputraḥ sa khilo ca mṛduko ca | vistāreṇa yāvad bhagavatā śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ | na kṣamati asammatena bhikṣuṇā bhikṣuṇīyo ovadituṃ | eṣa niḥsīmaṃ gatvā parasparaṃ sammanyāmaḥ | te dāni niḥsīmaṃ gatvā anyamanyaṃ saṃmanyitvā kalyato yeva nivāsayitvā prāvaritvā ca bhikṣuṇī upāśrayaṃ gatvā āhaṃsuḥ | sannipatatha bhaginīyo ovādo bhaviṣyati | yāyo ṣaḍvargiṇīyo tāyo 'cchanti sannipatitāḥ | yāyo yogācārāyo bhikṣuṇīyo tāyo na sannipatanti | āhaṃsuḥ | kim artham vayam eṣām avinītānām avavādaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ | te dāni tāhi saha muhūrtam antaraṃ kākavaṃhā bhañjitvā gatāḥ | āyuṣmān dāni śāriputro kālasyaiva nivāsayitvā pātracīvaram ādāya āyuṣmatā ānandena paścāc chramaṇena sārdhaṃ vistareṇa | yāvad āha | sannipatatha bhaginīyo ovādo bhaviṣyati | yāyo bhikṣuṇīyo yogācārāḥ tāyo 'cchanti sannipatitāyo | ṣaḍvargiṇīyo bhikṣuṇīyo nāgacchanti | thero pṛcchati | samagro hi bhikṣuṇīsaṃgho | āhaṃsuḥ | nahi ko nāgacchati | āhaṃsuḥ ṣaḍvargiṇīyo | tāsān dūtaḥ preṣito | āgacchatha bhaginīyo ovādo bhaviṣyati | tā dān āhaṃsuḥ | na vayam āgamiṣyāmaḥ | ovaditā vayam āryamiśrakehi ṣaḍvargikehi anyavihitakena ovādena | athāyuṣmān śāriputro vyagro bhikṣuṇīsaṃgho ti kṛtvā utthāyāsanāto prakrānto | bhagavān jānanto yeva pṛcchati kin dāni gautamī mātā śīghram āgato si | ovaditā bhikṣuṇīyo | āha | ahaṃ bhagavan kālasyaiva nivāsayitvā yāvad bhikṣuṇīupāśrayaṃ praviṣṭo ovadituṃ mayoktaṃ sannipatatha bhaginīyo ovādo bhaviṣyati | yāyo yogācārāyo bhikṣuṇīyo tāyo 'cchanti sannipatitāyo | yāyo ṣaḍvargiṇīyo bhikṣuṇīyo tā na sannipatanti | ahaṃ jalpāmi samagro bhikṣuṇīsaṃgho | āhaṃsuḥ | nahi | ko nāgacchati | āhaṃsuḥ ṣaḍvargiṇīyo | tāsān dūtaḥ preṣitaḥ | āgacchatha bhaginiyo ovādo bhaviṣyati | āhaṃsuḥ | na vayam āgamiṣyāmaḥ ovaditā vayam āryamiśrikehi ṣaḍvargikehi anyavihitakena ovādena | ahaṃ pi bhagavan vyagro bhikṣuṇīsaṃgho ti kṛtvā utthāyāsanāto sannirgato | bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha ṣaḍvargiṇīyo bhikṣuṇīyo | tā dāni śabdāpitāḥ | tad eva sarvaṃ bhagavān vistareṇa pṛcchati | yāvad āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtaṃ vo ṣaḍvargiṇīyo yāvat paryavadātāni bhavanti |
body.translated_text: 243. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Senior <s>bhikṣus</s> were instructing the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> in rotation. Now, the venerable group-of-six (<s>ṣaḍvargikas</s>) did not receive a turn to instruct. They said: 'They will not give you a turn to instruct. Whose instruction turn shall we attend?' They said: 'The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> — he is gentle and mild.' In detail, up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> laid down a training rule: 'It is not permissible for an unappointed <s>bhikṣu</s> to instruct <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>.' [They said:] 'Let us go outside the boundary and appoint each other.' They went outside the boundary, appointed each other, and early in the morning, having dressed and wrapped themselves, went to the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> residence and said: 'Assemble, sisters, there will be instruction.' Those who were the group-of-six [<s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>] came and assembled. Those who were diligent <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> did not assemble. They said: 'Why should we attend the instruction of these undisciplined ones?' Those [monks], having spent a moment with them, broke some crow's wing [bones — i.e., wasted time on trivia] and departed. Now the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having dressed early in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, together with the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> following behind as attendant — in detail — up to: he said: 'Assemble, sisters, there will be instruction.' Those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> who were diligent came and assembled. The group-of-six <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> did not come. The elder asked: 'Is the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> assembly complete?' They said: 'No.' 'Who has not come?' They said: 'The group-of-six.' A messenger was sent to them: 'Come, sisters, there will be instruction.' They said: 'We will not come. We have already been instructed by the noble group-of-six monks with a different kind of instruction.' Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, considering that the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> assembly was incomplete, rose from his seat and departed. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, though knowing, asked: 'How is it, mother <s>Gautamī</s>, that you have come back so quickly? Have the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> been instructed?' He said: '<s>Bhagavan</s>, I dressed early in the morning, up to: entered the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> residence to instruct. I said: "Assemble, sisters, there will be instruction." The diligent <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> came and assembled. The group-of-six <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> did not assemble. I asked: "Is the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> assembly complete?" They said: "No." "Who has not come?" They said: "The group-of-six." A messenger was sent to them: "Come, sisters, there will be instruction." They said: "We will not come. We have been instructed by the noble group-of-six monks with a different kind of instruction." I too, <s>Bhagavan</s>, considering that the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> assembly was incomplete, rose from my seat and departed.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon the group-of-six <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>.' They were summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> questioned all of it in detail. Up to: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavan</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, group-of-six, up to: [the rules] will be made clear.'

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī anvardha māsaṃ bhikṣusaṃghe ovādopasaṃkramaṇaṃ na satkareya pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should not respect the fortnightly approach to the <s>bhikṣu</s> assembly for instruction, it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | anvardhamāsan ti cāturdaśikena vā cāturdaśikaṃ | pāñcadaśikena vā pāñcadaśikaṃ | bhikṣusaṃghe ovadopasaṃkramaṇaṃ na satkareya pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | atha dāni jarādurbalā vā vyādhidurbalā vā ghṛtapītikā vā bhavati vaktavyaṃ | ovādasya chandan demi trikkhatto | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī agilānā ovādopasaṃkramaṇaṃ na gacchati gilānā vā chandan na deti pācattikam āsādayati | yadā poṣadho bhavati tadā cchandahārikāhi bhikṣuvihāraṅ gatvā vaktavyaṃ | samagro bhikṣuṇīsaṃgho samagrasya bhikṣusaṃghasya pādāṃ cchirasā vandati poṣadhañ ca pratīcchati avavādaṃ ca yācati evaṃ trikkhatto yācitavyaṃ | yadi tāvat kocid bhikṣuṇīovādako bhavati vaktavyaṃ | eṣa bhaginīyo ovādako āgamiṣyati | atha na kocid bhavati yo taṃhi aṅgopeto bhavati so saṃmanyitavyo | atha na kocid vaktavyaṃ | nāsti bhaginīyo bhikṣuṇīovādako apramādena saṃpādetha āpattiñ ca poṣadhaṃ pratijāgratha sagauravā ca bhavatha sthavirehi bhikṣūhi madhyehi navakehīti | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Fortnightly' means on the fourteenth with the fourteenth, or the fifteenth with the fifteenth. 'Should not respect the approach to the <s>bhikṣu</s> assembly for instruction' — it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to the rule establishment. Now, if she is weakened by old age, or weakened by disease, or has drunk ghee [as medicine], she should say [by proxy]: 'I give my consent for the instruction' — three times. If that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, does not go to the instruction approach, or being ill does not give consent — she incurs a <s>pācattika</s>. When the <s>upoṣadha</s> (observance) day occurs, the consent-bearers should go to the <s>bhikṣu</s> monastery and say: 'The complete <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> assembly bows at the feet of the complete <s>bhikṣu</s> assembly, receives the <s>upoṣadha</s>, and requests instruction' — this should be requested three times. If there is an instructor of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, it should be said: 'Sisters, the instructor will come.' But if there is none who is qualified, one should be appointed. If there is no one [at all], it should be said: 'Sisters, there is no <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> instructor. Practice with diligence, and be vigilant regarding offenses and the <s>upoṣadha</s>, and be respectful toward senior <s>bhikṣus</s>, middle-ranking ones, and juniors.' Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī anvardhamāsaṃ viśuddhipoṣadhaṃ na satkareya pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should not respect the fortnightly purification <s>upoṣadha</s>, it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 133
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> Rule 133

body.text: gaṇḍam vā piṭakam vā
body.translated_text: Boil or Abscess (<s>gaṇḍa</s> or <s>piṭaka</s>)

body.text: 244. bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati | jetāye bhikṣuṇīye saṃbādhe pradeśe gaṇḍam utpannaṃ | tāye antevāsinīyo gocarañ gatāyo | hiṇḍikavaidyo āgato | sā dān āha | dīrghāyuḥ śakyasi mama śastrakarma kartuṃ | so dān āha | bāḍhaṃ | so dāni pāṭayitvā dhovāyitvā upanāhayitvā gato | tāyo bhikṣuṇīyo āgatāyo | tāhi dāni so pradeśo dṛṣṭo pūyamrakṣito | tā dān āhaṃsuḥ | ārye kim idaṃ | āha | śastrakarma kāritaṃ | āhaṃsuḥ | sāhasam āryāya kṛtaṃ saṃbādhe pradeśe śastrakarma kārayantīya | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | pe | yāvad āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha | evaṃ ca nāma tvaṃ upari jānumaṇḍalābhyāṃ adho kakṣābhyāṃ gaṇḍam vā piṭakam vā kṣatam vā upahatam vā akṛtvā pūrvakṛtyaṃ anavalokayitvā saṃghaṃ śastrakarma kārāpayasi | tena hi na kṣamati | peyālaṃ | yāvat |
body.translated_text: 244. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>. The <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Jetā</s> had a boil in a private area. Her pupils had gone for alms-round. A traveling physician came. She said: 'Long-lived one, can you perform surgery on me?' He said: 'Certainly.' He then cut it open, washed it, and bandaged it, and left. Those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> returned. They saw the area — protected by pus. They said: 'Noble one, what is this?' She said: 'I had surgery done.' They said: 'The noble lady has acted recklessly, having surgery done in a private area!' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. [Abbreviated.] Up to: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavan</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'How could you have surgery performed on a boil, abscess, wound, or injury above the kneecaps and below the armpits without first performing the preliminary procedure and without consulting the <s>Saṃgha</s>? Therefore it is not permissible.' [Abbreviated.] Up to:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī upari jānumaṇḍalābhyām adho kakṣābhyāṃ gaṇḍam vā piṭakam vā kṣatam vā upahatam vā akṛtvā pūrvakṛtyaṃ anavalokayitvā saṃghaṃ puruṣeṇa pātāpayed vā dhovāpayed vā upanāhāpayed vā pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, without performing the preliminary procedure and without consulting the <s>Saṃgha</s>, should have a man lance, wash, or bandage a boil, abscess, wound, or injury above the kneecaps and below the armpits, it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | upari jānumaṇḍalābhyām iti ūrunābhibhyāṃ | adho kakṣābhyām iti stanodarasya | gaṇḍam vā piṭakam vā kṣatam vā upahatam vā akṛtvā pūrvakṛtyan ti bhikṣuṇī vaktavyo śastrakarma kārāpayiṣyan ti |
body.translated_text: 'If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Above the kneecaps' means above the thighs. 'Below the armpits' means of the breast and abdomen. 'Boil, abscess, wound, or injury — without performing the preliminary procedure' means the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should say: 'I am going to have surgery done.'

body.text: anavalokayitvā saṃghā ti saṃghamadhye avalokanā kartavyā | śṛṇotu me āryā saṃgho yadi saṃghasya prāptakālaṃ itthannāmā bhikṣuṇī śastrakarma kārāpeya | kārāpayiṣyati āryā saṃgho itthannāmā bhikṣuṇī śastrakarma | kṣamate taṃ saṃghasya yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam etad dhārayāmi |
body.translated_text: 'Without consulting the <s>Saṃgha</s>' means a formal consultation should be made in the midst of the <s>Saṃgha</s>: 'Let the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> hear me. If the time is suitable for the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> so-and-so will have surgery done. The noble <s>Saṃgha</s> will [authorize] that the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> so-and-so may have surgery done. If this is agreeable to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, let it be silent — thus do I hold it.'

body.text: puruṣeṇeti gṛhasthena vā pravrajitena vā pāṭāpayed vā dhovāpayed vā upanāhāpeya vā ti yathā jetā bhikṣuṇīti pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | atha dāni saṃbādhe pradeśe gaṇḍam vā piṭakam vā kṣatam vā upahatam vā bhavati antevāsinīye vā samānopādhyāyinīye vā samānācāryāye vā yasyā viśvāso tāya ākhyātavyaṃ | kaṇṭakena vā nakhena vā bhedāpayitavyaṃ bhaiṣajyena vā ālimpāpeyatavyaṃ atha dāni adho jānumaṇḍalābhyām upari kakṣābhyām bhavati gaṇḍam vā piṭakam vā kṣatam vā puruṣeṇa pāṭāpayati vā dhovāpayati vā upanāhāpayati vā evam śirām vā vedhāpayati nelāṭikam vā bāhuśirām vā gulphaśirām vā aparāya bhikṣuṇīya ākramitavyā tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'By a man' means by a householder or a renunciant. 'Should have [him] lance, wash, or bandage' means as [in the case of] the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Jetā</s> — it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to the rule establishment. Now, if there is a boil, abscess, wound, or injury in a private area, she should tell a pupil, a fellow student under the same preceptress, a fellow student under the same instructress, or whomever she trusts. It should be opened with a thorn or a fingernail, and medicine should be applied. But if it is below the kneecaps or above the armpits — a boil, abscess, or wound — a man may lance it, wash it, or bandage it. Likewise if a vein needs to be opened — on the forehead, arm, or ankle — another <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should press [the area]. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī upari jānumaṇḍalābhyāṃ adho kakṣābhyāṃ gaṇḍam vā piṭakam vā kṣatam vā upahatam vā akṛtvā pūrvakṛtyaṃ anavalokayitvā saṃghaṃ puruṣeṇa pāṭāpayed vā dhovāpayed vā upanāhāpayed vā pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, without performing the preliminary procedure and without consulting the <s>Saṃgha</s>, should have a man lance, wash, or bandage a boil, abscess, wound, or injury above the kneecaps and below the armpits, it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 134
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> Rule 134

body.text: varṣopagatā
body.translated_text: During the Rains Retreat (<s>varṣopagatā</s>)

body.text: 245. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | atha kālī nāma bhikṣuṇī varṣopagatā sāṃghikaṃ vihāraṃ bandhitvā cārikāṃ prakrāntāḥ | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | pe | yāvad āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtam te kāli evan nāma tvaṃ varṣopagatānāṃ cārikāṃ prakramasi | tena hi na kṣamati varṣopagatāya cārikāṃ prakramituṃ | atha khalu bhagavān yāvat paryavadātāni bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: 245. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Kālī</s>, having entered the rains retreat, locked up the <s>Saṃgha</s> dwelling and departed on a wandering tour. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. [Abbreviated.] Up to: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavan</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>Kālī</s>. How could you depart on a wandering tour during the rains retreat? Therefore it is not permissible to depart on a wandering tour while in the rains retreat.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> [spoke] up to: '[the rules] will be made clear.'

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī varṣopagatā cārikāṃ prakrāmeya pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, having entered the rains retreat, should depart on a wandering tour, it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | varṣā ti varṣārātraṃ | upagatā ti purimikāṃ paścimikām vā varṣopanāmayikāṃ upagatā | cārikāṃ prakrāmeyā ti anyatra gaccheya grāmāntaraṃ pi pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī ekarātram pi vipravasati pācattikaṃ | atha dāni rājabhayam vā senābhayam vā paracakrabhayam vā jīvitāntarāyo vā brahmacaryāntarāyo vā bhaveya kiñcāpi gacchati anāpattiḥ | nāsti bhikṣuṇyā avalokanākarma saptāhaṃ vā kiñcāpi bhikuḥ avalokanākarma kṛtvā saptāhaṃ vā adhiṣṭhiheya gacchaty anāpattiḥ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Rains' means the rainy season. 'Having entered' means having entered the first or the second rains-entry period. 'Should depart on a wandering tour' means should go elsewhere, even to another village — it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to the rule establishment. If that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> is away even for a single night, it is a <s>pācattika</s>. But if there is danger from a king, danger from an army, danger from a foreign invader, danger to life, or danger to the holy life — even if she goes, there is no offense. There is no formal leave procedure (<s>avalokanākarma</s>) for a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not even for seven days. But a <s>bhikṣu</s>, having performed the formal leave procedure and having determined seven days, may go without offense. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī varṣopagatā cārikāṃ prakrameya pācattikaṃ ||3 ||
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, having entered the rains retreat, should depart on a wandering tour, it is a <s>pācattika</s>. [3]

body.text: pācattikadharma 135
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> Rule 135

body.text: varṣāvustā
body.translated_text: After the Rains Retreat (<s>varṣāvustā</s>)

body.text: 246. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | bhikṣuṇīyo dāni śrāvastīyaṃ varṣoṣitāḥ vaiśālīm āgatāḥ | tāyo bhadrāye kāpileyīye jñātikulaṃ praviṣṭāḥ | tā striyo āhaṃsuḥ | kahiṃ āryamiśrikā varṣoṣitāḥ | tā dān āhaṃsuḥ | śrāvastīyaṃ | āhaṃsuḥ | kīdṛśī śrāvastī | āhaṃsuḥ | idṛśī ca idṛśī ca evam ārāmaramaṇīyā | evaṃ | jetavanaṃ | evaṃ gandhakuṭī | evam bhagavān viharati | evam āryamiśrikā śāriputramaudgalyāyanāḥ | yadi pravrajyā eṣā pravrajyā iyaṃ punar asmākam āryadhītā ihaiva jātā | ihaiva samvṛddhā | naiva kahiñci gacchati kūpamaṇḍūka iva tiṣṭhati aniḥkramā | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | yāvad bhagavān āha | tena hi varṣāvustāyā bhikṣuṇīya cārikā prakramitavyā | yāvad bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 246. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. <s>Bhikṣuṇīs</s>, having spent the rains in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, came to <s>Vaiśālī</s>. They entered the relatives' house of <s>Bhadrā Kāpileyī</s>. The women [of the house] asked: 'Where did you spend the rains, noble ladies?' They said: 'In <s>Śrāvastī</s>.' They asked: 'What is <s>Śrāvastī</s> like?' They said: 'It is such and such — the parks are delightful; such is <s>Jetavana</s>; such is the Perfumed Chamber (<s>Gandhakuṭī</s>); thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> dwells there; thus the noble <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> [reside there].' [The women said:] 'If going forth is like this, then this is truly going forth! But our noble daughter, born right here, raised right here — she never goes anywhere, sitting like a frog in a well, never venturing out.' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who has completed the rains retreat should set out on a wandering tour.' Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī varṣāvustā cārikāṃ na prakrameya pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: If any <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, having completed the rains retreat, should not depart on a wandering tour, it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | varṣoṣiteti vārṣikāṃ trayo māsān cārikāṃ na prakrameyā ti antamasato grāmāntaraṃ pi vā pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī evaṃ rātraṃ pi prakramati pācattikaṃ | atha dāni jarādurbalā vā vyādhidurbalā vā bhoti na pratibalā gantuṃ kiñcāpi gacchati anāpattiḥ | bhikṣur api varṣāvusto cārikāṃ na prakramati vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Having completed the rains retreat' means having dwelt for the three rainy-season months. 'Should not set out on a wandering tour' means should not proceed — not even to another village — it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to the rule establishment. That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, [if she does not set out] even for one night, incurs a <s>pācattika</s>. However, if she is weak from old age or weak from illness and is unable to travel — even if she does not go, there is no offense. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too who has completed the rains retreat and does not set out on a wandering tour incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s>. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī varṣāvustā cārikāṃ na prakrameya pācattikaṃ || ṇka ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, having completed the rains retreat, does not set out on a wandering tour — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 136
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 136.

body.text: udvaheya
body.translated_text: Driving out (<s>udvaheya</s>).

body.text: 247. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | sthūlanandāya bhikṣuṇīya jetā bhikṣuṇī rājagṛhaṃ gacchamānī nivāritā | ihāryāya varṣā vasitavyā tāya sā kulehi samvarṇitā | āryā jetā bhadrikā guṇavatī anubaddhā tā saṃvṛtā ca | etāya adhikāraṃ karotha sā dāni kulāni upasaṃkramati prāsādikena atikrāntena pratikrāntena avalokitena vyavalokitena sammiñjitaprasāritena saṃghāṭīpātracīvaradhāraṇena anubaddhā anunnaḍā acapalā amukharā aprakīrṇavācā | sā prāsādikā ti prasannā devamanuṣyāḥ | te taṃhi kārāṃ kurvanti | pratyālapanti pratyutthihenti nimantrayanti pātreṇa cīvareṇa glānapratyayabhaiṣajya pariṣkārehi | sthūlanandā bhikṣuṇi anākalpasaṃpannā anīryāpathasampannā omalinamalinehi cīvarehi pāṭitavipāṭitehi vaḍḍaḍiṅgarapuṣṭālaṃbehi stanehi vaḍḍhehi sphicakehi uddhatā unnaḍā capalā mukharā prakīrṇavācā | te tasyā na gauravaṃ kurvanti na nimantrayanti | sā dāni tāṃ udvahati kāyena vācā | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | yāvad bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha nandāṃ sā dāni śabdāpitā tad eva sarvaṃ pṛcchīyatīti yāvad āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha duṣkṛtaṃ te nande yāvat |
body.translated_text: 247. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Jetā</s>, while on her way to <s>Rājagṛha</s>, was stopped by the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Sthūlanandā</s>: 'Noble One, you must spend the rains retreat here.' She was recommended to the lay families [by <s>Sthūlanandā</s>]: 'The noble <s>Jetā</s> is virtuous and accomplished, well-disciplined, restrained, and devoted.' [<s>Sthūlanandā</s> said:] 'Show her your support.' <s>Jetā</s> then visited the families in a pleasing manner — with proper approach and departure, with proper forward glance and sidelong glance, with proper bending and extending [of the arms], with proper wearing of the patchwork robe, bowl, and robes — disciplined, unhaughty, unrestless, not talkative, not scattering her speech. She was pleasing, and gods and humans were delighted. They rendered her service: they rose to greet her, they invited her, they offered her bowls, robes, medicines for illness, and requisites. But the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Sthūlanandā</s> was ill-composed, lacking proper deportment, with soiled and grimy robes, torn and tattered, with large, sagging breasts, with large buttocks — agitated, haughty, restless, talkative, scattering her speech. They did not show her respect, they did not invite her. She then harassed <s>Jetā</s> by body and by speech. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> — up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon <s>Nandā</s>.' She was summoned. All of it was questioned in detail — up to: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>Nandā</s>' — up to:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṇīm evam uktvā ihārye varṣaṃ vasitavyaṃ ity uktvā paścād udvaheya vā udvahāpeya vā pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, having said to a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>: 'Noble One, you must spend the rains retreat here,' and then afterwards should drive [her] out or have [her] driven out — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | bhikṣuṇīm evam vade ihārye varṣāṃ vasitavyam iti trayo māsāṃ uktveti nivārayitvā paścād udvaheya vā ti kāyena vā vācā vā svayaṃ udvahati | udvāhāpeya vā ti pareṇa kāyena vā vācāya pācattikaṃ | yāvat prajñaptiḥ | na kṣamati nivārayitvā paścād udvahituṃ atha bhavati śithilikā vā bāhulikā vā aśikṣākāmā vā kalahakārikā vā paśyati yadīha vaśiṣyati āśrayam utpādayiṣyatīti | kiñcāpi udvahati anāpattiḥ | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī bhikṣuṇīm udvahati pācattikaṃ | śrāmaṇerīm vā śikṣamāṇāṃ vā udvahati vinayātikramaḥ | antamasato gṛhiṇī pi udvahati samvaragāmīvinayātikramam āsādayati |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Should say to a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> thus: "Noble One, you must spend the rains retreat here"' — for the three months. 'Having said' means having stopped [her]. 'Afterwards should drive out' means by body or by speech, [done] by herself. 'Or have [her] driven out' means through another, by body or by speech — it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to the rule establishment. It is not proper, having stopped [a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>], to afterwards drive [her] out. However, if she is lax, or self-indulgent, or unwilling to train, or quarrelsome, and [the preceptress] sees 'if she dwells here she will cause a disturbance' — even if she drives [her] out, there is no offense. That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who drives out a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> — it is a <s>pācattika</s>. If she drives out a <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> or a <s>śikṣamāṇā</s> — it is a <s>vinayātikrama</s>. At the very least, if she even drives out a laywoman, she incurs a <s>saṃvaragāmivinayātikrama</s> (restraint-leading transgression).

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī yevam vaditvā ihārye varṣam vasitavyan ti uktvā paścād udvaheya vā udvahāpeya vā pācattikaṃ || tṛ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, having said: 'Noble One, you must spend the rains retreat here,' and then afterwards should drive [her] out or have [her] driven out — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 137
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 137.

body.text: pūrvopagataṃ
body.translated_text: One who arrived first (<s>pūrvopagata</s>).

body.text: 248. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | atha kālī nāma bhikṣuṇī | sā upagacchati | tā kālaṃ grāmāntaraṃ gatā | sā bhikṣuṇīhi upagatāhi āgatā | tatra ca bhikṣuṇīhi vihāroddeśaḥ śayanāsanoddeśaḥ kṛtaḥ | sā dān āha | ārye mahyaṃ vihāraṃ detha | sā vihāraṃ na labhati | āhaṃsuḥ | kahiṃ āryā varṣopanāyikā kālaṅ gatā | sā kalahaṃ karoti | aparā dāni bhikṣuṇī yogācārā | sā dān āha | ārye ayaṃ mama vihāro | atra mañcakaṃ praveśehi sahitikā vasiṣyāmaḥ | tayā tahiṃ mañcako praveśito | sā kāṣṭhakhaṇḍā ti yatra śākhāni praveśayati | sā dān āha | ārye mā vihāre ovilayaṃ karehi | sā dān āha | bhadrāyaṇi kin tvayā vihāro kṛto kim vikrīto | sāṃghiko vihāro kim arthaṃ na praveśayiṣyam | sā udvahati kāyenāpi vācāye pi | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | yāvat śabdāpayatha kāliṃ sā dāni śabdāpitā | etad eva sarvaṃ pṛcchīyati | yāvad āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha | duṣkṛtaṃ te kāli |
body.translated_text: 248. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. There was a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> named <s>Kālī</s>. She came [to the monastery]. At the [appropriate] time she had gone to another village. When she returned, the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> who had arrived [before her] had already assigned the monastery quarters and sleeping places. She then said: 'Noble ones, give me a dwelling.' She could not obtain a dwelling. They said: 'Where did the Noble One go at the time of the rains-retreat opening?' She made a quarrel. Another <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, a practitioner of yoga, then said: 'Noble One, this is my dwelling. Bring a bed in here; we shall live together.' A bed was brought in there. <s>Kālī</s> then started stacking firewood and inserting branches [to mark territory]. The [yoga-practitioner] said: 'Noble One, do not make a mess in the dwelling!' <s>Kālī</s> said: 'Good woman, did you build this dwelling? Did you buy it? It is a <s>Saṃgha</s> dwelling — why should I not bring things in?' She harassed [her] by body and by speech. The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> — up to: 'Summon <s>Kālī</s>.' She was summoned. All of it was questioned in detail — up to: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>Kālī</s>.'

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī jānantī bhikṣuṇīṃ pūrvopagatāṃ paścād āgatvā udvaheya vā udvahāpeya vā kāyena vā vācāya vā pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, knowing that a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> arrived first, should come afterwards and drive [her] out or have [her] driven out, by body or by speech — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | jānantīti svayaṃ vā jāneya parato vā śruṇeya | bhikṣuṇīm pūrvopagatām iti purimikāyāṃ varṣopanāyikāyāṃ | paścād āgatveti paścimikāyāṃ | udvaheya vā ti svayaṃ | udvahāpeya | vā ti pareṇa kāyeṇa vā vācā vā pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇīm udvahati pācattikaṃ | śrāmaṇerīm vā śikṣamāṇām vā udvahati deśanāgāmivinayātikramam āsādayati | antamasato gṛhiṇīṃ pi udvahati samvaragāmivinayātikramaḥ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Knowing' means she knows herself or has heard from another. 'A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who arrived first' means during the earlier rains-retreat opening. 'Coming afterwards' means at the later [opening]. 'Should drive out' means by herself. 'Or have driven out' means through another, by body or by speech — it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to the rule establishment. That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who drives out a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> — it is a <s>pācattika</s>. If she drives out a <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> or a <s>śikṣamāṇā</s>, she incurs a <s>deśanāgāmivinayātikrama</s> (confession-leading transgression). At the very least, if she even drives out a laywoman, it is a <s>saṃvaragāmivinayātikrama</s>. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī jānantī bhikṣuṇīṃ pūrvopagatāṃ paścād āgatvā udvaheya vā udvahāpeya vā kāyena vā vācā vā pācattikaṃ || phu ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, knowing that a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> arrived first, should come afterwards and drive [her] out or have [her] driven out, by body or by speech — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 138
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rule 138.

body.text: vighasaṃ
body.translated_text: Refuse (<s>vighasa</s>).

body.text: 249. bhagavān kāśiṣu viharati | aparāya dāni bhikṣuṇīya uccāramallakaṃ apratyavekṣitvā rathyāyāṃ choritaṃ | tahiṃ dāni aparo brāhmaṇo śīrṣasnāto āhatavastranivastro tāya rathyāya atikramati | uccāramallakaṃ tasya śīrṣe patitaṃ | tasya śīrṣaṃ vastrāṇi ca vināśitāni | janena copahāsitaṃ brāhmaṇa susnātaḥ suviliptas tvam iti | so dāni tām ākrośati | āha | itikitikāya dhīte śramaṇike na paśyasi mama śīrṣaṃ vastrāṇi ca viṣṭhena vināśitāni | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | pe | yāvad āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha | duskṛtan te evan nāma tvam apratyavekṣiya choresi | tena hi na kṣamati apratyavekṣiya chorayituṃ | atha khalu bhagavān yāvat paryavadātāni bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: 249. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Kāśi</s> country. A certain <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> threw a chamber-pot out onto the street without looking. There, another <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — freshly bathed, wearing new clothes — was passing along that street. The chamber-pot fell on his head. His head and clothes were soiled. People mocked him: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, how well-bathed and well-anointed you are!' He then abused her: 'Daughter of a wretch! Renunciant woman! Do you not see that my head and clothes have been ruined by excrement?' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> — abbreviated — up to: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong! How can you throw [things] out without looking? Therefore it is not proper to throw [things] out without looking.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> — up to: 'so that [the rules] will be made clear.'

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī tirokuḍyaṃ uccāram vā prāsrāvam vā kheṭakam vā siṃghāṇakam vā vighasam vā saṃkāram vā apratyavekṣitvā chorayet pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should throw over a wall — excrement, or urine, or phlegm, or nasal mucus, or refuse, or sweepings — without looking — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | tirokuḍyan ti tiraḥprakāram uccāram vā prasrāvam vā kheṭam vā siṃghāṇakam vā vighasam vā saṃkāram vā vastradhovanam vā bhāṇḍadhovanam vā keśān vā nakhān vā | apratyavekṣitveti anirīkṣya | choreyā ti ujjheya | pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | yadi kiñcit ujjhitukāmo bhavati pratyavekṣitavyaṃ | yadi tāvad ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā rathyā bhavanti ārāmayitavyaṃ | atha dāni anākīrṇā bhavanti kiñcāpi chorayaty anāpattiḥ | taṃ pi dāni na kṣamati aśabdakarṇikāye chorayituṃ api tu acchaṭikā dātavyā ukkāsitavyam vā | sā eṣā bhikṣuṇī naiva pratyavekṣati nāpi acchaṭikāṃ dattvā chorayati pācattikam āsādayati | bhikṣur api apratyavekṣya acchaṭikām akṛtvā chorayati vinayātikramam āsādayati | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is fully ordained. 'Over a wall' means over a partition. 'Excrement, or urine, or phlegm, or nasal mucus, or refuse, or sweepings' — or cloth-washings, or vessel-washings, or hair, or nails. 'Without looking' means without inspecting. 'Should throw' means should discard — it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to the rule establishment. If one wishes to discard anything, one should first look. If the street is crowded with many people, one should wait. If it is uncrowded — even if one throws, there is no offense. But even then, it is not proper to throw without making a sound. Rather, one should snap the fingers or clear the throat. That <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who neither looks nor snaps her fingers before throwing incurs a <s>pācattika</s>. A <s>bhikṣu</s> too who throws without looking and without snapping his fingers incurs a <s>vinayātikrama</s>. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī tirokuḍyaṃ uccāram vā prasrāvam vā kheṭaṃ vā siṃghāṇakam vā vighasam vā saṃkāram vā apratyavekṣya choreya pācattikaṃ || grā ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should throw over a wall — excrement, or urine, or phlegm, or nasal mucus, or refuse, or sweepings — without looking — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 139, 140
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> rules 139, 140.

body.text: harita tṛṇe
body.translated_text: On green grass.

body.text:
udaka
250. bhagavān śrāvastīyaṃ viharati | rājño dāni prasenajitasya kośalasya pūrvakoṣṭhakaṃ nāma udyānam puṣkiriṇīsampannaṃ | anāvṛtaṃ bhikṣūnāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāṃ āvṛtaṃ itarāye janatāye | rājā dāni ārāmikasyāha | ho bhaṇe ārāmika pūrvakoṣṭhakam udyānaṃ siktasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ karehi | śvo haṃ sāntaḥpuro niryāsyaṃ | taṃ dāni ṣaḍvargiṇīhi śrutaṃ | śvo rājā sāntaḥpuro udyānabhūmin niryāsyatīti | tāyo dāni pratikṛty eva gatvā tahiṃ haritaśādvalopastarāṇāyāṃ pakvakheṭena ca pakvasiṃghāṇakena ca vināśayitvā padumapatrehi uccārasya puṭakāni bandhitvā puṣkiriṇīyaṃ pravāhayeṃsuḥ | tāyo dāni divasaṃ tahiṃ kākāvāhāṃ bhañjiya sāyāhnasamaye nagaraṃ praviṣṭāḥ rājā dāni prasenajita kośalo aparejjukāto niragato sāntaḥpuro | tāyo dāni antaḥpurikāyo kathañcid eva samrodhād avamuktā randhanamokṣam iva manyamānāḥ cañcūryante | kāścin niṣaṇṇāḥ kāścin nipannāḥ | kāścid ito ca ito ca dhāvanti avakāśaṃ gṛhṇanti śādvalopastaraṇe paribhrāmanti | tāsāṃ dāni pakvakheṭena pakvasiṃghāṇakena vastrāṇi vināśitāni | puṣkiriṇīṃ otīrṇāḥ snānāya | tāyo paśyanti puṭakān plavamānān | tāsāṃ bhavati kulaputrakehi śrutaṃ śvo rājā sāntaḥpuro udyānaṃ pravekṣyatīti tehi ete gandhapuṭakāḥ pravāhitā iti kṛtvā tāyo gṛhṇanti | te udakena klinnā uccāreṇa cā khāditāḥ prakṛtisukumāraṃ ca padmapatraṃ | gṛhītamātram eva vilīnaṃ | hī hī viṣṭhaṃ tā dāni rājño upasaṃkrāntā āhaṃsu | mahārāja eṣa tāvad īdṛśī avasthā rājā āha śabdāpayatha ārāmikaṃ | so dāni śabdāpito | rājā āha | ho bhaṇe ārāmika kena udyānaṃ viṭṭālitaṃ | āha ṣaḍvargiṇīyo śramaṇīyo eva divasaṃ kākavāhā bhañjitvā gatāḥ | rājā hasitvā āha | tāsām avinītānāṃ karma bhaviṣyati | etaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣuṇīyo mahāprajāpatīye gautamīye ārocayeṃsuḥ | mahāprajāpatī pi gautamī bhagavato ārocayet | yāvad
body.translated_text: In water. 250. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> had a garden called <s>Pūrvakoṣṭhaka</s>, furnished with lotus ponds. It was open to <s>bhikṣus</s> and <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> but closed to other people. The king told the garden-keeper: 'Ho there, garden-keeper! Make the <s>Pūrvakoṣṭhaka</s> garden watered and swept. Tomorrow I shall go out with the inner court.' The group-of-six <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (<s>ṣaḍvargiṇīs</s>) heard this: 'Tomorrow the king will go out to the park-grounds with the inner court.' They then went there beforehand and ruined the green, grassy lawn with ripened phlegm and ripened nasal mucus; they wrapped excrement in lotus leaves, made parcels, and set them floating in the lotus pond. They spent the day there playing games, and in the late afternoon entered the city. The next day, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> went out with the inner court. Those women of the inner court, like [creatures] released from long confinement and thinking it a holiday, frolicked about. Some sat down, some lay down, some ran here and there, claimed spaces, and strolled about on the grassy lawns. Their clothes were ruined by the ripened phlegm and nasal mucus. They descended into the lotus pond to bathe. They saw the parcels floating. They thought: 'Young men, having heard that tomorrow the king would enter the garden with the inner court, have sent these perfume-parcels floating!' They grabbed them. But these, soaked with water and eaten away by excrement — and the naturally delicate lotus-leaf — disintegrated the moment they were grasped. 'Ugh, ugh! Excrement!' They then went to the king and said: 'Great king, such is the state of affairs!' The king said: 'Summon the garden-keeper.' He was summoned. The king said: 'Ho there, garden-keeper! By whom was the garden defiled?' He said: 'The group-of-six renunciant women spent the day playing games and then left.' The king laughed and said: 'That will be the consequence of their lack of discipline.' The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reported this matter to <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> also reported it to the <s>Bhagavān</s> — up to:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī harite tṛṇe uccāram vā prasrāvam vā kheṭam vā siṃghāṇakam vā kuryāt pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should deposit excrement, or urine, or phlegm, or nasal mucus on green grass — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī udake uccāram vā prasrāvam vā kheṭam vā siṃghāṇakam vā kuryāt pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should deposit excrement, or urine, or phlegm, or nasal mucus in water — it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | uccāran ti gūthaṃ | prasrāvan ti mūtraṃ | kheṭam iti śleṣmā | siṃghāṇakan ti pakvasiṃghāṇakaṃ | harite tṛṇe iti śādvale acchinnālūnasmiṃ udan ti udakāni nāma daśa | nādikaṃ tāḍāgaṃ audupānikaṃ śvabhrodakaṃ praghārimaṃ vṛṣṭisthitaṃ ucchodakaṃ antarīkṣapānīyaṃ himavilīnaṃ sāmudram vā uccāram vā prasrāvaṃ vā kuryāt pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | atha dāni prāvṛṣeṇyā se sarvabhumiḥ śādvalopastareṇā bhavati yahiṃ pradeśe svalpaharitam bhavati tahiṃ kartavyaṃ | atha dāni alpaharitaṃ na bhavati kaṭāhake vā iṣṭakāyam vā upale vā śuṣkatṛṇe vā kāṣṭhakhaṇḍe vā yatra vā anyena uccāro kṛto bhavati balīvardena vā | yatra vā anyena manuṣyena kṛto tahiṃ kartavyaṃ atha dāni evaṃ na bhavati antamasato kanīyasiṃ pi aṅguliṃ upadrāhayitvā kartavyaṃ | tathā kartavyaṃ yathā tahim prathamam nipatati | atha dāni caṅkramati na kṣamati haritaśādvale śleṣmaṃ chorayituṃ | atha khu kaṭe vā patrapuṭikāyāṃ vā chorayitavyaṃ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is ordained. 'Feces' means excrement. 'Urine' means urine. 'Phlegm' means mucus. 'Nasal discharge' means matured nasal mucus. 'On green grass' means on a lawn that is uncut and unplucked. 'Water' means: waters are of ten kinds—river water, pond water, well water, pool water, drainage water, rainwater standing, spring water, atmospheric water, snow-melt water, or sea water. If she defecates or urinates [on green grass or in water]—it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to: it is a regulation. Now in the rainy season, when the entire ground is covered with green grass, one should use a spot where there is little green growth. If there is no spot with little green, [one should use] a basin, a brick, a stone, dry grass, a piece of wood, or wherever another [being] such as a bull has already defecated, or wherever another human has done so—there one should do it. If even that is not possible, at the very least one should lift the smallest finger and do it. One should do it in such a way that [the waste] falls there first. Now when walking in meditation, it is not permissible to spit phlegm on green grass. Rather, one should spit onto a mat or into a leaf-cup. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī harite tṛṇe uccāram vā prasrāvam vā kheṭam vā siṃghāṇakam vā kuryāt pācattikaṃ |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> defecates, urinates, spits phlegm, or blows nasal discharge on green grass—it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī udake uccāram vā prasrāvam vā kheṭam vā siṃghāṇakam vā kuryāt pācattikaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> defecates, urinates, spits phlegm, or blows nasal discharge in water—it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: pācattikadharma 141
body.translated_text: <s>Pācattika</s> (Expiation) rule 141.

body.text: gaṇalābha
body.translated_text: Communal gain (<s>gaṇalābha</s>).

body.text: 251. bhagavān śrāvastīyam viharati | tāyo dāni ṣaḍvargiṇīyo chandakaṃ aṇvanti | āhaṃsuḥ | prajāpati detha cchandakaṃ āryamiśrikāṇāṃ bhaktaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ | tā dāni striyo prayacchanti | tā dān āhaṃsuḥ āryā yaṃ divasaṃ saṃghabhaktaṃ kariṣyatha tadāsmākam api ārocayetha | vayam api pariveṣakā āgamiṣyāmo ti | tāhi dāni nimantritāḥ | āyuṣmanto śāriputramaudgalyāyanau aniruddho revataḥ kapphiṇo śroṇakoṭīviṃśa upavāno āyuṣmān rāhulo ṣaḍvargikāś ca | tāhi dāni dveāsanaprajñaptī kṛtā | ekā sthavirāṇāṃ aparā ṣaḍvargikāṇāṃ | tahiṃ dāni bhikṣū kālasyaiva nivāsayitvā prāvaritvā ca praviṣṭāḥ | tato āyuṣmato śāriputrasya dātuṃ śālināmodanaṃ mudgānāṃ sūpo ghṛtaṃ dadhi ca | āyuṣmato maudgalyāyanasya yavakodano māṣasūpo tailaṃ ca | apareṣām ṣaṣṭikodano sūpo ca | apareṣāṃ kodravodano | apareṣāṃ vyañjanāni dinnāni odano na dīyate | apareṣāṃ śākaṃ dinnaṃ odano na dīyate | apareṣāṃ vāṭikodano vyañjanaṃ na dīyate | āyuṣmato rāhulasya pi śyākaśākaṃ
body.translated_text: 251. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Those group-of-six <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> went soliciting contributions. They said: 'Good people, give contributions! We shall prepare a meal for the noble ones.' Those women contributed. They said: 'Noble ones, on whatever day you prepare the <s>Saṃgha</s> meal, tell us, and we too shall come to serve.' They then invited the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Revata</s>, <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, <s>Upavāna</s>, the Venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, and the group-of-six [monks]. They prepared two seating arrangements: one for the elders and another for the group-of-six. The <s>bhikṣus</s> arrived early in the morning, having dressed and put on their outer robes. Then to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> was given rice-pudding with bean soup, ghee, and curd. To the Venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, barley-rice with black-bean soup and oil. To others, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>-rice with soup. To others, <s>kodrava</s>-rice. To some, side-dishes were given but no rice. To some, vegetables were given but no rice. To some, <s>vāṭika</s>-rice was given but no side-dishes. And to the Venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, [only] <s>śyāka</s>-greens.

body.text: tā dāni striyo bhakṣyabhojyam ādāya gatāḥ pṛcchanti | kahin te āryamiśrikāḥ | tāyo dāni sthavirān bhikṣūn āvaritvā ṣaḍvargikān darśenti | tatas teṣān dīyate śālinā modanaṃ mudgānāṃ sūpo ghṛtaṃ | navanītaṃ ambu madhurāṇi gauḍan dadhi śvetaṃ dadhi kṣīraṃ samitāsamitaṃ yasyārthaṃ yāv arthaṃ dīyati | yat kiñcit praṇītasammataṃ bhakṣyabhojyaṃ peyaṃ coṣmaṃ taṃ ṣaḍvargikāṇān dāpayanti | ime te āryamiśrikāḥ bhikṣū pi bhuktavibhuktakāḥ utthāyotthāya bhagavataḥ pādavandā upasaṃkrāntā | bhagavān jānanto yeva pṛcchati | api tu śāriputra śobhane māsi mṛṣṭam vā praṇītam vā prabhūtam vā | sthaviro āha | kṛtaṃ bhagavan āhāreṇāhārakṛtyaṃ | dvitīyam pi tṛtīyam pi | bhagavān āha | thero āha | labdho bhagavan śālināmodanaṃ mudgānāṃ sūpo navanītaṃ ambu madhurāṇi vyañjanani gauḍan dadhi kṣīraṃ yasyārthaṃ yāvad arthaṃ dīyati yathāpīdaṃ bhaginīnāṃ śraddhāprasannānāṃ parigrahe | bhagavān āha | ke tahiṃ saṃghasthaviro bhūta | āyuṣmāṃ cchāriputro | bhagavān āha | satyaṃ śāriputra āha | āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha | durbhuktaṃ te śāriputra evaṃ ca nāma tvaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viheṭhayantaṃ adhyupekṣasi | yasya bhagavān durbhuktam ity āha tasya taṃ kalpam vā kalpāvaśeṣam vā tiṣṭheya naiva jarā gaccheya | sthavireṇa kākapoṭaṃ dattvā sarva daradarāya vāntaṃ | bhagavān āha | śabdāpayatha bhikṣuṇīyo tāyo śabdāpitāḥ | etad eva pṛcchīyanti | āhaṃsuḥ | āma bhagavan | bhagavān āha duṣkṛtaṃ vo bhikṣuṇīyo evam ca nāma yūyaṃ jānantīyo gaṇalābhaṃ gaṇasya pariṇāmayatha | tena hi na kṣamati | atha khalu bhagavān yāvat paryavadātāni bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: Then those women, bringing edibles and food, came and asked: 'Where are the noble ones?' They screened off the elder <s>bhikṣus</s> and showed [only] the group-of-six. To those [group-of-six] were given rice-pudding, bean soup, ghee, fresh butter, water, sweets, molasses, curd, white curd, milk, clarified and unclarified [butter]—for whatever purpose, in whatever amount, whatever was considered fine edibles, food, drink, and warm [beverages], they had it given to the group-of-six. 'These are the noble <s>bhikṣus</s>.' The <s>bhikṣus</s>, having eaten or not eaten, rose and went to pay respects to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, though knowing, asked: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, did you have a fine month? Was the food abundant, refined, and plentiful?' The elder said: 'The food has served its purpose, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' A second and third time. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: [The elder replied:] 'We received rice-pudding, bean soup, fresh butter, water, sweets, side-dishes, molasses, curd, milk—for whatever purpose, in whatever amount—as befits the devotion of sisters faithful and devout.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Who was the <s>Saṃgha</s> elder there?' 'The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is this true, <s>Śāriputra</s>?' He said: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have eaten badly, <s>Śāriputra</s>! How could you look on while the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> was being mistreated?' For one to whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> says 'you have eaten badly'—that would endure for an eon or the remainder of an eon; he would not even grow old. The elder, having administered an emetic, vomited everything thoroughly. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>.' They were summoned and questioned about this very matter. They said: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have done wrong, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. How could you, knowing it to be a communal gain, divert it for [your own] group?' Therefore it is not permissible. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>... up to: so that they may become utterly purified.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī jānantī gaṇalābhaṃ gaṇasya pariṇataṃ gaṇasya pariṇāmayet pācattikam |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, knowing it to be a communal gain that has been prepared for the community, diverts it for [her own] group—it is a <s>pācattika</s>.

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | jānantīti svayam vā jāneya parato vā śruṇeya | gaṇalābham iti bhikṣugaṇasya bhikṣuṇīgaṇasya | lābham iti aṣṭa lābhāḥ yāvat kāliko yāmayāmiko yāvat kalpikākalpiko pariṇatan ti pariniṣpannaṃ | gaṇasya pariṇāmayet pācattikaṃ yāvat prajñaptiḥ | eṣa dāni kocid āgacchati deyadharmaṃ dātukāmo | āha | ārye icchāmi parigṛhyamāṇan ti parigṛhṇītavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is ordained. 'Knowing' means either knowing by herself or hearing from others. 'Communal gain' means the gain of the <s>bhikṣu</s>-community or the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>-community. 'Gain' means the eight kinds of gains, up to: timely, watch-by-watch, up to: proper and improper. 'Prepared' means fully prepared. 'Diverts it for the group'—it is a <s>pācattika</s>, up to: it is a regulation. Now if someone comes wishing to give a gift: if he says 'Noble one, I wish it to be received,' it should be received.

body.text: prātideśanikā dharmā 18
body.translated_text: <s>Prātideśanika</s> (Confession) rules: 18.

body.text: sarpis tailaṃ etc
body.translated_text: Ghee, oil, etc.

body.text: 252. ti | te dāni bhikṣū ṣaḍvargikāḥ sarpikehi sarpi tailakehi tailaṃ gauḍakehi guḍaṃ mādhukehi madhuṃ mātsikehi matsyaṃ māṃsikehi māṃsaṃ dugdhikehi dugdhaṃ dodhikehi dadhiṃ vijñapiya khādanti | jano dāni ojjhāyati | paśyatha bhaṇe śramaṇo gautamo 'nekaparyāyeṇālpecchatāya varṇavādī yāvac chikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ | tasmād iha gautami bhikṣuṇībhir avi atraiva śikṣitavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: 252. Now those group-of-six <s>bhikṣus</s>, from ghee-dealers they would request ghee, from oil-dealers oil, from molasses-dealers molasses, from honey-dealers honey, from fish-dealers fish, from meat-dealers meat, from milk-dealers milk, from curd-dealers curd—having specially requested, they would eat. People were displeased: 'Look, friends, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> praises fewness of desires in many ways,' up to: the training rule was laid down. Therefore, <s>Gautamī</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> too should train in this very matter.

body.text: eṣaivārthotpattiḥ | ekam idam gautami samayaṃ tathāgato śākyeṣu viharati | yāvad bhagavān mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm āmantrayati | sannipātaya gautami bhikṣuṇīyo yāvat paryavadātāni bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: This is the same origin-story. At one time, <s>Gautamī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> was dwelling among the <s>Śākyas</s>. Up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>: 'Assemble the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>Gautamī</s>... up to: so that they may become utterly purified.'

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇī ātmārthāya agilānā kulehi sarpiṃ vijñāpetvā vā vijñāpāyetvā vā khādeya vā bhuñjeya vā pratideśayitavyaṃ tāya bhikṣuṇīya asaṃpreyam me āryamiśrikā prātideśanikaṃ dharmam āpannā tan dharmaṃ pratideśayāmi | ayan dharmo prātideśaniko |
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, for her own sake, not being ill, having specially requested ghee from families or having had it requested, eats or consumes it—she should confess: 'Noble ones, I have fallen into a <s>prātideśanika</s> offense, which is unseemly. I confess that offense.' This is a <s>prātideśanika</s> rule.

body.text: evam sarpis [1] | tailaṃ [2] | madhu [3] | phāṇitaṃ [4] | dugdhaṃ [5] | dadhi [6] | matsyaṃ [7] | māṃsaṃ [8] |
body.translated_text: Likewise for: ghee [1], oil [2], honey [3], molasses [4], milk [5], curd [6], fish [7], meat [8].

body.text: yā puna bhikṣuṇīti upasampannā | ātmārthāyeti ātmānaṃ sandhāya ātmānam upanidhyāya | agilānā ti pratyuddhṛtaṃ bhagavatā padaṃ anāpatti gilānāya | kin tāvad atra gailānyam abhipretam | jarādurbalā vā vyādhidurbalā tā virecanapītā vā śirāviddhā vā śleṣmā vā sannipātā vā | kulehīti kṣatriyakulāni vā brāhmaṇakulāni vā yāni vā punar anyāny api kānicit kulāni | sarpīti sarpin nāma gāviya māhiṣīye ajāye eḍakāya uṣṭrīya | vijñapetvā ti svayaṃ vijñāpetvā | vijñapāyetvā ti pareṇa vijñapāyetvā | khādeyā tī yaṃ khādanīyaṃ | bhojanīyan ti yaṃ bhojanīyaṃ | pratideśayitavyaṃ tāya bhikṣuṇīya yāvad ayam dharmo prātideśaniko |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' means one who is ordained. 'For her own sake' means with reference to herself, for her own benefit. 'Not being ill' means the <s>Bhagavān</s> has exempted this—no offense for one who is ill. What then is the illness intended here? Weak from old age, or weak from disease, or having drunk a purgative, or having been bled, or [suffering from] phlegm or a combined disorder. 'From families' means from <s>kṣatriya</s> families, brahmin families, or whatever other families there may be. 'Ghee' (<s>sarpi</s>) means ghee from a cow, a buffalo, a goat, a sheep, or a camel. 'Having requested' means having requested by herself. 'Having had it requested' means having had another request [on her behalf]. 'Eats' means what is to be chewed. 'Consumes' means what is to be eaten. 'Should confess'—she, that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, up to: this is a <s>prātideśanika</s> rule.

body.text: atha dāni pittasaṃkṣobho bhavati labhyā sarpi vijñāpetuṃ peyālaṃ | atha dāni piṇḍapātam aṇvanti paśyati ghṛtaṃ vikrāyantaṃ na dāni vaktavyaṃ | "dirghāyuḥ lābho labhyatu bahuñ ca bhavatu |" labdho ca sthāvaro bhavatu | atha dān āha | kenārtho āryāye | vaktavyaṃ piṇḍacāraṃ aṇvāmi | atha dān āha | artho āryāya sarpiṇā yady arthikā bhoti | vaktavyam artho | yadi pūraṃ pi pātraṃ labhati anāpattiḥ | atha dāni aparā pi kācid bhavati labhyā pratyutpannaprāyeṇa (!) vaktuṃ imāye pi dehīti |
body.translated_text: Now if there is a bile-disorder, it is permissible to request ghee. Abbreviated. Now when going on alms-round, if she sees ghee being sold, she should not say: 'May you live long! May you gain much profit, and may what is gained be stable!' If [the seller] then asks: 'What does the noble one need?' She should say: 'I am on my alms-round.' If he then says: 'Does the noble one need ghee? If you need it—' she should say: 'I need it.' Even if she receives a full bowl—there is no offense. Now if there is another [nun too], it is permissible to say in the ordinary course: 'Give to her also.'

body.text: evaṃ tailaṃ | yadi vātavikāro bhavati labhyā tailaṃ vijñapayituṃ taṃ pi dāni na tailapīḍakānāṃ tena vijñapayitavyaṃ | atha dāni piṇḍacāram aṇvanti paśyati tailaṃ māpiyantaṃ yāvat pūraṃ pi pātraṃ labhati anāpattiḥ | yāvat labhyā pratyutpannaprayogeṇa vaktuṃ imāye pi dehīti |
body.translated_text: Likewise for oil. If there is a wind-disorder, it is permissible to request oil. But it is not permissible to request from oil-pressers by that [specific request]. Now when going on alms-round, if she sees oil being pressed—up to: even if she receives a full bowl—there is no offense. Up to: it is permissible to say in the ordinary course: 'Give to her also.'

body.text: evaṃ madhu | yadi śleṣmavikāro bhavati labhyaṃ madhu vijñapayituṃ | taṃ pi dāni nā kṣamati madhughātakānāṃ tena vijñapayituṃ |
body.translated_text: Likewise for honey. If there is a phlegm-disorder, it is permissible to request honey. But it is not permissible to request from honey-gatherers by that [specific request].

body.text: evaṃ phāṇitaṃ | yadi gilānā bhavati vaidyo āha ārye guḍaprayogaṃ karohīti labhyaṃ guḍaṃ vijñapayituṃ |
body.translated_text: Likewise for molasses. If she is ill and the physician says: 'Noble one, use a molasses preparation,' it is permissible to request molasses.

body.text: evam dugdhaṃ | labhyaṃ dugdhaṃ piyayituṃ | atha dāni piṇḍacāram aṇvati paśyati yo kulehi gāvo duhyantāṃ na dāni vaktavyaṃ | bahulābho labhyatu kṣemeṇa gāvo carantu | āhaṃsuḥ | kena āryāye artho | vaktavyaṃ | piṇḍacāram aṇvāmi | āhaṃsuḥ | artho āryāye dugdhenāpūram pi pātraṃ pratīcchaty anāpattiḥ yāvat pratyutpannaprayogena labhyā vaktuṃ imāya pi dehīti | atha dāni śvetamayaṃ sikṣati | nāsti śvetamayaṃ | icchasi dugdhaṃ | āha | icchāmi | pūram pi pātraṃ labhati anāpattiḥ |
body.translated_text: Likewise for milk. It is permissible to drink milk. Now when going on alms-round, if she sees cows being milked at the houses, she should not say: 'May you have abundant gain! May the cows graze safely!' They ask: 'What does the noble one need?' She should say: 'I am on my alms-round.' They say: 'Does the noble one need milk?' Even if she receives a full bowl—there is no offense. Up to: it is permissible to say in the ordinary course: 'Give to her also.' Now if she is looking for buttermilk: 'There is no buttermilk. Do you want milk?' She says: 'I do.' Even if she receives a full bowl—there is no offense.

body.text: atha dāni pratiśyāyo bhavati | vaidyo āha dadhikṛtyaṃ karohīti labhyaṃ dadhi vijñapayituṃ | atha dāni piṇḍacāram aṇvati paśyati dadhi māpīyamānaṃ labhyā mastu vijñapayituṃ | atha dān āha | nāsti mastu icchasi dadhiṃ | āha icchāmi | pūraṃ pi pātraṃ pratigṛhṇāti anāpattiḥ |
body.translated_text: Now if there is a cold, and the physician says: 'Make a curd preparation,' it is permissible to request curd. Now when going on alms-round, if she sees curd being prepared, it is permissible to request whey. If he then says: 'There is no whey. Do you want curd?' She says: 'I do.' Even if she receives a full bowl—there is no offense.

body.text: atha dāni bhikṣuṇī vamanaṃ virecanaṃ vā kartukāmā bhavati vaidyo jalpati ārye abhiṣyandehi matsyarasehīti | yāvan na kṣamati kaivartānāṃ vijñapayituṃ | atha dāni piṇḍacāram aṇvati labhyaṃ āmbūkāñjikaṃ vijñapayituṃ |
body.translated_text: Now if a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> wishes to do an emetic or purgative, and the physician says: 'Noble one, flush [your system] with fish broth'—it is not permissible to request from fishermen by that [specific request]. Now when going on alms-round, it is permissible to request <s>āmbūkāñjika</s> (sour fish preparation).

body.text: atha dāni sirāviddhikā bhavati | virecanapītikā bhavati | vaidyo āha | ārye māṃsarasaṃ pratisevāhi | labhyaṃ māṃsarasaṃ vijñapayituṃ | na kṣamati orobhrikānāṃ tena | atha dāni piṇḍacāram aṇvati labhyaṃ śākarasaṃ vijñapayituṃ | atha dān āha | nāsti ārye śākaraso icchasi māṃsarasaṃ | āha | icchāmi | pūraṃ pi pātraṃ labhati anāpattiḥ |
body.translated_text: Now if she has been bled or has drunk a purgative, and the physician says: 'Noble one, take meat broth,' it is permissible to request meat broth. It is not permissible to request from butchers by that [specific request]. Now when going on alms-round, it is permissible to request vegetable broth. If he then says: 'There is no vegetable broth, noble one. Do you want meat broth?' She says: 'I do.' Even if she receives a full bowl—there is no offense.

body.text: atha dāni jānāti amukasmiṃ kāle kadācid gailānyaṃ bhaviṣyati imāni bhaiṣajyāni durlabhāni bhaviṣyantīti pratikṛty eva yācati anāpattiḥ | glānā vijñapiya agilānā khādati vinayātikramaḥ | agilānā vijñapiya glānā khādati anāpattiḥ | aglānā vijñāpiya aglānā khādati pratideśayitavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Now, if she knows that at some time in the future there will be illness and these medicines will be hard to obtain, she may request in advance—there is no offense. If she requests [medicine] when ill but eats it when not ill—it is a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression. If she requests when not ill but eats when ill—there is no offense. If she requests when not ill and eats when not ill—it must be confessed.

body.text: asaṃpreyaṃ siddhaṃ saṃpreyaṃ khādati anāpattiḥ | saṃpreyaṃ siddhaṃ | asaṃpreyaṃ siddhaṃ | asaṃpreyaṃ khādati vinayātikramaḥ | saṃpreyaṃ siddhaṃ saṃpreyaṃ khādati anāpattiḥ | parapratibaddhāya jīvikāya anāpattiḥ | tena bhagavān āha |
body.translated_text: If food prepared without being requested is eaten with what was requested—there is no offense. If food prepared with what was requested is [mixed with] food prepared without being requested and eaten—it is a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression. If food prepared with what was requested is eaten with what was requested—there is no offense. For one whose livelihood depends on others—there is no offense. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: yāni kho punar imāni praṇītasammatāni bhojanāni bhavanti sayyath' īdaṃ sarpiḥ evaṃrūpaṃ taṃ bhikṣuṇī agilānā kulehi vijñapetvā vā vijñāpāyetvā vā khādeya vā bhuñjeya vā pratideśayitavyaṃ tāya bhikṣuṇīya | asaṃpreyam me ārye gārhyaṃ prātideśanikaṃ dharmam āpannā taṃ dharmaṃ pratideśayāmi | ayaṃ dharmo prātideśaniko |
body.translated_text: Now, these foods are reckoned as exquisite, namely: ghee and such foods. If a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, not being ill, having requested or having had [someone] request from families, eats or consumes [these]—it must be confessed by that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>: 'Noble one, I have incurred a blameworthy <s>prātideśanika</s> offense through food not [properly] obtained. I confess that offense.' This is a <s>prātideśanika</s> rule.

body.text: evaṃ tailena kartavyaṃ | madhuphāṇitaṃ dugdhaṃ dadhi matsyaṃ māṃsaṃ |
body.translated_text: The same procedure applies with oil, honey, molasses, milk, yogurt, fish, and meat.
